body:
## Summary

- adds the Wave 2 conformance suites against the dated, amended block contracts
- runs store conformance on both PGlite and PostgreSQL in PR CI
- adds provider wire-format replay coverage, key-gated live legs, and a nightly live workflow
- adds semantic MCP shim coverage, corpus local-pack closure, canonical memory-store fixtures, and bidirectional UI wire parity gates

Linear: ENG-235

## Clause-to-test mapping

| Contract clause | Coverage added |
| --- | --- |
| `01-core` §7 | positive `door-auth` audit-kind leg in `packages/core/src/contract-coverage.e2e.test.ts` |
| amended `01-core` export surface and §12 | root utility and `/conformance` inventory coverage, plus canonical `memoryStoreAdapter` tests |
| amended `01-core` MCP grant source | `source: "mcp"` grant conformance leg |
| `02-store` §2 | explicit current-door audit mutation characterization, named for the Wave 3 append-only flip |
| amended `02-store` §3 | contract-to-code reserved collection drift test and canonical memory adapter reserved validation/projection semantics |
| amended `02-store` additive app ref | canonical memory adapter derives and filters `vendo_apps.trigger_kind` exactly like current main's ENG-254 routed store |
| `02-store` §4 / `01-core` §12 | the store conformance kit runs on PGlite and PostgreSQL; CI fails if its PostgreSQL leg is accidentally absent |
| `03-agent` §3(4) | visible skip for the catalog/theme assembly deferred to Wave 5 |
| `03-agent` §§2–4 | the complete approval pause/resume, blocked-outcome, and view-part journey on `MockLanguageModelV3` and recorded OpenAI-compatible HTTP/SSE |
| `03-agent`, `06-apps`, `07-automations` wire shapes | tsc-backed two-way assignability between owner types and `ui/src/wire-types.ts`, including a negative control |
| umbrella/corpus package closure | transitive `@vendoai/*` workspace dependencies reachable from the umbrella must all be present in the corpus pack list |

## CI added

- the main PR test job now provisions PostgreSQL 16 and exports `POSTGRES_URL`
- a `conformance` job runs the three package conformance suites on PostgreSQL and exercises the generated MCP shim in Chromium
- `turbo.json` explicitly passes and hashes `CI` / `POSTGRES_URL`, so the PostgreSQL legs cannot be hidden by Turbo strict env or a PGlite cache entry
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs the key-gated agent provider journey and existing live-agentic, E2B, egress, judge, and Claude legs, uploads logs, and fails after collecting every leg
- live provider gates use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and paired `VENDO_TEST_PROXY_URL` + `VENDO_TEST_PROXY_KEY`; missing keys remain explicit skips

## Shim gate

The generated shim was regenerated twice on macOS after building the jail runtime and produced the same SHA each time, but the first PR run exposed platform-specific Linux bundle bytes (928,417 vs. 929,241 bytes). Per the Task 5 fallback, CI now runs the Playwright-backed `test:mcp-shim` semantic contract instead of comparing platform-specific generated source. After the rebase onto current main, the checked-in shim already matches main (the MCP door merges refreshed it), so this PR no longer touches the generated file; the semantic gate is the enforcement.

## Code touched and why

- `packages/core/src/conformance/index.ts`: the shared conformance-only `memoryStoreAdapter` was the missing test seam; it now mirrors reserved route validation/projection, derived refs, timestamps, state IDs, and thread ownership while retaining an injectable fixed clock.
- After current main's ENG-254 routing landed, that seam and its test were updated to derive/allow the additive `vendo_apps.trigger_kind` ref exactly like production. `docs/contracts/02-store.md` records the approved dated addendum and routed-ref text.
- apps and guard memory-store fixtures now re-export that canonical seam; affected assertions were aligned with the real store's newest-first ordering.
- fixture HTTP helpers in automations, redteam, and integration retry only transient dev-server socket resets and wait for the required reset route before starting. HTTP error responses are never retried. This is test-harness stabilization for concurrent Next fixture servers, with no runtime behavior change.
- store and corpus Vitest timeouts were raised only for real database / child-process fixtures under the full Turbo graph.
- the generated MCP shim was refreshed. No product runtime behavior was changed.

## Validation

Passed locally without `POSTGRES_URL`:

```text
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
```

Passed locally with disposable PostgreSQL 16 and `POSTGRES_URL=postgres://vendo:vendo@127.0.0.1:55433/vendo_test`:

```text
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
CI=true pnpm turbo run conformance --filter=@vendoai/store --force
```

The full `pnpm test` run exercised all 45 PostgreSQL store conformance/gate tests; the explicit filtered command separately verified the CI-required Turbo env path. Also verified the MCP shim semantic browser contract and package-scoped provider, parity, fixture, and conformance suites. This PR intentionally does not merge itself or change branch protection; the coordinator can make `conformance` required after merge.

After merging current main, focused fresh-cache reruns passed for the canonical core memory seam (13/13) and automations (28/28), including the new `trigger_kind` path. A forced parallel core package run on the shared workstation hit the previously observed environmental 5-second packaging timeout while its conformance tests passed; the focused reruns and PR CI are the authoritative post-merge checks.


## Rebase note (2026-07-15)

Rebased onto main after the ~24-merge wave (streaming engine, catalog registration, custom-fields data plane, grant invalidation, edit reliability, MCP e2e, miss-event contract). Conflict resolutions were conservative: main kept `pnpm test:coverage` as the CI test step (now with `POSTGRES_URL`); package `conformance` scripts were merged alongside main`s `test:coverage` scripts; the canonical `memoryStoreAdapter` keeps main`s `revision`/atomic capabilities on top of this PR`s reserved-route projection; `docs/contracts/02-store.md` carries both dated amendments (atomic revisions + additive `trigger_kind` ref). Full gates re-verified green post-rebase.

body: An Octave row in the Sound group (-2 to +2) that transposes everything that sounds - clicks, musical typing, the scale player, and the fifths tour all go through the same press path - while the visual keyboard stays put, exactly like the octave buttons on a hardware controller. body:
Two fixes the tracks cleanup exposed:

1. **Match by email OR quizCode OR discordId** — auto-linked/clobbered docs often have no email (keyed only by `quizCode`), so email-only matching silently updated the wrong record or none.
2. **Write both `tracks` (array) AND `track` (singular string)** — `lib/access.ts` and the roster read the **singular** `track`; writing only the array left a stale singular value still granting quiz access. This is why editor saves appeared to 'not stick'.

`tsc --noEmit` passes.

body:
## What
- Validate each VideoControl and VideoStreaming descriptor length before dispatching the existing parser.
- Add deterministic synthetic coverage for zero, short-header, and oversized lengths in both descriptor iterators.
- Keep the exact 19-case hardware-independent regression inventory and document the follow-up.

## Why
This is a focused follow-up to the post-merge review of `3d1924607e9bfe9cfebfa9d07ad3944dc4980225`. That review found that both scanner loops trusted the next descriptor's declared length before checking the three-byte header minimum and remaining buffer length. Zero-length descriptors could fail to advance, while oversized lengths could underflow the remaining-byte accounting. The new scanner-level cases reproduce those inputs and the production guards return `UVC_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE` before parser dispatch.

## How to verify
- `cmake -S . -B build/postcommit-gate -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TARGET=Static -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DBUILD_EXAMPLE=OFF -DBUILD_TEST=OFF -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`
- `ctest --test-dir build/postcommit-gate --output-on-failure`
- The six scanner cases pass directly and the complete inventory is 19/19; sanitizer, shared/static, default-off, negative CMake, and actionlint checks are recorded in the attached local gate evidence.

## Risks
The change is limited to malformed descriptor-length validation in the two existing iterator loops. Valid descriptors and parser behavior are unchanged; no USB hardware is required for these tests.

author: saden1
body:
Device follow-up to #994. The white-noise keep-alive was **audible hiss over CarPlay**; this carries the same route-keeping energy as a low ~70 Hz sine tone, which is inaudible.

## Problem / Why

#994 added a keep-alive to stop the route idling between per-sentence clips — but it used **white noise**, and on-device that was noticeable hiss. Broadband noise spreads energy across the whole spectrum, including the **2–5 kHz band where hearing is most sensitive**, so even a low level reads as hiss — the most attention-grabbing artifact there is. (On-device report: the choppiness/popping was fixed, but the hiss was unacceptable.)

## What changed

`docs/src/lib/suono/stage.ts` — the keep-alive is now a continuous **low-frequency (~70 Hz) sine tone** (an `OscillatorNode`) instead of a looping noise `AudioBufferSourceNode`.

- **Same energy, moved out of the audible band.** The ear is ~40+ dB less sensitive at 70 Hz (equal-loudness contours), so the same route-keeping level is inaudible — and a faint hum, not hiss, if heard at all. 70 Hz stays **above deep sub-bass** (less likely to be *felt* through a subwoofer) yet **well inside every A2DP codec's passband** (the far end still sees signal, not silence, so the link stays warm). A concentrated tone also reads at least as "loud" to a silence detector as spread noise of equal level.
- New `keepAliveHz` `StageOption` (default 70); default `keepAliveGain` lowered to ~0.001 (≈ -60 dBFS). Both device-tunable.
- **Everything else is unchanged** — the idle-release lifecycle, barge-in survival, `dispose()` teardown, and the provable clock-independence (never in `activeSources`, never touches `currentTime`/onset) are exactly as merged in #994.

## Tests

- `docs/src/lib/suono/stage.test.ts` — 17/17. The keep-alive mock + assertions now build/track an oscillator and assert its **frequency** and **gain** (plus the unchanged clock-untouched, idempotent, barge-in-survives, dispose-stops, idle-release, and cancel-on-next-clip cases).
- Full audio suite 121/121 (suono + read-aloud + voice-model). `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (biome), `npm run build:check` all green.
- No shared Studio UI chrome touched.

## Caveats / not verified

- **Device-only, UNVERIFIED from CI (HARD RULE #23):** *"no hiss AND no choppiness over real CarPlay"* can only be confirmed on a real iPhone in the car. My expectation: 70 Hz at ~-60 dBFS is inaudible while keeping the link warm — but the exact `keepAliveGain`/`keepAliveHz` may need one on-device pass (drop the gain if any low hum is *felt*; raise it if choppiness returns).
- No behavior change on wired/speaker output; not a breaking change.

author: mikeoye11-priest
body:
## The disappearing-workspace bug
`loadWorkspace` called `res.json()` **without checking `res.ok`**, so a transient 401/500 from `GET /api/workspace` gave `workspace=undefined` → `parsed=null` → it **removed the localStorage backup and forced onboarding**. Re-onboarding then saved a fresh minimal workspace over the real one. The route compounded it by using `.single()`, which errors on "no row" and returned `{workspace:null}` — conflating empty with failure.

## Fix
- **Route:** `maybeSingle()` + return 500 on a real error, so "no workspace" (null) is distinct from "couldn't load".
- **Client:** treat a non-OK/exception as "server unreachable" → fall back to the local backup and **never destroy it**. Only clear the backup + onboard when a *reachable* server authoritatively reports no workspace for a signed-in user. Consolidated the duplicated restore into one helper.

Save guard already prevents clobber during the load window (`hasRealData` is false for the seeded "Your Firm"/"Your Company" defaults). Build clean.

author: lcsgmoraes-droid
krisbraun
body:
## Problem

Replies and forwards sent through the composite Google connector ("Gmail & Calendar") went out with a bare email address as the sender, so recipients saw an address instead of a name — including in the attribution line their client generates when quoting the message.

## Cause

The composite reuses the Gmail send path, which resolves the account's display name from Google's userinfo endpoint to build a `"Name" <email>` From header. That endpoint was missing from the composite's own Network allowlist, so the outbound proxy refused the lookup and the send path fell back to a bare address.

A connector declares its allowlist in `build()`, and **a composite does not inherit the allowlists of the connectors whose code it reuses**. Adding the endpoint to the standalone `gmail` package therefore had no effect on the composite — which is the package that actually deploys. Tests passed on both sides of the gap, because each package only covered itself.

## Fix

Add the userinfo endpoint to the composite's allowlist. The new test drives the composite's real `build()` and asserts the allowlist, so this can't silently regress.

## Also: make the fallback observable

The lookup is deliberately best-effort — a failure must never block a send — but two paths degraded silently, which is why a total failure looked like a working fix:

- **403** (endpoint absent from the allowlist, or a grant without the `profile` scope) logged only a generic warning. It now logs an error naming both causes. A 403 here is a misconfiguration that degrades *every* send for a connection, not a transient blip.
- **200 with no `name` claim** — what a grant without the `profile` scope returns — threw nothing at all and silently produced a bare address. It now logs an error pointing at re-authorization.

`getUserInfo` throws a typed `UserInfoError` carrying the HTTP status, so callers can separate a misconfiguration from a transient failure instead of matching on message text.

## Notes for connector authors

Connections whose grant predates the `profile` scope being requested still send a bare address: userinfo answers 200 without a `name` claim, and no re-request can add a scope to an existing grant. Those connections need to be re-authorized. The new error log makes this case identifiable rather than invisible.

## Testing

- New: composite allowlist test (fails without the fix), plus coverage for the 403 and no-`name` paths.
- `connector-google` 66 tests pass; `connector-gmail` 131 tests pass; lint clean on both.

body:
## Summary
- Fix 인원 체크 class-card synchronization so the current `dateKey + slotKey` preset is the source of truth for default class cards.
- Exclude empty stale/orphan classes that are not in the selected slot preset from the edit screen, local auto-save, and save payload.
- Preserve data-bearing classes outside the preset with a `설정 외` badge so existing real records are not silently deleted.
- Add slot/date/class scoped tombstones for X delete, with undo restore and `+ 반 추가` clearing the tombstone.

## Cause
The previous merge logic always appended every saved holding class that was not in the active slot preset. Empty stale classes such as `JONGHA반` and `MINGI반` could therefore reappear in `월/수 오전` even after the slot preset had been changed to only `HYOJU반` and `JEFF반`.

## Source Of Truth / Merge Handling
- Current slot preset creates the default 인원 체크 class cards.
- Tombstone key: `dateKey::slotKey::normalizedClassName`.
- Empty non-preset classes are treated as stale/orphan data and removed.
- Non-preset classes with real data remain visible as `설정 외` and are included while they have data.
- Manually added empty classes can be edited in the current session, but are not persisted to localStorage or record payload until they contain data.

## Scope Safety
- `MINGI반` in the weekend preset remains unaffected because deletion/exclusion is scoped by date and slot, not by global class name.
- Historical records rendering is not filtered by current presets.
- Google Sheets endpoint, Apps Script files, payload contract, and production server code were not changed.

## QA
- [x] `월/수 오전` stale saved classes `JONGHA반`, `MINGI반` are excluded; displayed/local-saved classes become `HYOJU반`, `JEFF반`.
- [x] Data-bearing external `JONGHA반` remains visible with `설정 외`.

author: larrypsmith
body:
Our Distr publish pipeline modeled each release channel as its own application (`copia`, `copia-edge`, `copia-pr`), but every channel pushed its chart to the same `oci://$DST/copia` artifact and hard-coded the ApplicationVersion `chart-url` there. So edge and PR builds landed in the customer-facing `copia` artifact, cluttering what a production customer browses and pulls, and the three applications never actually separated anything beyond the version name.

This change collapses the three applications into a single `copia` application and gives each channel its own artifact repo: stable to `copia`, edge to `copia-edge`, PR to `copia-pr`. Each channel still creates an ApplicationVersion, so edge and PR stay deployable through Distr for validation, but its `chart-url` now points at the per-channel repo. Which versions a customer sees is left to per-version entitlements; edge and PR versions are simply never entitled, so they stay invisible without needing a separate application.

Edge versions move to `<next-minor>-edge.<epoch>.<sha8>` (for example `1.4.0-edge.1752494400.abc1234` when `1.3.5` is the latest release): the numeric epoch orders builds chronologically per semver, the next-minor base sorts edge above the last release but below the next final, and the sha8 keeps traceability. After each edge publish the workflow archives superseded edge versions so only the newest stays live. PR cleanup now archives the PR ApplicationVersion under `copia` and deletes the PR tags from the `copia-pr` artifact; note artifact tags are hard-deleted, unlike ApplicationVersions which are archived.

I kept the existing two-target matrix so every channel still publishes to both Distr cloud and staging during rollout; a comment in each caller notes the future split where production and edge live only in the prod instance and PR lives only in staging.

Before the first cloud edge/PR publish, audit existing `copia` entitlements so they list explicit stable version IDs rather than an empty (all-versions) list, otherwise edge/PR versions would become visible. The old `copia-edge` and `copia-pr` applications can be retired in both instances once no new versions land there.

body:
## What / Why

Issue #5326 evaluates the signed `temporal_robustness` objective against the
`worst_case_snqi` baseline under **matched simulator-call budgets** across the
search families **random, TPE, and CMA-ES-class**. The prior cheap-lane slices
(PR #5333 runner/config, #5658 contract, #5684/#5700 durable table, #5694
multi-objective manifest, #5708 canonical-command test) built the full
comparison pipeline and durable-table DoD item, but the CMA-ES-class search
family named in the issue scope was never implemented — `build_sampler` only
offered `random`, `coordinate`, and `optuna` (TPE). This PR adds the missing
CMA-ES-class family as **new capability** (successor slice; does not duplicate
PR #5333/#5700/#5708).

## Change

- `robot_sf/adversarial/samplers.py`: new `CmaEsCandidateSampler` (Covariance
  Matrix Adaptation ES via the declared `cma` dependency) implementing the
  `FeedbackCandidateSampler` contract. It buffers a full CMA-ES generation
  internally (the sequential runner calls `sample`/`observe` one candidate at a
  time) and feeds the population back in a single `tell`. Degenerate (fixed)
  search-space dimensions are held at their midpoint; the all-degenerate case
  is supported on fixture bounds.
- `scripts/tools/compare_adversarial_samplers.py`: `build_sampler` + CLI
  `--sampler` choices + default sampler set now include `cmaes`.
- `configs/adversarial/issue_5326_objective_comparison.yaml`: the committed
  manifest now lists `cmaes` so the durable comparison table covers all three
  required search families.
- Tests: focused unit test for the sampler (in-bounds proposals + feedback) and
  a `run_sampler_comparison` CMA-ES-class cell; manifest-driven row counts and
  sampler tuples updated from 54/3 to 72/4.

- `uv run pytest tests/benchmark/test_adversarial_package_b_manifest_run.py -k 5326` — 7 passed (incl. canonical-command durable-table emit, now 72 cells)

This is a cheap-lane **infrastructure** slice: it adds the CMA-ES-class search
capability and wires it into the comparison/durable-table pipeline. It does NOT
execute the actual matched-budget campaign, certification/replay, or
independent-seed confirmation — those remain the SLURM-capable-worker
Definition-of-Done items (issue #5326 still requires real campaign execution and
a durable stop-rule decision from artifact-level evidence). No paper-facing
benchmark claim is made.

author: sebastienstdenis
body:
Clicking bare page now fires a soundwave pulse from the pointer instead of watching the ambient loop. The automatic center pulses pause while the visitor is clicking and resume after 2 seconds of no clicks, so the wave reads as an easter egg on the field and the random ambient ones stay the default.

## Changes

All in `soundwave-dots.tsx`; no other file is touched.

- Pulses carry their own origin (`x`, `y`) and `maxRadius`. Previously every wave radiated from the viewport center, so dot displacement could be computed from one shared center vector; now each dot sums a push vector per pulse. An off-center pulse also fades over its own reach (the farthest corner from where it fired) rather than the center's, so a click near an edge doesn't die early.
- A window-level `click` listener spawns a pulse at `clientX`/`clientY` and stamps `lastClick`. The auto-spawn timer keeps ticking but skips spawning while `lastClick` is under `IDLE_RESUME` (2s) old, so the first automatic wave after the visitor stops arrives a natural gap later rather than as a backlog burst.
- `isBackground()` gates the wave: only a click landing on `<body>` or `<main>` - the layout shells the dots show through - plays the field. Anything with content on it (text, button, card, form field) is ordinary UI and leaves the field silent, and doesn't reset the idle timer either, so the ambient loop keeps running while someone fills in a login form. Every page carrying the soundwave wraps its content in `<main>`; on the login and signup pages `<main>` is a narrow `max-w-sm` column, so clicks beside the card land on `<body>` and still play.
- A `mousedown` handler calls `preventDefault()` only when `event.detail > 1` **and** the target is the background, so double-clicking bare page can't snap a highlight onto the nearest word. All copy stays fully selectable everywhere, including drag-select, and single clicks behave normally (focus and blur are untouched).
- Both listeners are only attached when `prefers-reduced-motion` is not set, matching the existing still-frame path, and both are removed on cleanup. With reduced motion the page behaves normally: no waves, no selection handling.

Asking what a click landed *on*, rather than enumerating what it must avoid, is what keeps this small: no card selector, no `user-select` rule, no body class, no stylesheet change at all.

## Verification

`npm run lint` and `npm run build` both pass. The landing page renders the canvas and returns 200 from the dev server.

No browser automation was available in this environment, so I could not visually confirm the behavior. Worth an eyeball before merge: the wave feel on click, the 2s handoff back to the ambient loop, that only bare page plays, and that double-clicking bare page doesn't highlight anything.

author: krilliac
body:
## Outcome

ReSymbol can now turn a validated `.resym` analysis session into:

- a deterministic, debugger-neutral JSON symbol projection;
- a self-contained IDAPython importer; or
- a self-contained Ghidra Java importer.

The new `resymbol export` command provides predictable default filenames, refuses to overwrite existing output, and reports projected symbol and warning counts.

## Approach

- Add `resymbol-export`, a bounded neutral projection that reconciles functions, globals, types, names, boundaries, confidence, and provenance without changing the canonical symbol graph.
- Preserve source spellings and competing claims while generating unique, portable debugger-facing names.
- Resolve authority deterministically (user decisions, then core facts, then plugin claims) and emit structured warnings for ambiguity, loss, invalid text, overlaps, and collisions.
- Generate conservative IDA and Ghidra scripts that verify the exact input SHA-256 before mutation, resolve RVAs through the loaded image base, preserve protected names and existing function bodies, and reject names on the wrong program object.
- Bound generated scripts and Ghidra records; a Ghidra Java export fails before writing when more than 20,000 records would be emitted.
- Document export workflows, limitations, and the approved future workbench GUI/theme direction.

## User impact

A normal user can analyze once and produce immediately loadable IDA or Ghidra symbol scripts without installing another compiler, runtime, or ReSymbol plugin. JSON retains the richer evidence and conflict model for inspection and future writers.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- Workspace doctests
- 127 workspace tests plus the external-process custom harness
- Targeted exporter/CLI tests after final hardening, including deterministic output, hostile text, collision handling, no-overwrite behavior, identity gates, and the Ghidra record ceiling

## Compatibility and security

This adds projection schema version 1 and new CLI output formats without changing the existing `.resym` package schema. Debugger scripts mutate only after an exact SHA-256 match. They preserve user/imported names, never replace existing function bodies, avoid globals inside functions, and continue safely after independent per-symbol failures. PDB/MAP/DWARF, prototype/type application, provenance comments, and interactive bridges remain explicitly out of scope.

author: quanghuy128
body:
## Summary

- Adds the **P1 slice** of the Run Engine (v2 execution feature, explicitly deferred from the v1 spec): execute a **published command** node from the dependency graph via a headless `claude -p --output-format stream-json` spawn in the daemon, watch it live (node glow, raw log tail, cancel), and control it from a bottom-dock run bar visible app-wide.
- **Not included** (tracked as follow-ups in `docs/loops/graph-execution-realtime-STATE.md` §8.7): structured token telemetry / roll-up UI (P2 — needs a real subagent-dispatch fixture recorded first), run history popover + F5 replay UX + `Settings → Execution` editor (P3).
- Full pipeline artifacts for this feature: `docs/loops/graph-execution-realtime-STATE.md` (spec + architecture plan + build/QA notes), `-design.md` (UI spec), `-testplan.md` (the /qa contract).

## Why

Symbion could author workflows (commands/agents as `.md` files) but never run them from the tool itself — closing the author → execute → observe loop is the core ask. This PR lands the smallest slice that's genuinely useful on its own: click Execute, watch it run, cancel if needed, see what changed.

## Security (this is a new capability class — process spawn on a previously spawn-free, tokenless localhost daemon)

- `argv`-array spawn only, **never** a shell string — the user's requirement text is a single argv element (injection-tested with hostile shell metacharacters — all arrive as inert literal bytes, no shell evaluation occurs).
- `cwd` is always resolved server-side from the registered project; a client can never supply an arbitrary path.
- **Daemon-minted** (not UI-minted — an earlier draft of this design was unimplementable for that reason, see STATE §8.8 Flaw F1), single-use, 120s-TTL, config-bound consent nonce gates `startRun`, so a bare `curl`/forged RPC call cannot spawn a process.
- Cancel does SIGTERM→SIGKILL on the process group and **verifies liveness before ever reporting "cancelled"** — never claims a process is dead while it might still be running.
- Independently reviewed by `code-reviewer`, `architect`, and `security-reviewer` (all **PASS**) — one real bug found and fixed along the way: a TOCTOU race in the "1 active run per project" lock (two concurrent `startRun` calls could both pass the check before either's async CLI-version probe resolved), closed by making the lock reservation the last synchronous step before any `await`, with a genuinely-concurrent regression test (the original test used an artificial delay and didn't actually exercise the race).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npm run test:core` — 181/181
- [x] `npm run test:daemon` — 384/384 (incl. injection, nonce replay/binding/expiry, process-group kill, concurrency race, SSE Origin/Host allowlist, boot reconciliation)
- [x] `npm run test:web` — 11/11
- [x] Live manual QA (chrome-devtools/Playwright against a hermetic fake-CLI daemon + a real dev daemon+web pair): execute happy path, first-run consent (persists correctly across reopens), requirement pre-fill from last run, draft-blocked → inline Publish → auto-unblock without reopening the dialog, two-step Cancel from both the mission-mode strip and the app-wide run bar (verified against on-disk `run.json` + OS process death, not just the UI)
- [x] Security review — see above
- [ ] P2/P3 manual journey steps (J12+) — not applicable to this PR's scope

Full detail and defect-by-defect QA evidence: STATE §10 (first QA pass, found 4 defects), §11 (fix pass), §12 (re-verification, PASS).

body:
## What changed

One combined release resolving **every finding** of the v0.24.19 three-audit deep-mining pass (bug hunt on the newest code · end-to-end flow trace · tool-coverage analysis). Nothing skipped.

### Correctness (8)
- **`_acl_public` flags `AuthenticatedUsers` grants as public** — a real public-bucket exposure the security review previously reported clean *(the audit's #1)*.
- `overall_status='inconclusive'` when every config read errored (was `"reviewed"`).
- `_policy_facts` exact `'*'` principal match — a `role/deploy-*` ARN no longer false-CRITICALs "Anonymous GetObject".
- No-manifest multi-part inventory combine: header-dedupe only when part 0 really carries a header (headerless parts lost one **data row per part**; access-log parts lost a log line each).
- Headerless-inventory timestamps: date-only + epoch (s/ms) columns detected; epochs converted to ISO at import.
- `get_object_attributes` checksum algo from a known-algorithm whitelist (no more possible `"Type"`).
- Cancel path applies `_hold_back_contract` (no dangling ```` ```json ```` fence in persisted partials).
- Code-less 403 on `test_credentials` is a failure, not "authenticated (ListBuckets denied)".

### Flows (10)
- **Session uploads stream in 1 MiB chunks with the 2 GiB cap + HTTP 413** — the live composer endpoint buffered whole files in RAM with **no limit** (OOM on multi-GB inventories); the protection existed only on an endpoint the frontend never calls. Partial file removed on refusal.
- `.gz` access logs decompress (raw-bytes read → falsely-clean "no anomalies"); `.tsv` parses tab-separated in both importers + detector; `.json`/`.jsonl` selectable in the composer (backend always parsed JSONL).
- Steering (Enter mid-run) carries a pending attachment through the dataset-upload path instead of silently dropping it.
- Model-provider **Test performs a live probe** (`GET {base}/models`, 5 s timeout): key accepted / rejected / unreachable / reachable-but-no-`/models`. Secret resolved server-side only; nothing echoed.
- Fork copies `session_runs` links → run-dependent proposal cards stay actionable.
- Deleting a session mid-turn cancels the **server-side** turn too (new `registerTurnCancel`).
- Session report lists only terminal runs; RunDetail localizes status/run_type/severity enums (new `runtype.*` i18n keys, en+zh).

### Tool coverage (6 dropped-field surfacings + 3 new tools)
- `head_object`: +`replication_status`, `restore` (GLACIER progress/expiry), `archive_status`, `parts_count`, `lifecycle_expiration`, `version_id`, `content_type`/`content_encoding`/`cache_control`, `website_redirect_location`; accepts `version_id`.

- `list_object_versions`: `sample_versions[]` with `version_id`/`is_latest`/`is_delete_marker`/size/class.

- Everything remains read-only `get_*`/`list_*`/`head_*`; no body downloads; static `test_s3_safety` passes.
- Presigned-URL parser: no request made; credential material never enters the result (test asserts no leak).

## Summary

- Complete semantic matrix, including full SelectN and PayCosts descriptors and both Generic fallbacks

- Candidate/payment re-prompts retain the exact bound route
  Test: `PromptRouteBindingTest.PayCosts candidate and payment re-prompts retain the original route`
- Each response family accepts its compatible bound routes, including established EffectCost compatibility across PayCosts, SelectN, and Generic Targeting

body:
## Summary
The previous debias (#169) over-corrected: it stopped the "guess the film's famous cue" hallucination, but it also made the audio-listen model refuse to name the **composer** on genuine orchestral score cues — e.g. A Beautiful Mind's "Tanks — June Marx" false match, which the benchmark/ChatGPT reliably heard as a James Horner score, now came back `title:null, is_score_cue:null, low`.

The benchmark's finding is that the **composer/style is reliable, the exact title is not**. So the prompt now separates the two judgements instead of suppressing both:

```diff
- "...do NOT let the film's reputation influence your guess. If the audio is faint ... return a null
-  title and low confidence rather than guessing a well-known track. Only give a title you can hear."
+ "...never invent a specific well-known track title just to fit the film.
+  Separate two judgements:
+   (a) exact TITLE — only if you genuinely recognise it by ear, else null;
+   (b) whether it's an instrumental score cue and, if so, the likely COMPOSER and style —
+       you MAY name the composer/style even without the exact cue title, since composer is
+       more reliable than title.
+  If too faint/buried to tell anything, return nulls and low confidence."
```

Verified on both [REDACTED SECRET] (3× each):
- **A Beautiful Mind / Tanks** (should be a score cue): now `is_score_cue:true, medium`, and names **James Horner** — vs `null/null/low` before.
- **Joker / street scene** (the famous-cue trap): still `title:null, artist:null` — no "Rock and Roll Part 2 — Gary Glitter" hallucination.

Still advisory-only; title stays null when it can't genuinely hear it.

author: caioross
body:
## Contexto

`window.insertMessage` disparava o `fetch` da OpenAI sem controle de ciclo de vida: sem guarda de reentrância e com o `AbortController` preso em variável local. Isso causava (issue #27) envios concorrentes (múltiplos `#typing-row` com mesmo `id`, histórico fora de ordem, chamadas pagas em paralelo) e resposta do personagem antigo vazando para o novo ao trocar na gôndola.

## O que mudou e por quê

`js/mainJs.js` (único arquivo tocado, +37/-4):

1. **Estado de módulo `pending`** (`{ controller, timeoutId, cancelled }`) ao lado de `conversation`/`currentPerson` — dá controle de ciclo de vida à requisição.
2. **Lock de reentrância**: `insertMessage` retorna cedo se `pending` existir, e `setChatBusy(true)` desabilita `#chat-input` + `.action-box-submit` (estado `disabled` nativo — bloqueio visível). Cobre todos os pontos de entrada (Enter, botão, starter chips).
3. **Cancelamento na troca de personagem**: `applyPerson` marca `pending.cancelled = true`, aborta o controller e libera o lock. O handler `.then`/`.catch` da requisição antiga vê `cancelled` e descarta em silêncio — nada é renderizado nem entra no `conversation` do novo personagem.
4. **Silêncio no cancelamento intencional**: o guard `cancelled` fica **antes** do `appendAIMessage`, distinguindo-o do `AbortError` de timeout (que mantém `cancelled = false` e segue exibindo a mensagem de `chatErrorMessage`).
5. **Invariante do typing-row**: `showTyping` chama `hideTyping()` primeiro → `document.querySelectorAll('#typing-row').length <= 1` por construção.

## Acceptance criteria (#27)

- [x] Novo envio com resposta em voo não dispara 2º `fetch` (lock + input/botão desabilitados, visível).
- [x] Nunca mais de um `#typing-row` no DOM.
- [x] `applyPerson()` aborta a pendente; resposta antiga não é renderizada nem entra no `conversation` novo.
- [x] Abort por troca de personagem não exibe erro no chat (distinto do timeout).
- [x] Timeout de 30s (`OPENAI_TIMEOUT`) intacto.
- [x] `node scripts/gate.mjs` verde.

## Resultado do gate (real)

`node scripts/gate.mjs` → **GATE VERDE — 19/19 checagens passaram** (rodado no worktree). Não toca `js/personalities.js`.

## Teste manual sugerido (fluxo depende de chave OpenAI real; placeholder no repo)

Com uma chave válida em `OPENAI_KEY`:
1. **Lock**: envie uma pergunta e, antes da resposta, tente enviar outra (Enter/botão/chip) → input e botão ficam desabilitados; nenhum 2º balão "digitando" surge; só uma resposta chega, na ordem.
2. **Troca de personagem**: envie para Cleópatra → antes da resposta, troque para Einstein na gôndola → a resposta de Cleópatra **não** aparece, não há avatar trocado nem mensagem de erro, e o chat do Einstein começa limpo.
3. **Timeout**: (opcional) reduza `OPENAI_TIMEOUT` e verifique que a mensagem ⌛ ainda aparece normalmente.

## Riscos

Baixo, escopo restrito ao fluxo de envio. Fallback sem `AbortController` preservado (resposta ainda é descartada via flag `cancelled`, sem regressão). Nenhuma dependência nova, zero-build mantido.

Toca o fluxo do chat/OpenAI → **Solicito quórum (HANDBOOK §7)**.

Closes #27

author: c-bata
body:
<!-- Thank you for creating a pull request! In general, we merge your pull request after it gets two or more approvals. To proceed to the review process by the maintainers, please make sure that the PR meets the following conditions: (1) it passes all CI checks, and (2) it is neither in the draft nor WIP state. To minimize the review effort, we highly appreciate PRs only with related changes. Please note that submitted PRs may be closed if they include unrelated changes or significantly modified unit tests. If you wish to discuss the PR in the draft state or need any other help, please mention the Optuna development team in the PR. -->

## Motivation
<!-- Describe your motivation why you will submit this PR. This is useful for reviewers to understand the context of PR. -->

`Study.user_attrs` and `Study.system_attrs` can read an internal attribute dictionary after the storage lock has been released. When another thread updates the same study attribute dictionary concurrently, the reader may fail with:

```text
RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
```

## Description of the changes
<!-- Describe the changes in this PR. -->

This PR updates study attributes using copy-on-write in:

- InMemoryStorage
- JournalStorageReplayResult

As a result, readers keep observing the previous immutable dictionary while the writer replaces it with an updated dictionary.

## Steps to reproduce

The following script reproduces the issue on master:

```python
import threading
import optuna
from optuna.storages import InMemoryStorage

storage = InMemoryStorage()
study = optuna.create_study(storage=storage)
study.set_user_attr("key1", "value1")
study.set_user_attr("key2", "value2")

ready = threading.Event()
updated = threading.Event()


def writer() -> None:
    ready.wait()
    study.set_user_attr("key3", "value3")
    updated.set()


def reader() -> None:
    attrs = storage.get_study_user_attrs(study._study_id)
    for i, attr in enumerate(attrs):
        if i == 0:
            ready.set()
            updated.wait()
        print(attr)


tw = threading.Thread(target=writer)
tr = threading.Thread(target=reader)

tw.start()
tr.start()
tw.join()
tr.join()
```

author: sjpadgett
body:
Summary

This PR updates OpenEMR’s U2F security-key workflow to use the browser Web Authentication API.

The existing registration page relied on the legacy U2F JavaScript API. That API is no longer supported by current Chrome, Edge, and Firefox releases, causing the **Register** button to appear nonfunctional and preventing the normal operating-system security-key prompt from being displayed.

Changes

* Replace the legacy U2F browser registration call with `navigator.credentials.create()`.
* Replace the legacy U2F authentication call with `navigator.credentials.get()`.
* Convert server-provided challenges and credential IDs from base64url into `ArrayBuffer` values required by WebAuthn.
* Serialize WebAuthn credential responses back into base64url values for server-side processing.
* Add user-visible handling for unsupported browsers, cancelled prompts, invalid responses, and registration failures.
* Preserve the existing server-side challenge, CSRF, user, and credential validation flow.
* Preserve compatibility with existing OpenEMR security-key configuration where supported.

Problem fixed

Previously, clicking **Register** with a YubiKey inserted did not trigger any browser or Windows security-key prompt.

This occurred because the legacy extension-based U2F API was unavailable in modern browsers.

After this change, the browser invokes its native WebAuthn flow and displays the expected security-key prompt.

Clicking **Register** now opens the browser or operating-system security-key dialog. After the user activates the key, the credential is stored and can be used for subsequent MFA authentication.

Related issue

Fixes #12989

Three groups of fixes surfaced while running `/bs:quality --merge 558` and auditing the kit-pro collapse leftovers.

## 1. OSS boundary — remove private founder tooling from the public kit

`market-validation` and `office-hours` evaluate business ideas/markets, which crosses the OSS line (setup CLAUDE.md: *anything that evaluates an idea or market is private*). Private copies were taken into claude-setup top-level (#555) but the public copies here were never removed — so the kit still shipped and advertised them.

- Remove `skills/market-validation`, `skills/office-hours`, `commands/bs/office-hours.md`
- Scrub README, plugin.json, marketplace.json, EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md, workflow/SKILL.md of the removed tooling + "founder domain intelligence" copy

## 2. Quality-pipeline bugs (found running `--merge 558`)

- **Wrapper self-loop** (`commands/bs/quality.md`): re-invoking with the already-transformed args (`--args-file … --merge N`) re-ran the whole persist+invoke preamble forever. Added a Step 0 guard.
- **Bare PR# rejected** (`quality-target-resolver.js`): `--merge 558` matched no PR pattern and fell through to a cwd audit. Added `applyBarePrToken` — a bare integer under `--merge` is a PR#. Runs last + only under `--merge`, can't shadow a branch/path/flag. +3 tests.
- **False `commitTripped`** (`quality-run-governor.js` + `quality-bootstrap.sh`): commit budget was total-ancestry `rev-list --count HEAD` minus a numeric baseline; under `--merge <PR>` the baseline (PR worktree) and the later check (differently-based HEAD) produced a bogus cross-baseline delta (observed `commitsUsed: 21` with **zero** fix commits). Now baselines by HEAD SHA and counts `<sha>..HEAD` — rebase/checkout-immune. Legacy sentinels fall back to the old path. +3 tests.

## 3. Mechanical model routing (cost)

Per-call `model: "sonnet"` where the work is search/read/analysis, not the session's judgment work:

- `dev`: the `Explore` subagent
- `triage --fix`: the root-cause hypothesis subagent (makes the budget gate's documented "hypothesis → Sonnet, fix → session" tiering real)

Both are per-call Agent-tool overrides, **not** frontmatter pins, so neither trips the 1M-context Extra Usage billing gate. The `quality` skill's review agents are deliberately left unpinned (documented reason) — untouched.

author: jameswinegar
body:
## What
Upgrades the MotherDuck destination's `append_dedup` path and its test coverage, bumping the connector to 0.3.0.

- **Native `MERGE INTO` for append_dedup** — replaces the CDK's emulated UPDATE-then-INSERT fallback (requires duckdb >= 1.5.0, now pinned).
- **Dedup ordered by cursor field** — deduplication now picks the winning row by the stream's cursor field instead of extraction time.
- **CDC deletes applied in append_dedup** — records with `_ab_cdc_deleted_at` set are deleted from the final table instead of upserted.
- **Schema compatibility via information_schema** — avoids SQLAlchemy reflection, which queries `pg_catalog.pg_collation` (absent in DuckDB 1.4.x).

## Tests
- New unit suites: native merge, cursor ordering, CDC deletes, schema compatibility (63 tests passing).
- The same suite runs against a live MotherDuck database when `MOTHERDUCK_API_KEY` is set (optional `MOTHERDUCK_TEST_DB`, default `airbyte_test`). Each session writes to throwaway `test_*` schemas and drops them at teardown through the connector's own engine config.

## Notes
- Ruff format + import sorting applied to all new files.
- Verified end-to-end against MotherDuck with a live token.

author: g0rgonus
body:
## What

Adds a **review stage** to the results intake form. Before submitting, it parses the chosen file **in the browser** (shared `swimparse` + JSZip for `.zip`) and shows the **meet date, teams, and final score** — flagging any file dated to a previous year.

Motivation: a team re-submitted last year's results in error. The date-forward preview catches wrong-file / prior-season resubmissions before they reach n8n.

## Flow

Enter email + file → **Review results →** preview card → **Confirm & submit** (only then does anything reach n8n). A **Back** button returns to editing.

## Design

Parsing happens **client-side**, preserving the intake service's invariant: the server still forwards the file **untouched** and never parses (also keeps untrusted zip-decompression off the server). Mirrors the existing `entry-summary.html` client-side pattern.

- `server.mjs` — serves `../swimparse/src` read-only at `/vendor/swimparse` (single source, no committed copy); adds the JSZip CDN to CSP `script-src`.
- `Dockerfile` — copies `swimparse/src` into the image so the mount resolves.
- `public/index.html` / `public/app.js` — two-stage review/confirm UI; `app.js` is now an ES module.
- Degrades gracefully: a file that won't parse shows a warning but can still be submitted.

## Verification

Server boots; the full swimparse import chain serves 200; `node --check` passes on both JS files; parse+score on the fixture yields the correct date, teams, and totals with the stale-year flag computing correctly. Live browser click-through not run in this environment.

author: aeyakovenko
body:
## Public TDD

This regression reaches the lifecycle failure using only public LiteSVM instructions and a normally initialized market:

1. initialize a two-slot market and an empty user portfolio;
2. configure and legitimately update asset 1's authenticated mark;
3. call the sole public `PermissionlessCrank`, which advances K while the asset has zero effective OI, positions, loss weight, or obligations;
4. retire the empty asset;
5. reactivate the same finite slot under a fresh market id.

On parent engine `143e68c`, step 4 fails with wrapper `Custom(21)` / `EngineLockActive`. Shutdown does not recover the slot because the same empty-state predicate also blocks restart and retirement from Recovery.

With engine PR aeyakovenko/percolator#123 at `7b57c3b8baa684d0d0283fb06babfe4900128a5e`, retire canonicalizes the inert K history and reactivation succeeds. The test checks CU ceilings and proves engine vault accounting, real SPL custody, and the user's capital are unchanged across retirement and reuse.

## Impact

This is a partial public DoS. After any legitimate oracle move, a permissionless cranker can otherwise make an unused configured asset slot permanently unreusable, consuming finite listing capacity. No state injection, malformed account, or initialization mistake is required.

## Scope

- Pin engine PR #123.
- Add one net-new public LiteSVM regression.
- No wrapper program-code change.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo build-sbf --tools-version v1.52`
- Built both `auth_matcher` and `hostile_matcher` SBF fixtures
- `cargo test --all-targets`: 5 wrapper unit tests and 564 LiteSVM tests pass

author: lyfne123
body:
## Summary

Removes duplication across the IR Python layer, in three independent groups (combines what were PRs #2054 and #2055).

### 1. Compiled-program runtime facade
`CompiledProgram`, `_SubChipCallable`, and `DistributedCompiledProgram` each re-maintained the same runtime facade.
- **Unify param-metadata extraction.** `distributed_compiled_program._extract_param_infos_from_func` was a verbatim copy of `compiled_program._extract_func_param_infos` that had drifted to a bare/untyped signature and a shorter error message. Deleted it; the distributed path reuses `_extract_func_param_infos`. Only observable change: the distributed `TypeError` gains the richer `". Expected ShapedType or ScalarType."` wording.
- **Share the debug-runner emitter.** The byte-identical `_emit_debug_runner` bodies become one module-level `_write_debug_runner(output_dir, platform, get_metadata)`.
- **Light runtime-facade mixin.** `load` / `chip_callable` / `runtime_name` / `runtime_config` / `_ensure_runtime_loaded`, duplicated between `CompiledProgram` and `_SubChipCallable`, move into a `_RuntimeFacade` mixin. `CompiledProgram`'s multi-orch guard is preserved via an overridable `_check_runtime_access()` hook. `DistributedCompiledProgram` has no such facade and is untouched — no `__call__` / execution semantics are merged.

### 2. Small shared helpers
- **`_to_int32_scalar`** (RNG seed normalizer) was copy-pasted byte-for-byte in `op/tensor_ops.py` and `op/tile_ops.py`; moved to the shared `ir/utils.py`.
- **Builder `output()` / `outputs()`** — identical across `ForLoopBuilder` / `WhileLoopBuilder` / `IfStmtBuilder` (differing only in the "for loop" / "while loop" / "if statement" message label) — extracted into a `_ReturnVarsAccessor` mixin; each builder sets `_result_kind`.

### 3. Dead code
- `jit/specializer._collect_dep_names` had no callers anywhere — deleted.

### Review feedback addressed
- Builder `output()`/`outputs()` raise `RuntimeError` (not `assert`, which `-O` strips).
- `_write_debug_runner` wraps the script write in its best-effort try/except so a debug-file I/O error never crashes compilation.
- `_RuntimeFacade._ensure_runtime_loaded` publishes the `_chip_callable` sentinel last, after `_runtime_name` / `_runtime_config`.

## Not in scope
- Two items from the original review were already resolved by #2035 (ST fuzz framework removal): `_analyze_input_usage` and the Torch golden op-conversion duplication.
- `DistributedCompiledProgram`'s static `_build_full_args` near-duplicates the module-level one but intentionally omits an in-place-style hint in its `ValueError`; merging it would change a user-facing message, so it is left as a follow-up.

## Testing
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `pyright` (pre-commit): clean.
- `tests/ut/ir/` + `tests/ut/jit/`: 4935 passed, 1 skipped (rebuilt `pypto_core`).
- `test_compiled_program.py`, `test_distributed_compiled_program.py`, `test_run_script_writer.py`, `test_builder.py`: 149 passed.
- (3 unrelated `test_run_config.py` dfx tests fail locally on a stale `simpler` package — `ImportError: Tensor from simpler.task_interface` — an environment issue independent of this change.)

author: jv-k
body:
## Summary

`do-tag` hard-coded `git tag -a`, so provenance-conscious teams couldn't produce a signed release tag even though the 2.0 publish pipeline already does npm provenance + OIDC. This adds a `--sign` long-only boolean flag and a `TAG_SIGN` config/env key (R-CFG-3 precedence: CLI > env > `.ver-bumprc` > default `false`) that switch `do-tag` to `git tag -s`. Key and signing-program selection stay entirely in git's own config (`user.signingkey`, `gpg.format`) — ver-bump adds no key management and no gpg/ssh preflight; git's own error is the error surface.

Refs #68.

## R-SIGN coverage

| ID | Requirement | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R-SIGN-1 | `--sign` / `TAG_SIGN=true` → `git tag -s` instead of `-a`; default unchanged; precedence per R-CFG-3 | `lib/args.sh`, `lib/config.sh`, `lib/git-actions.sh` |
| R-SIGN-2 | Signing failure follows the existing tag-failure abort path with git's output surfaced | `do-tag` (existing `fail 1` path, now flag-aware) |
| R-SIGN-3 | `--dry-run` prints the `git tag -s …` would-run line (prefix parity with the `-a` preview) | `do-tag` dry-run branch |
| R-SIGN-4 | Composes with `-m`/`--message` — custom message signs the same as the default | `do-tag` (`tag_msg` untouched) |

Parity: `--sign` added to `--help` (row + synopsis), all three completion emitters (bash/zsh/fish), the README options block, and the `.ver-bumprc` key table (`TAG_SIGN`, default `false`). New `docs/features/signed-tags/requirements.md` + index row.

## Test plan

**Before:** `git tag -a` was the only tag form — no way to sign; 347 tests.

**After:** 358/358 pass (`pnpm tests:run`), `pnpm lint` zero warnings. New `test/signed-tags.bats` (9 cases):

- PATH-stubbed `git` capturing argv: `--sign` → `-s` present / `-a` absent; default unchanged (`-a` present, no `-s`)
- `--sign` composes with a custom `-m` message (R-SIGN-4)
- stubbed `git tag` failure under `--sign` → exit 1 via the existing failure path, git stderr surfaced (R-SIGN-2)
- `--dry-run --sign` prints the `git tag -s` preview and creates nothing (R-SIGN-3)
- precedence end-to-end via the dry-run preview: rc `TAG_SIGN=true` → signed; env `TAG_SIGN=false` beats rc `true`; CLI `--sign` beats env `false`
- real signing round-trip: throwaway ed25519 key + `gpg.format ssh` in a scratch repo → tag object contains `BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE` (skips where the environment can't sign)

Plus 2 parse cases in `args.bats` (`--sign` sets `TAG_SIGN`; `--sign=value` → exit 2), and the existing help↔README flag-parity test passes with the new flag.

author: nickraymond
body:
## Summary

Implements **Phase 3 (OpenMV N6)** — the Pi drives the N6 over USB using an allowlisted, newline-delimited JSON protocol (§8, no arbitrary remote execution), captures stills to the board's flash, and retrieves them length-framed over serial with SHA-256 verified end to end (§10, §19). The N6 is addressed by **USB serial number** (§12), never a fixed `/dev/ttyACM*`.

Also adds a **live focus stream** (requested for M12 lens adjustment): the board streams framed JPEG frames and `host_tools/focus_stream.py` serves them as browser MJPEG + a live sharpness readout over Tailscale.

## Hardware recon (nereus000 + N6, 2026-07-14) — resolves gating open questions

| OQ | Finding |
|----|---------|
| OQ-1 camera API | Legacy `sensor` API; sensor **PAG7936**; framesizes QVGA(320×200)/VGA(640×400)/**HD 1280×800 max** |
| OQ-2 USB transport | CDC serial, VID `0x37C5`, serial `005537493543`; enumerate by identity |
| OQ-3 file transfer | Capture to `/flash`, retrieve over serial; SHA-256 round-trips (no MSC mount) |
| OQ-5 firmware | MicroPython **1.26.0**, build `OPENMV_N6`, STM32N657X0 |

Note: the AE3 also enumerated (37c5:16e3, `OpenMV-AE3`, fw 1.25.0-preview) — Phase 4.

## What's here
- **Board (`openmv/`)**: `common/command_protocol.py` (shared codec, single source of truth), `common/device_info.py`, `common/capture_service.py` (capture + framed transfer + focus stream), `n6/{board_config,boot,main}.py`. Board-specific facts isolated in `board_config` — no `if board == ...` branching (§6).
- **Host**: `cameras/openmv_usb.OpenMvUsbCamera` (registered in `builtin`), `host_tools/{discover_openmv,deploy_openmv,focus_stream}.py`.

## Testing
- **Unit (Mac, no hardware)**: 120 pass — protocol codec + allowlist, adapter driven through a fake loopback board (capture→retrieve→checksum, mismatch detection, bad-command handling), discovery by serial, frame parsing.
- **Hardware (`./scripts/test_openmv_n6.sh`, on the Pi + N6)**: deploy → device info → **3 stills in a row with matching checksums** → reject `unknown_action` / `bad_json`. All green (4/4). Meets the Phase 3 exit criteria.
- **Focus stream**: live-validated — ~29 fps VGA / ~33 fps QVGA, 100 valid JPEG frames served with correct multipart framing, live sharpness + peak tracking, clean start/stop.

Two board bugs were caught on hardware and fixed: `Exception.__init__(self, …)` is unsupported on MicroPython (use `super().__init__`), and deploy now uses `python -m mpremote`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Tick Phase 3 boxes in `docs/SPEC_*.md` and mark OQ-1/2/3/5 resolved in `docs/open_questions.md` — held back to avoid conflicting with the parallel Phase 2 session editing those docs.
- `capture_video` to-file on the N6 (OQ-4) is still deferred; the adapter reports it as `not_supported`.
- AE3 (Phase 4) reuses `capture_service` with an `ae3/board_config`.

author: hdikeman
body:
Summary:

`NegatedBigintRange::mergeWith` computes `this->upper() + 1 < otherNegatedRange->lower()` to detect the disjoint case. When `this->upper() == INT64_MAX`, `+1` wraps to `INT64_MIN`, the comparison is spuriously true, and the merge takes the disjoint branch — emitting `col < smallLower OR col > bigUpper` instead of `col < smallLower`.

Example: merging `NOT BETWEEN -118 AND INT64_MAX` with `NOT BETWEEN 284 AND 479` produces `BigintMultiRange: [[INT64_MIN, -119], [480, INT64_MAX]]` instead of the correct `col < -118`.

Guard the disjoint-branch test with an explicit `this->upper() < INT64_MAX` check.

Reviewed By: Yuhta

author: buremba
body: ## Why The unknown-slug precheck on `entitySchema.createType` / `createRelType` is a `SELECT`, not a lock. Under multi-replica concurrency two callers can both pass the precheck and race the partial unique index — the loser then surfaces a **raw Postgres 23505** (`duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_entity_types_org_slug"`) instead of the coded `[entity_type_exists]` / `[relationship_type_exists]` 409 the sequential path emits. That breaks two things that depend on the *coded* duplicate signal: - `lobu apply`'s probe-create-then-update upsert (retries as `update` only on the coded 409). - The documented ensure-then-write flow in `search_sdk` (#1958), which catches the coded 409 to stay race-safe. Surfaced by the codex reviewer on #1958. ## What Wrap both INSERTs; translate the **constraint-specific** 23505 (via the existing `isUniqueViolation` helper) to the same coded `ToolUserError` (409) the precheck emits. Only that exact constraint is caught — any other unique violation still propagates. ## Tests (red→green) Added concurrent-create tests for both entity types and relationship types: fire 6 concurrent creates of one slug, assert exactly one wins and **every** loser gets the coded 409, never a raw 23505 / "duplicate key value". - **Red** (catch disabled): losers reject with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_entity_types_org_slug"` → test fails. - **Green** (fix in place): all 17 tests in the file pass. `make pre-pr` clean (typecheck + knip + biome). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01TvqppirynLxpoRU4ARjQv7 --- Need help on this PR? author: hdikeman
body:
Summary:

`tryMergeBigintRanges` takes N single-value `BigintRange` disjuncts and hands their `lower()` values to `common::createBigintValues`. When the disjuncts contain duplicates (e.g. `col = X OR col = X`), the `values` vector arrives at `createBigintValuesFilter` with duplicates. The `range + 1 == values.size()` contiguous-range short-circuit fails, control falls into the `BigintValuesUsingBitmask` branch, and `VELOX_CHECK_LT(min, max)` triggers because `min == max == X`.

Example crash: `col >= INT64_MAX OR col = INT64_MAX` — both disjuncts collapse to `BigintRange(INT64_MAX, INT64_MAX)`; the ctor blows up with `min: 9223372036854775807, max: 9223372036854775807`.

Sort + unique the `values` vector before the `createBigintValues` call so the distinct-values invariant that `createBigintValuesFilter` assumes is preserved.

Reviewed By: Yuhta

Differential Revision: D112010149

author: aaradhya-07
body:
## Overview

Every default `kubescape scan` invocation logs a spurious warning before completing:

[warning] failed to open file for writing, reason: open /dev/null.txt: operation not permitted

**Current behavior:** when `--format` is set without `--output`, `GetUIPrinter` silences the UI printer by pointing it at `os.DevNull`. `PrettyPrinter.SetWriter` then sees that `/dev/null` has no `.txt` extension and appends one, turning the path into `/dev/null.txt`. Creating a regular file there fails — `EACCES` on non-root Linux, `operation not permitted` on macOS devfs even as root — so the warning is emitted.

The warning is only the visible half of the problem. When the create fails, `printer.GetWriter` falls back to `os.Stdout`, so the pretty printer is not silenced at all: it writes to stdout, which is exactly what redirecting to `/dev/null` was meant to prevent. On `kubescape scan --format json`, the human-readable table can interleave with the JSON on stdout. Conversely, when the process *can* write to `/dev`, a stray `/dev/null.txt` regular file is created instead.

**Future behavior:** `PrettyPrinter.SetWriter` leaves `os.DevNull` untouched rather than appending an extension. `/dev/null` opens cleanly on both Linux and macOS, so the UI printer is genuinely silenced, no warning is logged, no file is created in `/dev`, and stdout carries only the requested format.

## Additional Information

The fix is a single condition in `PrettyPrinter.SetWriter` — the extension append is skipped for `os.DevNull`, and the rest of the path handling (trimming, the `report` default) is unchanged.

This follows existing intent in the codebase rather than introducing a new special case: `printer.LogOutputFile` already treats `os.DevNull` specially alongside stdout/stderr, so the literal path is expected to survive as far as the writer.

The `io.Discard` alternati considered and not taken:`PrettyPrinter.writer` is a concrete `*os.File`, so it would require changing the field type and rippling the for eliding a handful ofwrites the kernel already discards.

Only `GetUIPrinter` passes `os.DevNull` to a printer, and it only ever constructs
a `PrettyPrinter`, so no oon is affected.

## How to Test

Reproduce on `master` (as on macOS):

```bash
kubescape scan --format json
```
Before this change, the run emits failed to open file for writing, reason: open
/dev/null.txt: ... and thetdout alongside the JSON.After it, the warning is gone and stdout contains only JSON.

Unit tests:

go test ./core/pkg/resultshandling/printer/...

TestSetWriter_Pretty was added following the table style of the neighbouring TestSetWriter_Junit / Test os.DevNull case and pinsthe existing extension-append, .txt passthrough, and empty-output behaviours so they don't regress.

## Related issues/PRs:

- Resolved #2500

- [x] I have commented on my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] If it is a core feature, I have added thorough tests.
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Contexto

Sequência da Onda 1 (PR #68). Enquanto a Onda 1 zerou as anomalias de **baixo risco**, esta Onda 2 ataca os itens **estruturais** do backlog (`docs/plano-melhorias.md` / `arquitetura.md §12` R1–R8), mantendo tudo verificável e **preservando o invariante central** (paper-trading-first, HITL fail-closed, auditável). As duas formas eram algebricamente idênticas (`(p·b−q)/b ≡ p−(1−p)/b`), então **o contrato da API não muda**. Plugar Kelly no sizing real (`SquadOrchestrator._position_quantity`) fica como cauda do R5 (muda o trading → validação própria).
- **R2 — colisões de nome resolvidas.** Duplicatas mortas renomeadas por propósito: `protocols.SquadOrchestrator`→`A2ASquad`, `adaptive_replanner.AdaptivePlanner`→`AdaptiveReplanner`, `continuous_evaluator.ContinuousEvaluator`→`AgentPerformanceEvaluator`, `intelligent_forgetting.MemoryStore`→`RelevanceMemoryStore` (a de trading `SquadOrchestrator` em `orchestration/` permanece).

R1 (isolar cluster "BuildToValue"), cauda do R5 (Kelly no sizing real), R3 (política de risco/autonomia única), R6 (rotas de agentes), R8 completo, CandleOut `lo`→`l`.

body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The internal API key check used strict string equality (`===`), making it vulnerable to a timing attack where an attacker could theoretically guess the key by measuring the response time.
🎯 **Impact:** If exploited, an attacker could bypass authentication and perform restricted administrative actions on the application.
🔧 **Fix:** Replaced strict equality with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for validating the `INTERNAL_API_KEY`. The inputs are first verified as non-empty strings, converted to `Buffer` objects, checked for equal byte length, and then securely compared. Also added a `Sentinel` comment explaining the security concern.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by running `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:api` to ensure no regressions were introduced. Evaluated missing edge cases (e.g., missing env vars) to guarantee fail-safe behavior.

body:
## Scope

This pull request makes NomadPosting legally open source and adds the repository controls needed to accept contributions responsibly. It does not enable live posting or claim production readiness.

## Decisions

- License: GNU AGPL v3 or any later version (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`).
- Contributions: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1, contributor-retained copyright, no CLA.
- Governance: one active maintainer, documented bus-factor limitation, and independent qualified review required before any live security gate can close.

## What changed

- Rewrites the README around the verified dry-run boundary and contributor hardening tracks.
- Adds the canonical AGPL v3 `LICENSE`, DCO 1.1, contribution terms, governance, maintainer, conduct, and name/provenance policies.
- Adds `CODEOWNERS`, issue forms, and a stronger pull-request template.
- Separates vulnerability reporting from conduct reporting and documents authorized research boundaries.
- Adds adoption-aware DCO enforcement and adversarial self-tests to both pinned workflows.
- Keeps every live mode and production-readiness claim fail closed.

## Local verification

- Canonical AGPL and DCO texts verified after line-ending normalization.
- `scripts/check-dco-tests.sh`: signed author and co-author cases passed; unsigned author, unsigned co-author, unsigned post-adoption, and empty-range cases failed as required.
- Real range `aef6a31..543d916`: DCO adoption detected at `aecbbe9`; all three post-adoption commits passed.
- All relative Markdown links resolve across 16 repository files.
- All GitHub YAML parsed successfully after the workflow and issue-form changes.
- `go mod verify`, `go test -count=3 ./...`, and `go vet ./...` passed all 10 packages.
- `gofmt`, dependency-license policy, Linux amd64 CGO-disabled cross-builds, and high-signal literal-secret scan passed.
- `govulncheck v1.6.0` found no reachable symbol- or package-level vulnerability; the existing unreachable module advisory remains documented in `docs/VERIFICATION.md`.

## CI evidence

Current head: `543d916cf3593c5898a97cb7bc9b520b52613cb9`.

- DCO `signoff`: [passed](https://github.com/s00ly/nomadposting/actions/runs/29496931007).
- Pull-request `verify`: [passed](https://github.com/s00ly/nomadposting/actions/runs/29496931006).
- Push `verify`: [passed](https://github.com/s00ly/nomadposting/actions/runs/29496928573).

The prior head failed before assertions because the Windows-authored checker lacked an executable bit on Ubuntu. Commit `543d916` fixed the root cause by invoking the checker through Bash and recording both DCO scripts as executable; all replacement runs are green.

## Production boundary

This remains a dry-run research preview. Live release is still blocked on the reviewed Linux namespace/WireGuard/nftables/DNS executor and teardown; packet-capture no-fallback proofs across every fault phase; broker-backed pinned transports; concrete NIP-46 identity, permission, and Schnorr verification; OS-backed secret sealing; same-exit X reconciliation and length conformance; remaining metadata-index encryption; live relay review; provisioned and validated infrastructure; full accessibility and visual regression; canary evidence; and three clean production adversarial rounds.

author: rgbkrk
body:
One parser reads .ipynb content now: parse_notebook_jiter_for_notebook. Initial load, source reconciliation, the file watcher (process_watcher_event), the watcher-baseline refresh (refresh_primary_baseline_from_checkpoint), and the cfg(test) legacy loader all go through it. parse_cells_from_ipynb_for_notebook, parse_metadata_from_ipynb, and ParsedIpynbCells are deleted; metadata comes from the parse result's snapshot and raw value.

The watcher's diff shape is produced by streaming_cells_into_snapshots, which splits streaming cells into CellSnapshots plus an outputs-by-cell-id map that holds only non-empty entries, so map membership still means "has outputs".

Divergence mappings, per the characterization tests:

- Missing/invalid cells key, non-object root, invalid JSON: all Err. The watcher maps Err onto its existing warn-and-skip path (the route that already covered partial writes), so a malformed revision waits for the next event instead of degrading the room. Initial load keeps failing hard so the autosave zeroing guard preserves the on-disk file.
- Non-object cell entries: dropped, never synthesized. No caller consumed placeholder cells (the watcher diffs by cell id, the baseline refresh maps id to source), and enumeration runs over the raw array so surviving idless cells keep their index-derived ids.
- Non-i64 execution_count: "null". nbformat specifies int-or-null; the serde parser stringified out-of-spec numbers into NotebookDoc.
- Integers beyond i64 in outputs/metadata/attachments: converted to strings, preserving exact digits where the serde parser kept a lossy f64.
- Duplicate JSON keys: first-wins. JSON leaves resolution undefined; pathological input only.

The characterization tests are updated to pin the unified behavior and the chosen mappings (consolidation item 2 in docs/memos/room-lifecycle-simplification-and-verification.md).

author: petealbertson
body:
Closes #3

## Plan (progress checklist)

- [x] Redesign message bubbles to texting-app style: user messages right-aligned in a distinct bubble, assistant messages left-aligned, tool messages left and distinct. Role-based classes live on the re-rendered inner row + content column so Turbo Stream `update` broadcasts keep the layout stable. Preserves `prose`, `dark:` variants, avatars, Stimulus hooks, and the action row.
- [x] Add a regression assertion (`assert_select`) that locks in role-based alignment + bubble classes for user vs assistant.
- [x] `devloop test hostedgpt` equivalent — `bin/rails test` full suite green except 2 pre-existing errors unrelated to this change (present on `main`; `undefined method "each" for nil` in `_search_and_list.html.erb` on the create-error path); 24 skips.
- [x] **Follow-up feedback:** remove the AI/assistant bubble (revert assistant to original full-width no-bubble styling); make the user prompt bubble shrink-wrap its content (`w-fit max-w-[80%]`, no `flex-1`) so a short prompt like "yes" renders as a small bubble.

## What shipped

A texting-app style for chat messages, refined per review feedback:

- **User** messages: right-aligned (`flex-row-reverse`) in a rounded blue bubble (`bg-blue-500 dark:bg-blue-600`, white text) that **shrink-wraps to content** (`w-fit max-w-[80%]`) — a short "yes" renders as a small bubble, long messages wrap at 80%.
- **Assistant** messages: **no bubble** — original full-width styling (`flex-1 min-w-0 ml-3 mr-8 text-base text-gray-950 dark:text-gray-100`), left-aligned, avatar on the left.
- **Tool** messages: left-aligned, no bubble (same full-width styling as assistant).

**Streaming-safe:** role-based alignment + bubble classes live on the re-rendered inner flex row (`data-role="inner-message"`) and content column (`data-role="message-contents"`) — both rebuilt consistently on every token chunk by `GetNextAIMessageJob.broadcast_updated_message`. No role-based class depends solely on the persistent outer wrapper. `prose`, `dark:` variants, all Stimulus wiring, the action row, and tool-message `hidden` logic are all preserved.

## Review

4 parallel fresh reviewers (2 umans: correctness + security; 2 deepseek: quality + tests). Security, quality, and tests returned **clean — no blockers, no fix-now items**. The umans correctness reviewer hit a provider failure (model produced no output across multiple attempts); correctness-adjacent concerns were covered by the security and quality reviews. See the follow-up review-summary comment for details.

## How to smoke-test

1. Start the app, open a conversation.
2. Send a short message like "yes" — your message should appear on the **right** as a **small** blue bubble sized to the text, not a wide bar.
3. Send a long message / markdown — content wraps within `max-w-[80%]`.
4. The assistant's reply streams in on the **left** with **no bubble** (original styling).
5. Toggle dark mode — the user bubble keeps its blue background; the assistant stays bubble-free.
6. During streaming the layout should stay stable (no reflow/jump as tokens arrive).

## Out of scope (optional follow-ups noted by reviewers, not done)

- Add a tool-message assertion to the regression test.
- Assert dark-mode text classes (`text-gray-950`/`dark:text-gray-100`) on assistant message-contents.

author: stack-alerts
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is an open-source application for running and coordinating AI agents.
> - Long-running Paperclip servers emit diagnostic output to both stdout and a file transport.
> - The file transport previously kept a single `server.log` open indefinitely.
> - On a long-running instance, that file reached 22 GB before operator intervention.
> - External `logrotate` can mitigate the symptom, but the application owns the writer and should bound its own output.
> - This pull request adds size-based rotation with conservative, operator-configurable defaults.
> - The benefit is predictable disk usage without changing stdout logging or log formatting.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

No public GitHub issue was found for this problem.

**What happened**

With file logging enabled, the server wrote indefinitely to one `server.log`; an observed long-running instance produced a 22 GB file.

**Expected behavior**

Paperclip should rotate its own file logs at a bounded size and retain a bounded number of files.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run the Paperclip server with `logging.mode: file`.
2. Generate sustained server activity.
3. Observe that `server.log` grows without an application-level size or retention limit.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduced against the pre-change behavior on the current `master` lineage; this PR is based on `7f2ed0ad9`.

**Deployment mode**

Long-running local server using file logging.

A GitHub search for open issues and pull requests matching `server.log rotation` found no duplicate other than this PR. The roadmap contains no overlapping log-rotation item.

## What Changed

- Route the file transport through `pino-pretty` and `pino-roll` while leaving stdout unchanged.
- Default rotation to 200 MB per file with 10 retained files.
- Add `logging.maxSizeMb` and `logging.maxFiles` schema settings for operator overrides.
- Cover rotation defaults, overrides, transport wiring, and single config-file initialization in focused tests.
- Read the configuration file once during logger initialization.

## Verification

- `pnpm --dir server exec vitest run src/__tests__/logger-tz.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `pnpm --dir packages/shared exec vitest run src/config-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- The logger test verifies `pino-roll` receives `size: 200`, `limit.count: 10`, `mkdir: true`, and the `server.log` path.
- The schema test verifies defaults and operator-provided overrides.

## Risks

- Rotated logs consume up to roughly 2 GB with defaults; operators can lower both limits.
- `pino-roll` is a new runtime dependency, adding a small supply-chain and maintenance surface. Socket reports no vulnerability or supply-chain findings for version 4.0.0.
- File transport behavior changes, but stdout level, formatting, redaction, and timestamp handling remain unchanged.

> This is a targeted reliability fix. `ROADMAP.md` has no overlapping logging-rotation work.

## Model Used

- Follow-up diagnosis and CI corrections: MiniMax-M3 with tool use and local code execution.
- The initial implementation was produced by a prior Paperclip agent; its exact model identifier was not preserved in the exported issue run metadata.
