author: momochen1013
body:
## Summary

Fixes the broken hero + practices layout the user reported (plain-text 起源與異象, black wave in place of the amber decorative line, cards laid out horizontally instead of the merged vertical design), plus lands the three follow-ups from #36 on top of the current default branch (which supersedes #36).

## Root cause of the visible breakage

Cleanup commit `648e1d4` merged the `.section-dark blockquote` rule but dropped the closing `}` right before `.philosophy__inner`:

```css
.section-dark blockquote {
  font-size: clamp(22px, 2.6vw, 30px);
  color: var(--text-on-dark, #F5F1E8);
  letter-spacing: .03em;
  margin: 0 0 32px;
.philosophy__inner {          /*  ← should have been } on its own line first */
  ...
}
```

CSS parsers silently discard the malformed rule *and* every subsequent rule in the block, so every scoped rule in `about.html` after this point stopped applying — hero background image lost its filter chain, verse styling reverted to UA defaults, the practices vertical layout / glassy card recipe / semi-transparent white background were all inert, and `.practices-line-bg path { fill: none; stroke: var(--amber-500) }` was gone → the SVG path fell back to the UA default `fill: black`, which is the huge black wave shape in the reported screenshot.

Fix: add the missing `}`. Verified brace count is now balanced (82 / 82).

## Follow-ups landed alongside

1. **Practices scroll order** — card 3 still had `.scr-fade` on it, whose separate `once: true` ScrollTrigger snapped it to `opacity: 1, y: 0` when it hit 85% viewport, well before the pinned timeline reached card 2. Removed the class and rewrote the pinned tweens with `gsap.set()` + `fromTo(..., { immediateRender: false })` so each tween owns its "from" value and reversal during scrub is deterministic.

2. **Pin centering** — `.practices-stage` now has `min-height: 100vh` + flex-center, and the pin starts from `top top`. The stack lands vertically centred while pinned instead of clinging to the upper viewport.

3. **Amber unification** — stripped `.sage` / `.clay` / `.coral` modifiers from the two about feature labels (`COMPANIONSHIP · 同行`, `RELATIONSHIP · 關係`) and CTA links (`與我們聊聊`, `加入我們`) so they inherit the amber accent; moved `.newsletter-label` and `.newsletter-success` from `--sage-700` to `--amber-700` so the shared 代禱信 block matches the gold theme site-wide.

## Test plan

- [ ] `/about.html` hero shows the water hands background image + eyebrow + title again.
- [ ] Practices section renders three vertical cards with semi-transparent white glass + amber halo (no black wave shape).
- [ ] Scrolling into the pinned practices section reveals cards 1 → 2 → 3 in order; card 3 no longer appears before card 2.
- [ ] While pinned, the three-card stack sits vertically centred in the viewport.
- [ ] `COMPANIONSHIP · 同行`, `RELATIONSHIP · 關係` eyebrows + `與我們聊聊`, `加入我們` CTAs render amber.
- [ ] `STAY CONNECTED · 保持連結` label above `訂閱我們的代禱信` is amber on every page that mounts the newsletter partial.
- [ ] Reduced-motion still bypasses the pinned timeline and shows final states directly.

Note: this closes out #36 — #36 was stacked on the pre-cleanup branch so it can't cleanly merge anymore.

author: vilenarios
body:
## 🔴 CRITICAL — universal operator-attestation forgery via unconstrained RSA exponent

Found by the **post-PRD adversarial security pass** (red-team RT1), **before any npm/PyPI release**.

**The break:** the operator-address binding `operator = base64url(SHA-256(n))` commits to the RSA **modulus alone** and never covered the **exponent**, and neither kernel constrained it. With `e = 1`, RSA verification is the identity (`s¹ mod n = s`), so an attacker:
1. takes a **real operator's public modulus** (public — it's the `owner` of every tx they sign),
2. sets `e = 1` and builds a PSS "signature" equal to the encoded message — **no private key**,
3. and `npx @ar.io/proof verify` reported **`VERIFIED` / exit 0** on a fully fabricated attestation attributed to that real operator.

It was also a **cross-kernel divergence**: TS accepted, Python rejected only *incidentally* (pyca refuses `e < 3`).

**Reproduced against the shipped CLI** before the fix (VERIFIED/0); **after the fix it reads `failed`/exit 1 in both kernels.**

## Fix

Both kernels enforce `e == 65537` — the Arweave-wallet exponent the modulus-only binding assumes — in the RSA-PSS verify. A non-65537 exponent makes the signature invalid (a **failed attestation, exit 1**), identically in TS and Python.

- **`ts/src/crypto.ts`** — `RSA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT` guard in `verifyRsaPssSha256` (before import; `e=1` imports fine in WebCrypto and would otherwise "verify").
- **`src/ario_proof/rsa_pss.py`** — explicit `e == 65537` check (was a library artifact, not an intentional guard).
- **`specs/evidence-export.md` §3.3** — the exponent is now a hard, security-critical requirement: the modulus-only binding is sound *only because* `e` is fixed.

## Verified

- The exact forged export is pinned as a **regression fixture** (`ts/test/fixtures/…` + `test-vectors/evidence-export/negatives/…`); both kernels MUST verify it as `failed`.
- **TS 243 / Python 283 pass**; **cross-kernel gate `ALL MATCH` (14 cases)** — both kernels now reject the forgery *identically*, closing the divergence too.
- Legitimate exports (`e=65537`) still verify — no false rejection.

**This must merge before any `@ar.io/proof` release.**

author: databasecm
body:
Purchase order material sebagai **satu-satunya sumber** expense material. Kategori `material` sudah diblok dari entri manual (6-3), jadi PO adalah jalurnya.

## Skema (header + line items)
- `purchase_orders`: `po_number` (unik), `project_id` FK nullOnDelete, `supplier_id` FK nullOnDelete, `status` {draft, ordered, received, cancelled}, `total` decimal, `note`, `ordered_by`, `received_by`, `received_at`. **Auditable**.
- `po_items`: `material_id` FK nullOnDelete (jejak/referensi), `description`, `unit`, `quantity`, **`unit_price` = SNAPSHOT harga material saat PO dibuat** (PO tak bergerak walau harga material berubah), `subtotal`. BigDecimal.

## Kapan expense diposting: saat **RECEIVED** (bukan ordered)
- Barang di tangan = kas keluar terrealisasi; order bisa dibatalkan → belum ada expense. Konsisten prinsip "peristiwa nyata → transaksi".
- Saat terima: `transactions(type=expense, category=material, amount=PO.total, project_id=PO.project_id [6-3b], reference=po)`.
- **Idempoten + race-safe** (`lockForUpdate`): re-receive ditolak → satu expense, tak dobel.
- `draft→ordered→received` maju; `cancelled` hanya dari draft/ordered. **Received/cancelled = FINAL** (immutable — item tak bisa diubah).

## SoD & RBAC (sesuai keputusanmu: Manager draft+order)
- **Manager (bidang-scoped)**: buat + order PO untuk proyek bidangnya, boleh batalkan sebelum diterima — **TIDAK pernah menerima** (receive = titik kas, milik Finance). Mirror SoD payroll.
- **Finance + Owner/Direktur**: seluruh lifecycle termasuk **Terima** (posting expense).
- Manager bidang lain: tak lihat PO tsb. HR/Mandor/Mitra/Konsumen: nol akses. Ditegakkan di `PurchaseOrderPolicy` + query resource ter-scope bidang.

## Filament `PurchaseOrderResource`
- Buat PO dgn repeater item (pilih material → snapshot harga/satuan/nama; total dihitung ulang BigDecimal saat simpan). Aksi **Pesan / Terima / Batalkan** tergate policy; item read-only di halaman view.

## Cara tes
```bash
php artisan test tests/Feature/Finance/PurchaseOrderTest.php
php artisan test tests/Feature/Filament/PurchaseOrderResourceTest.php
php artisan test   # suite penuh
```
- `PurchaseOrderTest`: lifecycle → expense material tertaut `project_id`, amount = Σ subtotal (BigDecimal); **expense hanya saat received** (draft/ordered tak posting); idempoten re-receive; final immutable; **unit_price snapshot** (harga material naik setelah PO → PO & expense tak berubah); SoD/RBAC.
- `PurchaseOrderResourceTest`: create via panel menghitung total; visibilitas aksi SoD (Manager Pesan tampil, Terima tersembunyi; Finance Terima tampil); Finance terima → expense material terposting.
- Hasil: **504 passed (2160 assertions)**, Pint clean.

body:
## 做了什麼

評估把地圖改成 3D／地球儀 → 先做 **d3 vs three.js 兩個原型比較重量／觀感**，你選了 **d3（輕量）做正式功能、three.js 版封存供其他專案用**。本 PR 已完成整條路：比較 → 正式整合 → 封存。

## 正式功能：地圖新增「🌍 全球」地球儀 + 下鑽

在 dementia-exposome 的**同一個地圖區**：
- 國家選單新增第一項 **「🌍 全球總覽」並設為預設著陸視圖** —— d3-geo 正射投影 canvas 地球儀，拖曳旋轉＋緩慢自轉、hover tooltip、圖例、深色與雙語，全部**重用既有** `PM_BINS`／PAF bins／`RAMP`／`L()`／主題（與各國平面地圖同一套色階）。
- 全球視圖只放**可跨國比較**的兩個指標：**PM2.5**（各國近年全國值，175 國）與**可調控風險 PAF**（27 國）。**盛行率不放全球** —— 因各國年齡分母不同（65+／60+／50+）不宜跨國比較，改在下鑽後的各國 admin-1 地圖顯示（方法框已說明原因）。
- **下鑽**：在地球上**點國家**，或用選單切換 → 顯示該國既有的 admin-1 2D Leaflet 地圖（省／州／縣）；選「🌍 全球總覽」回到地球。切換沿用 `selectView()`，Leaflet 於首次下鑽才建立。
- 模式鈕依視圖啟用/停用（全球：PM2.5＋PAF；各國：盛行率＋PAF＋PM2.5＋單因子）。

**重量**：正式版只多載 d3-array+d3-geo ≈ **18 KB gzip** ＋ world-globe.geojson ≈ 39 KB gzip。

## 封存 three.js 版（不部署）

- 移到 **`prototypes/globe-3d-reference/`**：self-contained standalone HTML ＋ `globe.gl.min.js` ＋ `world-globe.geojson` ＋ README（如何 serve、如何複製到其他專案）。此資料夾在 `src/` 與 `public/` 之外，**Astro 不會 build／部署**（所以那顆 1.79 MB 的 globe.gl 不會上線）。
- 移除兩個比較用原型頁 `globe-lab-{d3,3d}.astro`；`d3-array`／`d3-geo` 保留（正式地圖使用）。

## 共用資料

`scripts/build_data.py` 的 `build_world_globe_geojson()`：Natural Earth admin-0（110m）× 全球 PM2.5（175/177 國）× 合成 PAF（27 國）→ `public/data/geo/world-globe.geojson`（124 KB）。已接進 `main()` 與 `manifest.json`。

## 驗證

- `npm run build` 通過（23 頁）。
- headless Chromium **15 項全 PASS**：預設地球儀著色（55 色）；模式閘控（全球停用盛行率）；PAF 切換；選單下鑽中國（31 省，盛行率重新啟用）；**點地球下鑽**（Canada）；回全球；深色重繪；語言切換；無 console 錯誤。截圖確認淺／深色地球儀與下鑽的中國省級地圖。

## 需要注意的地方

- 預設著陸改成地球儀（原本是台灣盛行率）。若你想維持台灣優先，一行可切回，跟我說即可。
- 地球儀為國家層級；之後可 fast-follow 疊上各國 admin-1（資料已在）。皆標註模型估計。

author: isaacrowntree
body:
Two gaps left from the sync repair.

## Identity guard

`/api/sync` and `/api/backup` are **both** routed by the server-side Access email, while the rows they carry belong to whichever avatar is selected on the device — and the switcher is one tap away.

- Finish a workout as someone else → their workouts land in **your** journal, permanently (append-only log).
- Back up as someone else → their whole database overwrites **your** `latest.json`.

This is live: two real users share the deployment. The two identities can't be reconciled client-side, so `mayWriteAs` refuses when they disagree.

An **unresolved** identity still allows writes — `/api/me` has a 2s timeout and falls back to a saved selection, so blocking there would strand devices that are almost certainly fine, and the server is the real authority regardless.

Note this is the *opposite* of the "normalize userId on apply" idea considered earlier, which would have merged the two users irreversibly.

## Sync status

Every failure path is a silent catch — offline, a 500, an expired Access session — because none of them should interrupt a workout. The cost: **a week of failed syncs looked exactly like success.**

- `flushOutbox` / `pullAndApply` now report whether they actually reached the journal.
- `syncEngine` records it; Settings shows it.
- It cannot read "Synced" while broken, and it keeps the last good time when a later attempt fails ("Not syncing … Last synced 7 days ago. 3 workouts waiting to upload.").

Verified against a production build: on localhost, where there's no Access session and `/api/sync` 401s, the row correctly reads **"Not syncing · Couldn't reach the sync journal."** Under the old code that state was indistinguishable from success.

## On state management

Deliberately **no state library**. IndexedDB is the source of truth and `useLiveQuery` already reads it reactively; a second in-memory copy would reintroduce exactly the two-stores-disagree bug this work exists to fix. Sync state is external mutable state — it changes from timers and page lifecycle, not rendering — so it's exposed as a subscribe/getSnapshot pair for React's `useSyncExternalStore`, with a referentially-stable snapshot (pinned by a test, since an unstable one spins React).

## Testing

Tests written first. **283 pass**, typecheck clean, lint errors 0 (warnings 7 → 6).

## Summary

- separate content-length selection from optional presentation duration
- ask only one outcome-changing question per round and skip known route, mode, audience, goal, length, action path, and hard-duration facts
- offer concise / standard / detailed when content length is missing, then estimate pages dynamically from actual material
- keep the six-question hard cap and stop immediately at design-ready state
- preserve the verified real action-path rules introduced in PR #3

## Root cause

The startup contract allowed route, use mode, and length to be bundled, but it did not explicitly distinguish the content-length choice from a presentation-duration constraint. In an idea-only live-presentation intake, the Agent could therefore treat duration as a missing startup requirement even when presentation mode was already known.

## User impact

For an idea-only request that already specifies live presentation mode, TaoHtml now asks for the missing content-length level instead of asking how long the talk is. If the user supplies a hard duration, TaoHtml uses it as a scope, pacing, and density constraint without re-confirming it. If no duration is supplied, intake continues without blocking.

body:
Clears the post-review backlog in three self-contained commits. All acceptance suites green (no-browser units, store/bridge/export/catalog/sdk-helpers, pool 13/13, **per-game 10/10**, p2p-acceptance/multiseat/reconnect ×3).

## 1. Issue #21 transport residuals (`c4e386e`)
Hardens `p2p/p2p-core.js` against the remaining unchecked multiplayer-protocol review findings:
- **Session-resume identity binding** — `generateId()` now draws 96 bits from `crypto.getRandomValues` (was 36-bit `Math.random`); the session stash records the remote DTLS fingerprint and `_sessionResumable` refuses resume on a positive fingerprint mismatch or past a 12 h TTL. Rejects only on evidence, so ephemeral-cert / pre-remote-description resumes still work.
- **ack/resync bounds** — `_clampSeq` validates + clamps peer-supplied `upTo`/`have` to `outSeq`. Also fixes a latent bug: `NaN` passed the old `typeof === 'number'` guard and `filter(e => e.seq > NaN)` silently **wiped the outbox**, defeating replay.
- **Relay fan-out amplification** — inbound app frames over `maxAppFrameBytes` (256 KB) are dropped before the host fans them to the other N-1 clients.
- **`noteRemotePeer` dunder guard** + **wake-probe identity guard** (`peers.get(id) === peerData`, not bare membership).

New `tools/p2p-core-unit.mjs` (27 no-browser checks) covers all of the above, wired into CI. The same-origin `BroadcastChannel` signaling relay is documented as an accepted boundary (games are opaque-origin since #50). Closes the last open items on #21.

## 2. T-4 concurrent-rendezvous scenario (`52dc17a`)
Adds scenario 13 to `p2p-reconnect-acceptance.mjs`: a hub with two spokes, both links cut at once, both repairing through the same rendezvous instance. Proves per-pair episode isolation and that the host re-holds **both** links. This was the last open item in the framework-review plan banner.

## 3. Issue #40 starter template (`7124dcf`)
- `tools/templates/starter-app/` — a minimal but complete Arcade app (SDK init + `ready`, namespaced `state`/`stats`, player name, settings-aware CSS, suspend/resume, `onStateReplaced`, scoped offline SW), root-relative `/arcade-sdk.js`, `{{APP_ID}}`/`{{APP_TITLE}}` placeholders.
- `./dev.sh new <app-id>` — scaffolds `../<app-id>` from the template and prints the catalog entry + next steps.
- A rendered fixture (`tools/fixtures/starter-app/`) now drives the **full per-game §13 `acceptance.mjs`** in CI — the step the pages.yml note deferred "until the starter-template fixture exists."

Running per-game acceptance (dormant in CI since opaque frames landed in #50) surfaced two fixes folded in here:
- `tools/acceptance.mjs`: `--serve` now sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (opaque frames load ES modules as `Origin: null` CORS requests — matches dev.sh/Pages); new `--mount <id>=<dir>`; check 6 drives the real bridge broadcast instead of an obsolete storage-event path.
- `index.html`: `currentSettings()` reads `fontScale` from storage (authoritative), like every other setting — so a font change in another launcher tab, or any direct write to the global key, propagates to mounted frames. `sw.js` CACHE_NAME v29 → v30.

## Also in this session (not in the diff)
Closed stale issues #1/#10/#27 as fixed/obsolete; pruned merged local branches; symlinked pi-game's stale vendored SDK to main.

author: znz
body:
これまで MDCompiler は、記述リストの説明(dd)の直後にカラム0で書かれたコードフェンスも dd に取り込んで描画していました。これは RD の `//emlist` が dd に取り込まれる挙動(rdcompiler.rb の `dd_with_p`)を踏襲したものですが、CommonMark には無い挙動で、GitHub などのプレビューではフェンスがリストの外に出てしまいます。

説明(dd)の一部として取り込むのは「項目の内容カラムにインデントされたフェンス」だけにし、カラム0のフェンスは dd の外(トップレベル)として扱うよう改めます。

- **mdcompiler.rb**: `dd_with_p` / `dd_without_p` からカラム0フェンスの取り込みを削除(インデントフェンスのみ `INDENTED_FENCE_RE` で取り込む)。
- **rrd_to_markdown.rb**: RD→MD 変換で、dd や `@param` 等の説明の中にある `//emlist`・`#@samplecode` を、項目の内容カラム(2スペース)にインデントしたフェンスとして出力します。**これまでカラム0で出力していたのが、doctree のソースにカラム0フェンスが残っていた原因**でした。前処理ディレクティブ(`#@since` 等)は Preprocessor がカラム0でしか認識しないため、そのまま残します。
- **markdown_to_rrd.rb**: 逆変換で、インデントされた dd/`@param` 内フェンスをカラム0の `//emlist{` / `#@samplecode` に戻します(ラウンドトリップ維持)。
- **MARKUP_SPEC §9.5**: カラム0フェンスがトップレベル扱いになることを明記。

## 互換性・マージ順

**doctree 側で該当フェンスをすべてインデント済み**([doctree #3105](https://github.com/rurema/doctree/pull/3105))のため、この変更後も生成される HTML は変わりません。doctree の `manual/` 全 1257 ファイル × サポート全バージョン(3.0〜4.1)で、この bitclust の変更前後の描画がバイト単位一致することを確認済みです。

**マージ順は doctree #3105 が本番反映されてから**にしてください。旧 doctree(カラム0フェンスが残った状態)にこの bitclust を当てると、フェンスがリストの外に描画されてしまいます。

全テスト(17619)green・`steep check` 型エラーなしです。

author: only-ouc
body:
## What changed

- Added a .NET 8 WPF widget that shows Codex rate-limit windows only while Codex is foreground.
- Added a compact 220×82 click-through overlay with outside-window docking, multi-monitor/DPI support, and a tray-controlled move mode with saved position.
- Added local Codex App Server integration through the official standalone CLI, plus an optional strict UI Automation fallback.
- Added tray refresh/startup/fallback controls, privacy boundaries, architecture docs, and semantic release metadata.
- Added 18 core tests and a local App Server integration test.

## Why

The Microsoft Store Codex package binary cannot be launched by an unpackaged desktop process. The monitor therefore discovers the official npm-installed Codex CLI and excludes protected WindowsApps binaries, while never reading authentication files or credentials.

## Validation

- `dotnet format CodexQuotaMonitor.sln --verify-no-changes --no-restore`
- `dotnet test CodexQuotaMonitor.sln --no-restore` (18 core tests plus integration harness)
- Real local App Server integration test with response values suppressed
- `dotnet build CodexQuotaMonitor.sln -c Release --no-restore` (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- Self-contained win-x64 smoke test: process responsive, 220×82 overlay, click-through enabled, percentage rendered, App Server source confirmed
- Staged secret scan: 0 credible matches

## User impact

Users install the official `@openai/codex` CLI once, unpack the portable release to a stable directory, and run the monitor. It auto-hides outside Codex and registers user-level startup only from a published location.

author: kiwoook
body:
# ✅ 체크리스트

- [x] merge 타겟 브랜치 잘 설정되었는지 확인하기 (dev)

# 🔥 연관 이슈

- close #1553

# 🚀 작업 내용

ADR-0020 Phase 2 — Boot 4.0.7 전환, Jackson 2 호환 모드 유지. 3개 커밋(`60456cb2`, `f09f0aaa`는 이전 작업, 이번 세션에서 `dfbae688`~`4ee06d9c` 추가)으로 구성된다.

**1. Boot 4.0.7 전환 코어**

- `spring-boot 3.5.3 → 4.0.7`, `springdoc 3.0.3`, `resilience4j spring-boot4` 모듈, `spring-dotenv → springboot4-dotenv` 아티팩트 교체
- `io.spring.dependency-management` 플러그인 제거 → Gradle 네이티브 `platform()` BOM(`spring-boot-dependencies`)으로 전환. CVE 오버라이드용 `extra["*.version"]` 프로퍼티는 Boot 4 BOM이 자체적으로 패치된 버전을 관리하므로 제거
- `:infra`의 OTel 개별 의존성(`micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel`, `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp`)을 `spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry` 스타터로 통합

**2. Jackson 2 호환 모드**

- `spring.jackson.use-jackson2-defaults=true` + `spring-boot-jackson2` 모듈을 실제 Jackson 2 API를 쓰는 모듈에 한정 추가(grep으로 확인한 모듈만, 전체 일괄 적용 아님). `:common`은 Spring-free 제약 때문에 raw `jackson-annotations`만 별도 버전 명시
- 이후 `admin`/`user`/`app`은 상류 모듈(`infra`/`websocket`)에서 전이적으로 이미 제공돼 중복이던 `jackson2` 선언을 제거(`f09f0aaa`)

**3. Boot 4 모듈러 재구성에 따른 패키지 이동 반영**

- `spring-boot-starter-aop → -aspectj`, `actuate.health → boot.health.contributor`, `autoconfigure.*` → 기술별 서브패키지(`jdbc`/`persistence`/`data.redis`/`hibernate` 등), 각종 `@AutoConfigureXxx` 테스트 애너테이션이 전용 `-test` 모듈로 분리(`webmvc-test`, `data-jpa-test`, `jdbc-test`, `resttestclient`, `micrometer-tracing-test` 등 필요한 모듈에만 추가)
- OAuth2 client(`:admin`, `:user`)에 `spring-boot-restclient` 추가 — Boot 4에서 RestClient 자동구성이 분리되며 `OAuth2Client`가 `RestClient.Builder`를 요구
- `NoResourceFoundException` 3-arg 생성자 대응, `DataRedisProperties` 이름 변경 대응

**4. WS 커맨드 봉투 Jackson 3 네이티브 회귀 수정 (이번 세션에서 발견·수정)**

- Boot 4의 STOMP 인바운드 컨버터는 커스텀 컨버터 미등록 시 기본으로 Jackson 3을 쓴다. `use-jackson2-defaults`는 자동 구성 `JsonMapper`의 기본값만 정렬할 뿐 컨버터 선택엔 영향이 없어, `MiniGameMessage.commandRequest`가 Jackson 2 `JsonNode`로 선언돼 있으면 모든 미니게임 WS 커맨드 역직렬화가 실패했다. `MiniGameMessage`/`CommandType`/`MiniGameWebSocketController`를 Jackson 3 네이티브 타입(`tools.jackson.databind`)으로 전환해 수정
- 참고: 최초 Phase 2 작업(`60456cb2`) 시점엔 이 실패가 "격리 실행 시 통과하는 기존 크로스테스트 플레이키"로 판단됐으나, 이번 세션에서 재현·A/B 비교(마이그레이션 직전 커밋과 worktree 비교) 결과 실제로는 이번 마이그레이션이 유발한 결정론적 회귀로 확인됐다
- `CardGameIntegrationTest.selectCard()`는 `test-support`의 테스트 STOMP 클라이언트가 별도로 Jackson 2 컨버터를 쓰는 것과 충돌하지 않도록 JSON 문자열 전송 경로로 변경

**5. REST 응답 직렬화 회귀 테스트 추가**

- ADR-0020 Phase 2 검증 항목(WebSocket·REST 직렬화가 Boot 3.5와 동일함을 보장) 중 REST 응답 쪽 커버리지가 비어 있어 `FriendRequestResponseSerializationTest` 추가. 마이그레이션 직전 커밋(976d76a8, Boot 3.5.3)에서 동일한 오토와이어드 `ObjectMapper`로 캡처한 JSON과 바이트 동일함을 검증

**6. 문서**

- ADR-0020: WS 커맨드 봉투가 Boot 4 STOMP 기본 동작 제약으로 Phase 2에서 Jackson 3 네이티브로 앞당겨 전환됐음을 기록(REST 응답은 기존 계획대로 Jackson 2 호환 유지, 와이어 포맷은 불변)
- ADR-0021: 트레이싱 검증 애너테이션의 Boot 4 리네임(`@AutoConfigureObservability` → `@AutoConfigureTracing`) 반영

# 💬 리뷰 중점사항

- **범위**: Phase 3(Jackson 3 전면 네이티브 전환, `@Retry` → 내장 `@Retryable` 교체)는 이 PR 범위 밖이며 별도 이슈로 진행 예정이다. 이번 PR에서 Jackson 3 네이티브로 전환한 건 WS 커맨드 봉투 하나뿐이고, 그 이유(Boot 4 STOMP 기본 동작 제약)는 ADR-0020에 기록했다.
- **회귀 정정**: `60456cb2`에서 "기존 플레이키"로 분류됐던 `CardGameIntegrationTest` 실패가 실제로는 이번 마이그레이션이 유발한 진짜 버그였다. 다른 미니게임 WS 커맨드도 동일 패턴으로 영향받았을 것으로 보이나, 현재 WS 커맨드 봉투(`MiniGameMessage`)를 쓰는 게임이 카드게임뿐이라 이번 회귀로 드러난 것은 하나다.
- **검증**: 전 모듈(`game`, `app`, `user`, `admin`, `infra`, `room`, `web`, `websocket`, `profanity`, `zzolbot`, `game-api`, `common`) 테스트 통과 확인. ArchUnit 5개 클래스 전부 통과.

author: 0xmaxma
body:
## Summary

The `gateway.bind` upgrade migration (Issue #204) broke in production across three releases while the unit suite stayed green. Root cause of the blind spot: `config-migrator.test.ts` builds a **hand-written mirror** of `config.template.json` (its own comment says *"Mirror the real config.template.json"*), so the tests never notice drift between the real shipped template and the migrator. v1.3.29 shipped a migration that reintroduced `127.0.0.1` on upgrade, and every unit test passed.

This PR adds a **real-artifact** upgrade test that drives the migration exactly like `src/index.ts main()` does on startup, bound to the actual files that ship to users.

## What's added

- **`tests/fixtures/configs/baseline-v1.3.25.json`** — a real `config.json` produced by the published **v1.3.25** package's own `create-agent` first-run logic (`configVersion: 1.0.11`, no `bind` key). This is what a real pre-localhost-default user's config looks like.
- **`tests/unit/config-migration-real-upgrade.test.ts`** — runs `detectMigration` + `applyMigration` against the **actual repo `config.template.json`** (not a stub) and asserts `gateway.bind` across every scenario:

| Case | Input | Expected |
|------|-------|----------|
| A | real v1.3.25 config → current | `bind: "0.0.0.0"` + warning |
| B | fresh install | `bind: "127.0.0.1"`, no migration |
| C | no `configVersion`, no bind | `bind: "0.0.0.0"` |
| D | already-migrated persisted bind | left untouched (needs manual fix) |
| E | explicit user bind on old config | preserved, never overwritten |

## Why it works where the old tests didn't

Because the test binds to the **real template**, a migrator ordering regression (`deepMerge` before `preserveBindDefault` — the exact v1.3.29 bug) turns scenarios A and C red. Verified by temporarily reverting the ordering: A and C fail with `127.0.0.1`; restoring the fix makes all 6 green.

This suite runs inside `test:unit`, which is the `release.yml` gate **before `npm publish`** — so a broken bind migration can no longer be released.

## Not covered by design

Configs already "poisoned" by a broken intermediate build (bind persisted + `configVersion` already at the template version) are intentionally **not** auto-repaired — the migrator must never override a `bind` the user may have set on purpose. Those need a one-line manual fix (set `bind` to `"0.0.0.0"`). Case D documents this.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- New + existing migrator suites: `config-migrator` + `config-migration-real-upgrade` = **64 tests green**
- Full `test:unit`: **105 of 106 suites pass**. The one failure is `watch-factory.test.ts` — a pre-existing timing flake unrelated to this change (file-watch debounce timing out under full-suite parallel load; it passes **7/7 in isolation**). This PR touches only test fixtures/specs for config migration.

> Note: `watch-factory.test.ts` flaking under load is a separate CI-reliability risk for `release.yml` and is worth a follow-up (raise the fake-timer/debounce tolerance or run it serially), but it is out of scope here.

author: marcelroozekrans
body:
## What

Splits PR #81's inline *"Compile the instrumented sources"* step out of `build-test` into its own **`android-build`** job, so the Android shell's compile is a distinctly-named required check — symmetric with the existing **`ios-build`**.

## Why

The M6 audit found that when the Android shell fails to compile, the failure surfaced only as a red `build-test` — the same check that reddens for a .NET build error, a .NET test failure, or a JVM unit-test failure. You could not tell from the check list which shell broke. iOS never had this problem: `ios-build` names itself. Now Android does too.

## Shape

- **`android-build`** (ubuntu-latest, `needs: build-test`): JDK 21 Temurin, downloads the `BlazorNative.Runtime-linux-bionic-x64` artifact `build-test` uploads, runs `gradlew --no-daemon compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin -PciSoDir=<artifact dir>` (mirrors the advisory emulator job's `.so`-consumption so `verifyNativeAssets`/`copyRuntimeSo` resolve without a NativeAOT publish tree). Fails loudly, citing the AGP 9 precedent.
- The inline step is **removed** from `build-test` (a duplicated gate is drift) with a breadcrumb comment left in its place.
- The bionic `.so` artifact uploads are **untouched** — the emulator lane and now `android-build` both depend on them.

## Not changed

- **No behaviour / no test-count change.** `compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` runs no tests. Counts stay 324 / 83 / 111 / 72.
- `android-instrumented.yml`'s emulator job and its 111-test assertion are untouched — device execution stays advisory.
- Branch protection is **not** touched (owner adds `android-build` once green).

The required-lane picture now reads cleanly: `build-test` (windows) · `android-build` (ubuntu) · `ios-build` (macos) — each native shell with a distinctly-named required compile gate.

### Generated by /code

**Agent:** Charlie Shin
**Prompt:** `meta-session: [meta-moderator session]
You are Charlie Shin, the Meta-Moderator — the cross-repo operator who watches the whole oodim portfolio the way a human SRE does. You are scoped to **phynars/oodim-game** for this session.

Your mandate is OPEN-ENDED. There is no checklist. Ask the operator's question: **what is wrong or stuck in this repo, and what should be done about it?**

Investigate FIRST with your read tools — form a ROOT-CAUSE hypothesis before acting:
- \`query_db\` — the live database (read-only). Useful: code_sessions (implement attempts, no-PR loops, costs), task_queue (backlog / stuck jobs), dimensions, agent_personas.
- \`list_issues\` / \`read_issue\` — the backlog; look for issues parked \`agent-needs-human\`, or ones a recently-merged fix may have unblocked.
- \`read_pr\` / \`get_check_results\` / \`diff_branch\` — open PRs: stranded/idle, mergeable-but-sitting, behind main, or red on an already-fixed problem.
- \`blame\` / \`file_history\` — trace how something came to be the way it is.

Look for (use judgment, NOT a fixed list): stranded or behind-main PRs; issues a shipped fix unblocked; backlog issues attempted repeatedly that never open a PR (a give-up loop); a product or capability that is incomplete; anything an attentive operator would notice is off.

**PARKED-PR TRIAGE (standing duty, 2026-07-07):** PRs labeled \`agent-needs-human\` are YOUR backlog, not a graveyard — left alone they pile up and demoralize the humans. Check each against CURRENT main and close its loop one of three ways:
1. **SUPERSEDED** — its content (or a better version) already merged: close the PR with a one-line provenance comment pointing at what replaced it. Never leave a merged idea's husk open.
2. **BLOCKER CLEARED** — the structural cause it exhausted on has since been fixed: prefer PORT-AND-CLOSE (re-ship the branch's still-valuable content as YOUR edits this session — a fresh CI-gated PR opens — then close the husk). Only un-park the original branch if it is CLEAN against main and you VERIFIED the original blocker is gone. Un-parking without fixing the blocker just re-exhausts the loop and doubles the waste (learned 2026-07-07: a well-meaning blind un-park burned a full iteration cycle twice).
3. **STILL BLOCKED** — leave the label, and name the unresolved root cause in your report so the humans know exactly what they own.

Then ACT:
- If the fix is CODE you can make now, MAKE THE EDITS (\`edit\` / \`write\`). Your staged changes are opened as a **CI-gated PR automatically** at the end of this session — editing IS shipping a PR. If an open issue already describes that work, just do it and write "Closes #N" in your final summary; do NOT also file a duplicate issue for work you're doing this session.
- If a problem needs something you CANNOT do — a deploy, a DB write, or work outside phynars/oodim-game — FILE a precise issue with \`create_issue\` (root cause + exact fix + files).

**ELEVATED hands are ON this session** — you can close the loop yourself:
- \`merge_pr(number)\` — merge a PR, but ONLY if its CI is green AND it has an approving review (the tool refuses red/pending/conflicting/unreviewed). You CANNOT self-merge your own unreviewed PR — green proves it compiles, not that it's right; let the reviewer pass it first. Use it to LAND a PR that's already green + approved (e.g. an approved one that's sitting unmerged).
- \`set_labels(number, add?, remove?)\` — manage labels; the key use is UN-PARKING: remove \`agent-needs-human\` once you've confirmed the blocker cleared. On a PR, ALSO add \`agent-retry-granted\` in the same call — iteration depth is durable, so without the grant the loop re-parks it instantly; the grant buys exactly one fresh round.
- \`close_issue(number, comment?)\` — close a done-but-open issue (deliverable already exists, duplicate, or stale), leaving a one-line reason.
- \`close_pr(number, comment)\` — close a PR WITHOUT merging (provenance comment REQUIRED). THE PORT-AND-CLOSE RULE: whenever you re-ship a blocked PR's content as your own edits, you MUST close the old husk with this in the SAME session — a port that strands its husk grows the parked pile (+1 per rescue; issue #622 accumulated four).
Use these surgically and only on confirmed state — a merge is revertable and a close is reopen-able, but don't act on a guess.

**Your COMPUTER is ON this session** — an isolated Linux container with a real shell and git (the box is yours alone). Use it for what the virtual repo tools CAN'T do — most of all, resolving a CONTENT conflict on a behind-main PR that the automatic rebase couldn't (the \`rebase-pr.yml\` workflow only auto-resolves lock files; real conflicts need your judgment):
- \`sandbox_git_checkout(branch)\` — clone phynars/oodim-game into the box on the PR's branch (the push credential is injected; you never supply a URL or token).
- \`sandbox_exec(command)\` — run shell: \`git merge origin/main\`, \`git status\`, run tests, then \`git add -A && git commit && git push\`.
- \`sandbox_read_file(path)\` / \`sandbox_write_file(path, content)\` — read a conflict-marked file, write the resolved version, then \`git add\` it.
Resolve conflicts by UNDERSTANDING both sides (union real content, keep the newer real change, drop placeholders) — never just delete markers. After a clean \`git push\`, the PR updates and CI re-runs; report what you resolved.

Constraints:

body:
## StockPilot 0.4 — Source-Grounded AI Research Assistant

### Scope
- Adds an optional, user-triggered AI Research Assistant to stock detail pages.
- Builds a deterministic Evidence Bundle from eligible SEC identity, company facts, annual trends, filing metadata, and system-derived FCF.
- Uses the OpenAI Responses API with Structured Outputs (responses.parse + zodTextFormat, store:false).
- Keeps AI server-only: no API key in browser bundles, no secrets in the repository, and no portfolio/checklist/journal/insights/watchlist data sent to the model.
- Keeps Draft status; this PR is not merged or deployed.

### Merge-blocker fixes
- Grounding is claim-local: each claim can use only values, years, periods, percentages, and accessions from its own cited sources.
- Enforces exact sourceIndex union, rejects unavailable facts, wrong metrics, wrong years, unsupported tickers, fake IDs/accessions/numbers, and prohibited ratings/position/price/return language.
- Supports monetary formats including $391B, billion dollars, comma-separated USD, Chinese 亿/万亿, negative and parenthesized values, plus percentage growth/decline forms.
- FCF provenance now resolves exact taxonomy/concept/unit/form/accession/period inputs and permits only Operating Cash Flow + Capital Expenditure; UI exposes System-derived, OCF source, and CapEx source links.
- OpenAI refusal and incomplete responses map to safe diagnostic codes without exposing refusal text or caching partial output.
- Rate limiting prefers cf-connecting-ip, then trusted x-forwarded-for, with a global fallback.
- Live smoke script reports model/status/latency/input-output-total tokens/source count/cache/grounding without logging prompts, evidence, responses, keys, or contact values.

### SEC live smoke
All five tickers passed with sourceMode=live and valid CIK/filing/source URL normalization. AMZN is partial only because Liabilities is explicitly unavailable; no zero substitution was made.

| ticker | submissions bytes | company facts bytes | unavailable metrics |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| AAPL | 164,394 | 3,748,682 | none |
| MSFT | 184,142 | 4,788,959 | none |
| NVDA | 160,426 | 4,039,082 | none |
| AMZN | 159,720 | 4,399,593 | Liabilities |
| TSLA | 161,953 | 3,587,168 | none |

Final SEC_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES is 8,000,000. The largest observed payload is 4,788,959 bytes, leaving 3,211,041 bytes of headroom. The streaming response-size guard remains enabled.

### OpenAI live validation (current run)
- Redacted local configuration check: OpenAI and SEC configuration are present; .env.local remains ignored and untracked. No secret values were logged.
- The bounded `pnpm test:ai-live` was attempted twice for AAPL and AMZN. Both attempts stopped at AAPL with the safe `AI provider unavailable` result before a successful structured response; AMZN was not reached after the early failure.
- No prompt, Evidence Bundle, response body, API key, or contact value was logged. The failure was not relabeled as mock or cached.
- The exact provider category remains unresolved because raw provider errors are intentionally redacted and no further paid retry was made.
- Result: **NOT READY FOR STOCKPILOT 0.4 REVIEW**. Keep this PR Draft; do not merge, deploy, tag, or start 0.5.

### Verification
- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ✅
- pnpm lint ✅
- pnpm typecheck ✅
- pnpm test ✅ (unit/integration tests + 3 rendered HTML tests)
- pnpm build ✅ (vinext chunk-size warning only)
- pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high ✅ (no known vulnerabilities)
- pnpm test:sec-live ✅ (five companies; bounded submissions/companyfacts requests)
- pnpm test:ai-live ❌ attempted with a configured local server-side key; AAPL stopped at safe provider-unavailable before AI success, so AMZN success, grounding, token usage, and cache validation are not claimed.
- Browser QA ✅ no-key fallback: Dashboard and all five stock routes responded 200; English/中文, light/dark, 390px layout, mobile Insights navigation, SEC FCF/source links, and console/page/network error checks passed. Live AI brief/citation rendering is not signed off.
- Secret scan ✅ no tracked .env.local, node_modules, .next, dist, or .wrangler; no key/contact-string matches outside ignored local env.

### Known limitations / remaining blocker
- A real server-side OPENAI_API_KEY is present locally, but the bounded request did not produce a successful AI response. The next diagnostic step must inspect the OpenAI project key, model access, billing/quota, and outbound network without exposing the key or raw response.
- Because live AI generation was not completed, this PR is **NOT READY FOR STOCKPILOT 0.4 REVIEW** yet. Keep this PR Draft. Do not merge, deploy, tag, or start 0.5.

author: operations-jacrentals
body:
**Draft — the live-deploy automation for the auto-fix engine. OFF until you flip the switch.**

Closes the last mile so an end-user's reported fix reaches app.jacrentals.com in real time, with no one touching the deploy machinery — but fully machine-gated, and nothing goes live until you enable it.

### What it does
- **`auto-promote.yml` (new):** when a Wrangler auto-fix PR (labelled `auto-promote`) squash-merges to `trunk`, it runs `tools/promote.mjs` to fast-forward `production` → live. **Only auto-fixes carry the label**, so your own merges to trunk still wait for your `/promote`.
- **`wrangler-fix.yml`:** the agent now also deploys the fix to staging (so staging stays in sync + the go-live step can verify) and labels the PR `auto-promote`. Stale "Pages deploys trunk = live" comments corrected.
- **`promote.mjs` / `deploy-staging.mjs`:** removed the stale "DRAFT — do not run" headers (both operational).

### Safety (fully machine-gated — no human review, but every gate must pass)
`smoke` + `logic-test` CI gate the merge → `promote.mjs` enforces staging-freshness + verifies the live `?v=` bytes after. Any red gate fails and the fix **stays at trunk, not live**.

### Your one-time switch-on (when you're ready)
1. Repo **secret** `STAGING_DEPLOY_PAT` (same one `/deploy` uses) — so the CI agent can publish to staging.
2. Confirm secrets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `WRANGLER_PAT` are set (already needed by the fix engine).
3. **The go-live switch:** Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → **Variables** → `WRANGLER_AUTO_PROMOTE = true`. Until this is `true`, merged fixes stop at trunk (not live).

### Please verify before flipping the switch
- **Pages source branch = `production`?** This whole thing assumes it. If Pages still serves `trunk`, merging is already live and none of this is needed — tell me and I'll adjust.
- **Not tested end-to-end** (needs a real test issue + live deploy). Recommend: with the switch **on**, file one throwaway `wrangler-fix` test issue and watch it flow report → fix → staging → merge → promote → live, before trusting it.

### Known limitation
Two auto-fixes merging within seconds of each other can make the staging-freshness gate fail-*safe* (the second waits at trunk rather than promoting a stale mismatch) — rare, and it never promotes bad bytes; you'd just `/promote` it by hand.

author: clyeh
body:
DR-002 additive contract bump **v1.1 → 1.2** (DESIGN §26 **DR-010**). **Contract + contract-tests only** — runtime lands in UXC1b. Source: the UX-redesign Phase C roadmap + the external functional review §P0#4 (define the metadata envelope *before* upload freezes, to avoid a second bump).

## Additions
1. **`POST /projects/{project}/builds/{build_id}/eval`** — async job (`202` + `JobAcceptedResponse`, SSE-watchable via `/jobs/{id}/events`), `Idempotency-Key` + `409`, **no request body** (build named in path, golden set = project config). Result lands where activation preflight reads §14 scores → Console gating with zero new coupling.
2. **`POST /projects/{project}/uploads`** — multipart into a server-managed corpus dir, registers/updates **one canonical `file://` source** (BA9 uri-normalization stays the SoR's). Client filenames are never used as paths. Honest per-file manifest (`accepted`/`rejected` + reason — no silent drop). Request-level refusals: `415` (non-multipart body) / `413` (over the size limit).
3. **Universal document-metadata envelope** `{schema_version, system, context, governance}` — `system` server-owned & **structurally not client-writable** (`DocumentMetadataInput` is `additionalProperties:false`, context/governance only); `context` **project-defined** (`projects.config.metadata_schema` — no global field enum, 不失一般性); `governance` exposure gated by a `projects.config.metadata_exposure` allowlist (never "present in JSONB ⇒ exposed").

## Design decisions (audited by the local code-reviewer)
- **413/415** carry no dedicated `ErrorCode` (the enum is frozen/additive-only); they surface as `VALIDATION_ERROR` via the existing coarse-4xx fallback — the same pattern as `405`. The `responses.Error` prose documents this (phrased to stay safe against the regex in `test_http_status_map_matches_the_contract_prose`).
- **`mcp_response.schema.json` untouched** (stays `schema_version` 1.0): `SourceRef.metadata` is already `additionalProperties:true`, so the envelope flows to agents without an MCP contract change. Only `openapi.yaml` changed → only it needed the version bump (governance-check confirmed).
- Downstream metadata stages (chunk-local, filterable indexing + search-by-metadata, embedding participation, auto-extract namespace, entity promotion) are explicit roadmap follow-ups, **not** this task.

## Tests
Frozen-path surface +2, `info.version` 1.2, write-endpoint count 10→12, plus 3 new contract tests encoding the *whys*: `system` immutability (rules 1/4), per-file manifest honesty, and the async/no-body eval shape. `schema.ts` regenerated (mechanical). `poe check-all` green (backend 1038 + frontend 360); 53 contract tests pass.

## Summary

This PR prevents sensitive request data from being stored in audit logs.

## Changes Made

- created a sanitized copy of the request body before logging
- redacted sensitive fields such as:
  - `password`
  - `oldPassword`
  - `newPassword`
  - `token`
  - `pendingToken`
  - `backupCode`
- preserved all non-sensitive request data

## Why This Change?

Previously, the audit middleware logged the entire request body without filtering.

This could expose credentials or authentication data in audit logs, increasing the risk of accidental disclosure.

This change masks sensitive fields before audit events are queued while preserving the rest of the request context.

## Benefits

- prevents sensitive credentials from being stored in audit logs
- improves application security
- follows secure logging best practices
- preserves useful audit information

## Testing

- ✅ verified passwords are redacted
- ✅ verified authentication tokens are redacted
- ✅ verified backup codes are redacted
- ✅ verified non-sensitive request fields remain unchanged
- ✅ confirmed audit events continue to be recorded successfully

Closes #293

author: foxmon
body:
The backend half of the notification pipeline (#50). A real HTTP shelter approval writes a transactional outbox row, and the gRPC relay contract that hobom-event-processor drives then drains it.

## What it proves
1. `POST /shelters` → `POST /approvals/:id/decision` (204) — the approval callback writes a `SHELTER_VERIFICATION_APPROVED` outbox row inside the `@Transactional` unit of work.
2. gRPC `FindOutboxByEventTypeAndStatusUseCase(SHELTER_VERIFICATION_APPROVED, PENDING)` returns it, correctly discriminated into `approval_approved` (approval_type `APPROVAL_TYPE_SHELTER_VERIFICATION`, `recipient_user_id` = approver).
3. gRPC `PatchOutboxMarkAsSentUseCase(eventId)` → row is SENT and no longer appears in a PENDING poll.

Boots the app with the gRPC microservice bound (vendored proto) and drives it with a real `@grpc/grpc-js` client — the same calls hobom-event-processor makes.

## Scope
The Kafka publish itself is the processor's responsibility (external), so it's out of scope for this repo's CI. This test locks the contract at the boundary this service owns.

## Verification
- `test:e2e` — 4 suites / 14 tests (new spec runs alongside the others under `--runInBand`, no port conflict)
- lint / typecheck pass

author: ellevas
body:
# Ghost Environments (ADR-0065) — Phase 6.4

Questa fase aggiunge la verticale **Dev/PR ghost environments**. Viene introdotto **1 nuovo scanner**, portando il numero di `ResourceKind` da 35 a 36.

## Nuovo Scanner Introdotto

* **`environment-ghost`** *(always-on)*
  * **Descrizione:** Raggruppa le risorse per ambiente (tag `Environment`/`env`/`branch`, con fallback su naming convention tipo `*-pr-*`/`*-preview-*`/`*-dev-*`/`*-feat-*`) e segnala i gruppi in cui **tutte** le risorse valutate risultano inattive da più di N giorni (default 7) — la firma tipica di un ambiente Dev/PR effimero mai smantellato.
  * **Copertura risorse:** vengono valutate solo le 4 tipologie per cui cloudrift ha già un segnale di stato/idle affidabile — istanze EC2, istanze RDS, funzioni Lambda, load balancer. Altre risorse taggate/nominate nello stesso gruppo (S3, DynamoDB, ...) restano fuori scope per questa iterazione (tradeoff documentato nei commenti dell'entity/scanner, sotto ADR-0065).
  * **Nota economica:** nessun costo AWS diretto associato al gruppo stesso — come `eni-orphaned`/`sqs-dlq-abandoned`, è un flag di igiene ($0), non un risparmio stimato. Scanner sempre attivo, nessun gate `--live-pricing`.
  * **Config:** nuovo blocco `environmentDetection` (`tagKeys`, `namingPatterns`, `inactivityDays`, default 7) in `cloudrift.config.ts`.

---

## Modifiche e Documentazione Incluse

### Architectural Decision Records (ADR)
Nessuna nuova ADR: il design (allowlist dei 4 resource type vs. mappa generica per-tipo, grace period senza singola "data di creazione" per un gruppo eterogeneo) è documentato inline nei commenti di `environment-ghost.entity.ts` e `aws-environment-ghost.scanner.ts`, sotto l'ombrello di ADR-0065.

### Configurazione e Pricing
* Aggiunto `environmentDetection` a `CloudriftConfig` (`tagKeys`, `namingPatterns`, `inactivityDays`) con validazione Zod.
* Nuova dipendenza `@aws-sdk/client-resource-groups-tagging-api` per il grouping via tag.
* Registrato `environment-ghost` in `scanner-registry.ts` come scanner always-on.
* Aggiunti i contract fixtures e la copertura *scanner-contract* per il nuovo scanner.

### Note di Architettura
Nessuna modifica a `AnalyzeCloudWasteUseCase`, alla struttura dei DTO o al meccanismo di dispatch del presenter. Il nuovo tipo di risorsa si inserisce direttamente nello `switch` esaustivo esistente e nel registro dichiarativo degli scanner (ADR-0043).

body:
## 概要

Addness子ゴール「ミーティング系エンドポイントをCLIに追加する」の実装です。

`docs/cli-endpoint-coverage.md`（ブランチ `docs/backend-endpoint-coverage`）記載の
ミーティング（Huddle / Meeting Bot / Meeting Note・Minutes）グループ全30本のうち、
CLIの一回性実行モデルに合う23本を `addness meeting huddle/bot/notes/minutes` サブ
コマンドとして実装しました。

### 追加サブコマンド・対応エンドポイント（23本）

**`addness meeting huddle`**（9本、`internal/huddle/handler/endpoints/*.go`）
- `status` — `GET /api/v2/objectives/:id/huddle`
- `active-subtree` — `GET /api/v2/objectives/:id/huddle/active-subtree`
- `session-status` — `GET /api/v2/objectives/:id/huddle/sessions/:sessionId`
- `recording-start` / `recording-stop` — `POST .../huddle/recording/{start,stop}`
- `inviteable-members` — `GET .../huddle/inviteable-members`
- `active` — `GET /api/v2/huddle/active`（204時はnull表示）
- `transcription-progress` — `GET /api/v2/huddle/transcription-progress`
- `invite` — `POST /api/v2/huddle/sessions/:sessionId/invitations`

**`addness meeting bot`**（4本、`internal/meetingbot/handler/*.go`）
- `list` / `get` / `create` / `delete` — `/api/v1/team/meeting-bot/jobs[/:id]`

**`addness meeting notes`**（5本、`presentation/handlers/meeting_note/*.go`）
- `transcribe`（ローカル音声ファイルをmultipartアップロード） / `summarize` /
  `post-minutes` / `suggest-goals` / `create-goals`

**`addness meeting minutes`**（5本、`presentation/handlers/meeting_note/*_minute.go`）
- `create` / `list` / `get` / `update` / `delete`

### 除外項目と理由（7本）

Huddleの以下はLiveKitへのリアルタイム接続が前提で、CLIの一回性実行モデルに
合わないため除外しました（`src/api/models/meeting.rs` 冒頭コメントに明記）:
- `join` / `leave` / `switch`（音声通話への参加・退出・切替）
- `token`（LiveKitトークン再発行）
- `heartbeat`（生存確認ping）
- `screen-share` acquire/release（画面共有の取得・解放）

webhook受信（`POST /api/v1/webhooks/livekit`, `/recall`）は元々スコープ外です。

### レスポンス仕様の実地確認

Go実装（`/tmp/vtb-main`）を確認したところ、Huddle系は共通ヘルパー経由で
`{"data": ...}` ラップ、Meeting Note/Minutes系は `RespondWithJSON`（生JSON、
ラップなし）と、グループごとにレスポンス形式が異なっていたため、それぞれ正しく
実装しています。

### 本番APIスモークテスト（読み取り系）

認証済み本番環境に対して以下を実行し、正常応答を確認しました:
- `meeting bot list` / `meeting bot get`
- `meeting minutes list`（`--source-type`フィルタ含む） / `meeting minutes get`
- `meeting huddle status` / `active-subtree` / `active` / `transcription-progress`
- `meeting huddle inviteable-members`（ページング・ソート含む）

実地確認により、`Minute.sourceType` に未文書化の `"bot"` 値が存在すること、
`HuddleInviteableMember.avatar` が文字列でなくオブジェクトであることが判明し、
それぞれ型定義を修正済みです。書き込み系（bot create/delete、minutes
create/update/delete、notes transcribe等）は本番データ保護のため実行していません。

### ベースブランチについて

作業指示では `origin/feat/cli-execution-calendar` にスタックする予定でしたが、
着手時点で同ブランチの内容はPR #155として既に `main` にマージ済み（直前に
マージされたばかり）だったため、`main` を直接ベースにしています。

## 品質チェック

- `cargo build` / `cargo test`（674 passed） グリーン
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` グリーン（追加ファイルはwarningゼロ）
- `cargo fmt -- --check` グリーン

author: nikcoder25
body:
Three related Fix Engine UX improvements on this branch.

---

## 1. Target the exact keyword across all on-page SEO areas

**`KEYWORD_PLAN_SYSTEM` prompt** — previously asked only for the keyword *(exact **or** variant)* in the title and section heading. Now it requires the **exact keyword (verbatim, same word order)** in: `<title>`, H1, section H2, opening answer-capsule sentence, meta description, URL slug, and ≥1 image alt. A light variant is allowed only in supporting body copy; anti-stuffing guard kept.

**Search volume** — detection already gates on `MIN_VOLUME` (≥100/mo) + `MAX_COMPETITION`; the prompt now states this explicitly so the model never optimises for a dead phrase.

**Reviewable output** — the keyword draft now carries `suggestedH1` / `suggestedMetaDescription` / `suggestedSlug`, and the preview lists the exact keyword plus each on-page target.

---

## 2. Edit / regenerate a shipped title or meta fix

A shipped fix only offered Re-check / Undo / View on site. You can now **Edit** or **Regenerate (with guidance)** from a shipped/verified card.

- Gated to **overwrite-style modules** (title/meta — those with a `revert()`); append modules would duplicate on re-ship, so they must be Undone first.
- **Non-destructive**: revising re-opens the fix to review; the live page keeps its shipped copy until the new draft is approved and re-shipped.
- On any failure (credits, generation error) a live fix is restored to exactly its shipped status — never flipped to detected/failed.

---

## 3. Archive tab — keep the main list a to-do

Published fixes (shipped/verified) used to stay in the default **ALL** list even though they're done and live, cluttering the queue.

- **ALL is now a true to-do**: shows only detect / review / approve / attention. It hides ignored (as before) **and** published fixes; the ALL count drops the archived ones too.
- Published fixes move to a dedicated **ARCHIVE** tab (the old "LIVE" tab, renamed and reordered after the actionable tabs) — still fully re-checkable and undoable.
- When the to-do list is clear but the Archive has entries, the empty state becomes an **"all caught up"** message linking to the Archive.

---

## Testing

- `vitest run src/lib/__tests__/` → **465 passed** (added: on-page keyword target fields + preview line; revise-a-live-fix — re-open with fresh draft, failed/payment-failure keeps it live).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `src`.

## Notes

Builds on the merged #700 (branch restarted from `main`). Change 3 is purely list filtering/labelling — no change to how fixes are generated, shipped, or edited.

author: sahilsaini5
body:
## Summary

`ToolContextCredentialStore` (used by `OPENAPIToolset` tools to cache an exchanged auth credential) cast `context.state` to a plain object and used bracket access:

```ts
const state = (this.context as unknown as {state: Record<string, unknown>}).state;
state[key] = credential;   // store
const serialized = state[key]; // load
```

But `context.state` is a `State` instance that keeps its data in a **private** value/delta store, reachable only via `get()` / `set()`. As a result:

- **`storeCredential`** set an *own property* on the `State` object. It was never recorded in the state delta, so it was never committed to the session.
- **`getCredential`** read that own property, never the value/delta store.

Because a fresh `Context`/`State` is created for every tool call (`functions.ts`), the stored own-property was discarded before the next call. So an `OpenAPIToolset` tool secured with **OAuth2 or a service account re-ran the token exchange on every single invocation**, and the exchanged credential was never persisted — the cache was effectively dead.

This is a mis-port: in adk-python, `tool_context.state[key] = ...` records a delta and persists.

## Fix

Use the `State` API — `context.state.get()` / `context.state.set()` — so the exchanged credential is recorded in the delta, persisted to the session, and read back on subsequent calls.

## Why the tests didn't catch it

The existing tests passed a plain `{state: {}}` object instead of a real `State`, so bracket access "worked" and the tests were green while real usage was broken. This PR updates them to use a real `State`, and adds coverage that:

- the stored credential is recorded in the delta (`State.hasDelta()`), and
- a credential persisted by one tool call is reused by the next — the second call's `State` is rebuilt from `State.toRecord()` (mirroring the per-call `State` reconstruction), and no re-exchange is triggered.

I verified all three credential-cache tests **fail** against the old bracket-access implementation and **pass** with the fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `core/test/tools/openapi_tool/tool_auth_handler_test.ts` updated + extended (6 tests).
- [x] Confirmed the new tests fail without the fix, pass with it.
- [x] Full core unit suite green (`npx vitest run --project unit:core`): 2082 passing.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, and Prettier all clean.

author: yuhao-su
body:
I hereby agree to the terms of the [RisingWave Labs, Inc. Contributor License Agreement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/risingwavelabs/risingwave/17af8a747593ebdbfa826691daf75bdab7d14fa0/.github/contributor-license-agreement.txt). ## What's changed and what's your intention? The `kill_cn_and_wait_recover` / `kill_cn_and_meta_and_wait_recover` / `kill_random_and_wait_recover` helpers in the simulation integration tests only sleep a fixed 10 s after killing nodes. Under some madsim schedules recovery takes longer than that, and the next batch statement fails with: ``` Scheduler error: Streaming vnode mapping not found for fragment 2 ``` (observed in `recovery::batch_refresh::test_batch_refresh_periodic_update`). Evidence that this is a pre-existing, schedule-dependent flake: the outcome is deterministic per binary+seed — it fails at seed 3 on PR #26277's binary (Buildkite build 98233) and at seed 47 on unmodified main (`2bdeee0adb`), and each binary passes the other's seed. The error signature is already in the sim framework's own retry allowlist (`src/tests/simulation/src/slt.rs`) and matches closed flaky issue #23393 — the SLT path retries it, but raw `session.run()` calls in integration tests do not. Fix: after the existing sleep, poll `Cluster::wait_for_recovery()` (`rw_recovery_status() == 'RUNNING'`, 200 s cap) — the same pattern the log_store recovery tests already use. Helper signatures change `&Cluster` → `&mut Cluster`; all call sites updated (`backfill_tests.rs`, `recovery/background_ddl.rs`, `recovery/batch_refresh.rs`). Validation (deterministic simulation, provenance-verified builds): - On `2bdeee0adb`: seed 47 fails before this change, passes after. - On this branch (rebased on latest main): seeds 1-10, 3, and 47 all pass. ## Checklist - [ ] I have written necessary rustdoc comments. - [x] I have added necessary unit tests and integration tests. - [ ] I have added test labels as necessary. - [ ] I have added fuzzing tests or opened an issue to track them. - [ ] My PR contains breaking changes. - [ ] My PR changes performance-critical code, so I will run (micro) benchmarks and present the results. - [ ] I have checked the [Release Timeline](https://github.com/risingwavelabs/rw-commits-history/blob/main/release_timeline.md) and [Currently Supported Versions](https://docs.risingwave.com/changelog/release-support-policy#support-end-dates-for-recent-releases) to determine which release branches I need to cherry-pick this PR into. ## Documentation - [ ] My PR needs documentation updates.

body:
## Summary

Ports the shift-left SPIR-V functional tests into the public `rocm-tests` framework. Each test builds a public HIP sample for `amdgcnspirv`, verifies the binary carries an `amdgcnspirv` offload bundle (`llvm-objdump --offloading`), then runs it.

- **`hip_basic_spirv`** (`tests/e2e/compiler/`) — clones public `ROCm/rocm-examples` at `amd-mainline`, builds the representative single-GPU `HIP-Basic` samples with `amdgcnspirv`.
- **`hip_samples_spirv`** (`tests/e2e/hip_runtime/`) — **reuses the exact `_SAMPLES` list from the existing `test_hip_samples.py`** (same `ROCm/hip-tests` `samples/` sources); the only differences are the SPIR-V build fixture (`-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=amdgcnspirv`) and the added offload-bundle assertion. This keeps the SPIR-V suite in lock-step with the regular sample suite (no duplicated list to maintain).

### Design / alignment
- The single-GPU representative lists mirror `test_hip_samples.py`'s convention: special-case samples (multi-GPU setup, extra toolchains, arch-gated, custom parsers) are kept out of the representative set.
- **Multi-GPU** samples are covered by dedicated `@pytest.mark.hw.multi_gpu` + `@pytest.mark.gpu_count(2)` tests (`peer2peer`, `multi_gpu_data_transfer`). The framework **auto-skips** these where fewer than 2 GPUs are available and runs them across the allocated GPUs otherwise — no false failures on single-GPU runners.
- Marker taxonomy (`hw.gpu` / `hw.multi_gpu`, `runtime.*`) is applied per the existing profiles.

### Coverage
| Suite | Single-GPU | Multi-GPU | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hip_basic_spirv` | 14 | 1 (`multi_gpu_data_transfer`) | `ROCm/rocm-examples` HIP-Basic |
| `hip_samples_spirv` | 9 (shared with `test_hip_samples`) | 1 (`peer2peer`) | `ROCm/hip-tests` samples |

### Deferred to follow-up (intentionally not included)

**`hip_basic_spirv` (`ROCm/rocm-examples` HIP-Basic)**
| Reason | Samples |
|---|---|
| Arch-gated / runtime SPIR-V gap | `cooperative_groups` (SIGABRT), `texture_management` (texture unsupported on gfx942) |
| No device SPIR-V bundle (host-only / module-load / hiprtc) | `bandwidth`, `device_query`, `module_api`, `runtime_compilation` |
| Not SPIR-V by nature | `vulkan_interop`, `vulkan_interop_mipmap`, `opengl_interop`, `hipify`, `hello_world_cuda`, `static_device_library`, `static_host_library`, `assembly_to_executable`, `llvm_ir_to_executable` |

**`hip_samples_spirv` (`ROCm/hip-tests` `samples/`)**
| Reason | Samples |
|---|---|
| Arch-gated / runtime SPIR-V gap | `2_Cookbook/14_gpu_arch` (gfx908-gated), `1_Utils/hipDispatchLatency` (exit 1) |
| No device SPIR-V bundle | `1_Utils/hipInfo` |
| Build-special (need extra build steps) | `0_Intro/module_api`, `0_Intro/module_api_global`, `0_Intro/generic_target` |
| Not SPIR-V by nature | `2_Cookbook/16_assembly_to_executable`, `2_Cookbook/17_llvm_ir_to_executable`, `2_Cookbook/11_texture_driver`, CMake demos (`12/18/19/21/22/23_cmake_*`) |

> Note: `module_api` appears in both — under `hip_basic` it builds but emits no `amdgcnspirv` bundle (loads a separate code object); under `hip_samples` (`0_Intro/module_api`) it fails to build (target mismatch). Same concept, different upstream repos / failure modes.

### Review
- Addressed: `assert_spirv_offload_bundle` now `pytest.fail()`s (was `pytest.skip()`) when `llvm-objdump` cannot be located, so an incomplete ROCm install fails loudly.

## Test plan

Validated on **MI325X (gfx942)** against a ROCm 7.14 install:

- [x] `pytest tests/e2e/compiler/test_hip_basic_spirv.py tests/e2e/hip_runtime/test_hip_samples_spirv.py --rock-dir <rocm> --gpu-arch gfx942 -q`

- [x] Multi-GPU tests auto-skip cleanly on single-GPU allocation
- [x] `--collect-only -q --no-gpu`

author: abimaelmartell
body: ## Summary Follow-up to cubic's review finding on #157 (`detect_stacked_box_table` is unreachable for 3-5-rect clusters — the main loop requires ≥6-rect clusters on a ≥6-rect page). **The finding is factually correct, and this PR resolves it by documenting the gate as deliberate rather than removing it.** Routing smaller clusters through the detector was fully implemented and measured first: - opendataloader-bench: **0.0000 movement** on every metric — no corpus doc needs the small-cluster path (the #157 target doc's cluster has 75 rects). - pdf-evals: **four real-document regressions** across three guard-tuning iterations — striped bullet lists became tables (Russian grading norms), wrapped regulation text became tables (td9264), a stats-table column got ripped out (dergi), a label column got separated from a hospital equipment table (HTM 02-01). Each guard fix for one doc broke another: with only 3-5 boxes the anti-prose/anti-grid guards have too little signal to discriminate. So this PR ships the honest version: a NOTE at the call site explaining the precision gate and the measurements behind it, plus `stacked_box_three_rows_below_cluster_minimum` — an end-to-end test through `detect_tables_from_rects` that pins the 3-box stack as intentionally below the detection floor and marks the entry point if it's ever revisited. Verified: full test suite passes, opendataloader-bench byte-identical to post-#157 main, pdf-evals snapshots byte-identical to main. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Documented the stacked-box detector’s 6-rect precision gate so 3–5 box stacks stay below the detection floor, and clarified same-baseline handling in the run-counting comment. Updated the end-to-end test (`stacked_box_three_rows_below_cluster_minimum`) to push the page past the 6-rect page gate and explicitly pin the cluster-minimum behavior. Written for commit 270ff509d56ba7e8d8fbbbe246c634e7ff6fb20d. Summary will update on new commits.

author: jaro-c
body:
**CI has not run in this repo since 2026-07-02.** Every run is a `startup_failure`.

`ci.yml` has passed `test-command` and `apt-packages` since then, while pinned to `.github` **v1.7.0**, which doesn't define those inputs. A reusable rejects an undefined input at *startup* — so the workflow never begins, and the failure looks like infrastructure noise rather than a broken gate.

The consequence isn't cosmetic: **#35 — the PR that added the new Ed25519 release key to the keyring — merged with its own tests never executing.** That's the key deciding what this archive admits.

The pin's own comment said to bump it before merging; v1.8.0 didn't exist yet, so it went in with the note, and the note is all that stayed. Those inputs shipped in **v1.8.0** on 2026-07-15.

Pins to **v1.9.1** — `shell-ci` is byte-identical between v1.8.0 and v1.9.1 (verified; v1.9.0/v1.9.1 only touched `rust-ci`), so taking the latest costs nothing.

This restores `tests/verify-debs.test.sh`: valid admitted, missing/invalid/wrong-key/unreadable-control rejected, rotation-overlap admitted, reserved keyring name rejected. **This PR's own CI run is the proof** — if it starts and goes green, the lane is alive again.

author: tdabasinskas
body:
### PR Category

Performance

### Summary

The PR gate compiles the code twice. The ASan build produces the debian packages, and a separate manylinux job compiles again to produce a wheel. In the PR gate that wheel is only used by the docs build, which installs it so it can import ttnn to check op docs and run Sphinx. That second compile costs about 12 minutes of runner time on every PR gate and merge queue run, and it is not used for anything else.

This drops the wheel job from the PR gate. The ASan build now uploads a small extra artifact with the compiled build/lib shared objects and the runtime tree, and the docs build imports ttnn from it through setup.py's existing `TT_FROM_PRECOMPILED_DIR` path.

The result is about 12 minutes of runner CPU saved per run. Time to green stays about the same and is often a little better, because the wheel job ran inside the ASan build and every downstream job waited for the whole thing to finish. The only new cost on the critical path is roughly 32 seconds to strip and upload the new artifact, and that is usually cancelled out by no longer waiting on the wheel.

### Notes for reviewers

- `docs-latest-public.yaml` now accepts either input, so the other two callers are unchanged. The docs wrapper and the release pipeline still pass wheel-artifact-name and install a real wheel. Only the PR gate passes `ttnn-import-artifact-id` and imports in place. Each install step is gated on the input it uses.
- The docs build imports the ASan instrumented libraries, so shared object dependencies like `libtt_metal` and `libtracy` resolve at import through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, which already points at `/work/build/lib`. We ship all of build/lib instead of a hand picked subset so nothing needs to stay in sync, and strip the libraries with strip `--strip-unneeded` before upload, which keeps the dynamic symbols needed to import.
- One thing worth a look is compression. Level 1 on the new artifact adds about 8 seconds to the upload, which sits on the critical path, and in return cuts the artifact from 824 MB to 263 MB (the wheel it replaces was 587 MB). The faster download happens in the docs build, which is not the long pole, so that part does not help time to green.
- Validated on [workflow_dispatch](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/29331682591) and [PR](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/29398425139) runs: the wheel job is skipped, the docs build passes with both the undocumented ops check and Sphinx importing ttnn, and smoke and examples stay green.

author: niro-demos[bot]
body:
## Summary

Browser redirects built by web handlers could use the request's `Host` header as their origin. Initialize the shared request context with the configured canonical Site URL so magic-link and other browser redirects cannot be redirected to an untrusted host.

## Consequence

When a deployment accepts an untrusted Host header, an attacker who can cause a visitor's magic-link request to carry that header can redirect the visitor to an attacker-controlled site, enabling phishing through the application's login flow.

## Reproduction

Actor: unauthenticated remote user able to supply an untrusted HTTP Host header (substitute your own equivalent).

1. Send the magic-link request with an untrusted host:

   ```sh
   curl -i -H 'Host: evil.example' \
     "$TARGET/login/one_time_link?t=invalid&redirect_to=%2Fchannels%2Fx"
   ```

   → Observed `302 Found` with `Location: http://evil.example/login?extra=login_error&message=Magic link is disabled`.

2. Repeat the same request:

   ```sh
   curl -i -H 'Host: evil.example' \
     "$TARGET/login/one_time_link?t=invalid&redirect_to=%2Fchannels%2Fx"
   ```

   → Observed the same attacker-controlled absolute redirect origin.

3. Control — send the request through the configured public host:

   ```sh
   curl -i -H 'Host: <configured-public-host>' \
     "$TARGET/login/one_time_link?t=invalid&redirect_to=%2Fchannels%2Fx"
   ```

   → The service remains healthy and returns the expected login-error redirect under the configured public origin.

Expected secure: reject the untrusted Host or return a `Location` under the configured public service origin.

## What changed

- Set the shared web request context's Site URL from `ServiceSettings.SiteURL` for all deployments.
- Stop constructing browser redirect origins from the request protocol and `Host` header.
- Preserve existing redirect consumers, including magic-link, OAuth, and SAML handlers, while giving them a trusted canonical origin.

## Regression test

`server/channels/web/magic_link_test.go` proves the configured-host control remains functional and asserts that an otherwise identical magic-link request with `Host: evil.example` still redirects under the configured Site URL.

## Validation

Before the fix, the configured-host control passed and the untrusted-host case failed at the redirect-origin invariant:

```text
--- FAIL: TestMagicLinkRedirectUsesConfiguredSiteURL (0.70s)
    --- FAIL: TestMagicLinkRedirectUsesConfiguredSiteURL/untrusted_request_host (0.00s)
        Error: Not equal:
            expected: "http://mattermost.example/login?extra=login_error&message=Magic link is disabled"
            actual  : "http://evil.example/login?extra=login_error&message=Magic link is disabled"
        Messages: browser redirects must not trust the request Host
FAIL github.com/mattermost/mattermost/server/v8/channels/web 1.209s
```

After the fix:

```text
ok github.com/mattermost/mattermost/server/v8/channels/web 1.213s
```

Command: `go test ./channels/web -run '^TestMagicLinkRedirectUsesConfiguredSiteURL$' -count=1`

## Full suite

The full `channels/web` package suite passes: `go test ./channels/web -count=1` (`29.688s`). The repository-wide suite was not run in this focused CI remediation.

## Residual risk

Deployments must configure `ServiceSettings.SiteURL` for absolute redirects; an empty Site URL now produces a same-origin relative redirect instead of trusting the request Host.

#### Release Note

```release-note
Used the configured Site URL instead of the request Host for browser redirect origins.
```

_Pentested and fixed by [Niro](https://github.com/apxlabs-ai/niro)_

author: weiso131
body:
While developing scx_teddy, we encountered a `shm_open` permission denied error.

The root cause was that the created shared memory object had permissions set to `0644`, preventing it from being opened by processes running under different users.

This change forces the shared memory object permissions to `0666`, ensuring it can be opened by both unprivileged users (the game) and root (scx_teddy).

author: saucetech
body:
## Summary

Fixes two related defects in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`'s ship/scout worktree resolution observed on 2026-07-14:

**Defect 1 — wrong worktree recorded.** When treehouse DID create an isolated slot, the spawn summary line and `state/<id>.meta` sometimes recorded `worktree=<project clone path>` instead of the real treehouse slot path, even though the pane's actual cwd was the slot. Root cause: the recorded value came from a raw pane-path poll captured mid-wait, not from `validate_spawn_worktree`'s own freshly re-resolved, canonicalized toplevel check that runs immediately after.

Fix: `validate_spawn_worktree` now exposes its verified canonical path via a new `VALIDATED_WT_REAL` global; the treehouse-get wait call site reassigns `WT=$VALIDATED_WT_REAL` after the assert passes, so the recorded value can never diverge from what was actually verified. Orca's own worktree-create API call site is intentionally excluded (it never polls a pane and already returns a canonical path from its own API), so its existing tests are unaffected.

**Defect 2 — pool exhaustion silently proceeds.** With the treehouse pool transiently exhausted, a spawn's pane could stay in the project clone (the fleet's mirror), and `fm-spawn` still launched the agent there and returned success — real agents made scratch commits into the mirror before being emergency-stopped.

Fix: the worktree-discovery wait now retries across bounded, overridable rounds (`FM_SPAWN_WT_WAIT_ROUNDS`/`_TRIES`/`_INTERVAL`, defaulting to the original 60x1s bound plus 2 more rounds), re-sending `treehouse get` each retry round, since the pool has been observed growing new slots asynchronously within minutes. Exhausting every round is a hard refusal — never a silent launch into the project clone. Any isolation-check refusal now also kills the already-launched backend window via `fm_backend_kill` before exiting non-zero, so a refusal never leaves an agent-less window stranded in the tangled directory.

## Changes

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` — the fix described above, plus review-round hardening (regex-validated `FM_SPAWN_WT_WAIT_INTERVAL` fallback, matching the codebase's other fractional-wait env vars)
- `tests/fm-backend.test.sh` — two new tests (stuck-pane refusal + window kill; late-settling-pane authoritative recording through a symlinked alias path) and an update to the existing symlink test to expect the new canonical recording
- `docs/configuration.md` — new env vars and behavior
- `docs/zellij-backend.md` — document-step fix dropping a now-stale "60s" figure
- `AGENTS.md` — section 7 update describing the new retry/kill/authoritative-recording behavior

Bash 3.2 (stock macOS) compatibility verified throughout (`/bin/bash -n`, and the full suite run under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57).

## Test plan

- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh` (pinned ShellCheck) clean
- [x] `bash -n` clean on both GNU bash and stock macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57
- [x] Full `tests/*.test.sh` suite passes, including the two new tests, under both bash versions
- [x] Confirmed via `git stash` clean-checkout comparison that the one pre-existing local test failure (`fm-turnend-guard.test.sh`'s Node `ExperimentalWarning` quirk) is unrelated to this change and predates it
- [ ] CI green on this PR

body:
## Summary

This PR delivers a single, evidence-based investigation document that explains — and demonstrates at runtime — how SFTPGo (v0.9.5-dev @ commit `44634210287c`) governs server-side execution of external utilities, validates and parses command input, and enforces directory restrictions and filesystem-trick protections relative to path transformation.

This is a **read-only investigative (Q&A) task**. The deliverable is a new markdown document — **not** a source-code change. Net change vs. the base commit is exactly one added file; zero source, manifest, build, or CI files were touched.

## Deliverable

- `blitzy/documentation/sftpgo_44634210287c.md` — 2,537 lines / 247,882 bytes, answering five objectives with complete unedited runtime evidence, exact `file:line` references, and cause→effect reasoning:
  - **Q1** — Security model for invoking external utilities (the `enabled_ssh_commands` allow-list; in-process handlers vs. `PATH` system commands).
  - **Q2** — Client-vs-server control boundary (startup `checkSSHCommands` + per-request membership gate).
  - **Q3** — Structured/unusual input handling (`parseCommandPayload` naive single-space split, no shell quoting).
  - **Q4** — Permission enforcement vs. path-transformation ordering (`ResolvePath` runs before `HasPerm`; proven with a discriminating test).
  - **Q5** — Filesystem-trick protections & coverage asymmetry (`isSubDir` containment, rsync `--safe-links`/`--munge-links` injection, git no-injection, reproduced TOCTOU + prefix-edge).

## Methodology & Compliance

- **Run-first, real entry point:** every behavioral claim is backed by output from the built binary launched via `sftpgo portable` and driven by real `ssh`/`scp`/`rsync`/`git` clients (46 client-command captures, 59 exit-code captures).
- **Read-only mandate honored:** `git status --porcelain` is empty; `git diff 44634210..HEAD` = one file added, 0 source files changed.
- **Evidence integrity:** 14 CR (`0x0d`) and 18 ESC (`0x1b`) bytes are deliberately preserved (SSH-CRLF stderr + zerolog ANSI) and are byte-identical across working tree, index, and committed HEAD.
- **Observed-vs-inferred discipline:** all non-reproduced, code-derived statements are explicitly labeled `(inferred)`.
- **Cleanup complete:** all temporary harness scripts, scratch server homes, and the throwaway binary were removed; no residual processes.

## Validation

Final Validator independently reproduced Q1–Q5 through the real entry point, confirmed the source compiles clean (`go build -mod=readonly ./...`, exit 0), fixed a single citation discrepancy (`vfs/osfs.go` line reference) using a byte-preserving edit, and verified byte fidelity.

## Findings surfaced (documented, not fixed — read-only)

The investigation reports real SFTPGo weaknesses that are **out of scope to remediate** here: CVE-2025-24366 (unvalidated rsync option passthrough), the `isSubDir` `HasPrefix` trailing-separator edge, the git-vs-rsync symlink-protection asymmetry, a non-atomic (TOCTOU) containment check, and system commands running with server-process privileges.

## Status

**94.9% complete** (74h autonomous / 78h total). Remaining 4h is human-only path-to-production: technical accuracy review (3h) and stakeholder acceptance (1h).

author: teta2k
body:
## Summary

- register request capture with `EventHandlerTaskAsyncHelper` and `AddOnBeginRequestAsync`
- await request-body capture directly instead of blocking on `Task.Run(...).Wait()`
- keep request context creation, body parsing, and stream rewinding in the ASP.NET request pipeline

## Why

The synchronous `BeginRequest` handler blocked the ASP.NET request thread while waiting for asynchronous request-body reads. Under IIS/System.Web, a JSON body read can require the request pipeline to make progress, producing a deadlock while the pipeline thread is blocked.

Using ASP.NET's asynchronous event registration lets the pipeline track and await request capture without synchronously blocking its request thread.

## Validation

- `dotnet cake build.cake --target=Test --framework=4.8 --configuration=Release --downloadRetries=3 --downloadRetryDelaySeconds=1` completed successfully (build and core test target)
- direct Visual Studio test execution discovered 24 .NET Framework tests: 22 passed; the same 2 ambient-context tests fail on unmodified `main`
- IIS/Compose JSON regression: the previously hanging POST completed in 0.634s and a follow-up GET succeeded
- request-context benchmark and slow-upload checks completed without a deadlock and preserved context propagation
