author: soundblaster
body:
## Motivation

ASP defines six independently claimable role profiles, but it did not yet provide an executable matrix that could test their highest-risk authority, replay, revocation, receipt, privacy, and mediation boundaries. Review item #60 therefore remained a proposal without machine-verifiable evidence.

## Goals

- Publish one versioned, dependency-closed conformance catalog for all six ASP v1 role profiles.
- Execute positive and negative vectors without exposing the assertion oracle to the stimulus adapter.
- Emit closed, reproducible, machine-readable reports bound to the exact RFC, catalog, subject, counterparts, runner, adapter, and probe.
- Run the suite in the repository quality gate and represent review item #60 as machine validated without claiming implementation or interop maturity.

## Changes

- Add a normative RFC section for the Interoperability Test Suite and the exact `agent-surface/0.1` protocol identifier.
- Add six profiles, 32 requirements, 47 vectors, 10 semantic baselines, 38 closed mutations, and six Draft 2020-12 wire schemas under `conformance/v1`.
- Add a strict I-JSON catalog validator, isolated adapter/probe runner, digest derivation, report verifier, feature inventory, counterpart topology checks, and derived verdicts.
- Add 22 Python regression tests that collectively execute all 47 vectors, including malformed output, timeout, oversized output, oracle separation, topology, applicability, and report-tampering cases.
- Add `conformance-check` to the Make quality gate used by GitHub Actions.
- Bind review item #60 to canonical RFC, schema, and registry evidence and advance it to `present / machine_validated`; regenerate the dashboard.

## Validation

- `make review-check`
- `make conformance-check`
- 22 conformance tests, collectively covering all 47 vectors
- 40 review-data tests
- 6 dashboard state tests
- 11 JSON files parsed successfully
- 74 RFC fenced JSON examples parsed successfully
- Python AST validation for 12 changed Python files
- Markdown hygiene check for changed Markdown files
- `git diff --check main...HEAD`

## Boundaries and Non-Goals

- A passing report is descriptive evidence for the exact pinned suite subset, not certification or complete role-profile conformance.
- Repository self-test subjects always produce `incomplete` and cannot be used as implementation evidence.
- Adapter and probe executables are trusted test components. The runner applies resource limits but does not sandbox filesystem or network access.
- This PR does not claim `implementation_tested` or `interop_tested` maturity and does not provide independent Mock App / Mock Runtime implementations.

## Notes

The history is split into three reviewable commits: normative suite/catalog, executable tests and CI, then dashboard maturity/evidence integration. The recommended follow-up is #58 Mock App / Mock Runtime so the suite can produce its first independent implementation reports.

## Summary
Implements the plan in `plans/recutils.md`, addressing #378.

- New reader/writer pair (`pkg/input/record_reader_rec.go`, `pkg/output/record_writer_rec.go`) for GNU recutils `.rec` format: blank-line-separated `Key: value` records, `+`-continuation and backslash-newline continuation, and generic comment handling. `%rec`-descriptor "schema" records are parsed like any other record — no special constraint/type-checking semantics, since Miller has no schema-enforcement concept.

body:
Two pieces of work, from the design handoff and the follow-up deploy request.

## Bound Codex redesign

Implements the handoff in `design_handoff_bound_codex`: the whole app becomes one bound book lying open on a desk. Parameters as ruled ledger lines on the left page, the generated menu as a rubricated manuscript page on the right. EB Garamond plus IM Fell English replace the mono family.

- All changes confined to `index.html` plus two small `ui.js` adjustments (incipit and versal capitals in `renderMenu`, lock buttons appended into authored `.register-line` rows). Element ids, rendered class names, theme mechanism, and the generator contract are unchanged; `src/generator.js`, `src/llm.js`, and `data/` untouched.
- Three responsive modes on the same two page elements: desktop spread, mobile portrait (one page at a time behind book tabs plus a fixed Generate bar), mobile landscape (full spread, pages scroll internally, sticky action dock).
- New behavior JS lives in one delimited block in `index.html`.

Verified with Playwright across all three modes and both themes: generation, locks surviving Randomize, seed determinism, theme persistence, tab switching, and the mobile action bar all pass.

## Auto-deploy with branch previews

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` rebuilds a generated `gh-pages` branch on every push and branch deletion:

- Trunk (the repo default branch) at the site root, every other branch at `/previews/BRANCH-NAME/`, generated index at `/previews/`.
- Composition happens in `scripts/build-preview-site.mjs` (read-only, `git archive` based, locally dry-runnable).
- Pushes to a branch with an open PR get a sticky preview-link comment, updated in place per deploy.
- Docs updated: CLAUDE.md deployment section, SETUP.md walkthrough and troubleshooting (including the ~10 minute Pages cache), README layout.

Already running: three green deploys so far. **One manual step remains:** Settings, then Pages, then "Deploy from a branch" with branch `gh-pages`, folder `/ (root)`. Until then the live site keeps serving `main` as before.

author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your script_lung_cancer_analysis.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your project, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today.

The bundle points the analysis at the `data/lung_cancer.csv` already in your repo (the NCCTG cohort), so the `PROC PRINT` / `PROC CONTENTS` QC pass, the `PROC LIFETEST` Kaplan-Meier with `strata Sex` and `plots=survival`, and the `PROC PHREG` Cox model all run and return the survival estimates, the log-rank test, and the hazard ratio with its risk limits — the same workflow your README walks through.

One thing I appreciated reading through this: the censoring convention is handled cleanly end to end. Your `data_prep.R` does `status <- status - 1` precisely so that a `0` means censored, and the SAS side then reads `Status(0)` in both `time Time * Status(0)` and the Cox model. That R-to-SAS handoff is where survival analyses usually go quietly wrong, and yours lines up. The `class Sex (ref='1')` with `/rl` is the right call too — fixing Male as the reference is what makes the "reduction in risk for females" reading in your README the correct interpretation of the hazard ratio, rather than its inverse.

The `jenner-check/` directory is self-contained: a copy of your analysis adapted to load the repo's own CSV, the captured log and listing from a passing run, and a small runner. Nothing outside `jenner-check/` is touched, nothing executes on merge, and there are no workflow files or hooks.

```
jenner-check/
├── README.md
├── run_jenner.sh
└── t001_lung_cancer_survival/
    ├── script.sas
    ├── autoexec.sas
    ├── expected.json
    ├── meta.json
    └── expected/
        ├── log.txt
        └── output.txt
```

To try it, check out this branch and, from the repo root, run the bundle straight against the hosted API:

```bash
git checkout jenner-check/initial-bundles
cat jenner-check/t001_lung_cancer_survival/autoexec.sas \
    jenner-check/t001_lung_cancer_survival/script.sas \
  | curl -sS --data-binary @- https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

Or run `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all`, which re-runs the bundle and verifies each field pinned in its `expected.json`. It's free to try, no signup; full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

On what leaves your machine: the runner uploads only the SAS source text it runs — the two-line autoexec plus the script — to api.jenneranalytics.com, which runs it and returns the log and listing. It does not read or upload any data files, so anything sitting next to a script stays on your machine, and nothing is sent unless you run a command yourself. Only the code you run is transmitted, as when pasting a snippet into any hosted tool; since a script's own source is what's sent, you can always review it first.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — all fine, and no response is expected; we won't open further PRs in this repo. To opt out of any future contact, leave a comment containing `no-more-prs` or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

---

Lawrence W. Sinclair  
CEO / Jenner Analytics Ltd  
[linkedin.com/in/lwsinclair/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lwsinclair/)

author: benthingktangk
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two live production acceptance gaps found after Vercel Production env
vars were configured, without altering ANS calculations or existing report
behavior.

**1. Admin console still showed the retired Supabase magic-link "admin email" step.**
- `requireRole()` and `/api/admin/me` now authorize off the env-configured admin
  gateway (`ADMIN_GATEWAY_USERNAME` + `ADMIN_GATEWAY_PASSWORD_HASH` +
  `ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET`) via its signed, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite session
  cookie, resolving to `super_admin`. Supabase is only consulted when the
  gateway is unconfigured (local/dev). The gateway plumbing (`_adminGateway.ts`,
  `admin-gateway.ts`: scrypt hashing, HMAC session, constant-time compare, per-IP
  rate-limit/lockout) already exists in `main` — this wires it as the sole path.
- The client login is now a single username + password form. The old magic-link
  page is deleted (re-exports the credential page) and the "admin email" entry
  link is removed, so username/password is the only way in.
- Secrets (password, hash, session secret) never reach the client, logs, or
  error bodies. Verified: the production client bundle contains only the env-var
  *names* (in an operator "not configured" diagnostic), never their values.

**2. Ask Atom had Patient/Clinician text modes but no microphone or spoken reply.**
- Mic dictation for both roles via browser-native Web Speech STT: listening
  state, accessible labels/`aria-pressed`, and a graceful type-only fallback
  when recognition is unsupported. Mic audio is never sent to ElevenLabs.
- A VOICE-originated answer is spoken in the configured Atom voice; typed
  questions are not auto-spoken. Header mute toggle stops speech + suppresses
  auto-speak; per-message play/stop retained.
- `/api/tts` hardened: voice chosen server-side via `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` (the
  client can never pick it), per-IP rate limit, 15s upstream timeout, PHI
  redaction, and safe 502/500 → browser fallback. `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` stays
  server-side only (0 occurrences in the client bundle).

## Test plan

All commands run locally on this branch:

- [x] `npm run check` (tsc) — clean

- [x] `npm run build` — client + server build pass
- [x] Secret-leakage scan of `dist/public/assets/*.js`: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`,
      `xi-api-key` → 0; gateway env names appear only as operator help text,
      no secret values

**Requires in Vercel Production:** `ADMIN_GATEWAY_USERNAME`,
`ADMIN_GATEWAY_PASSWORD_HASH` (`scrypt$N$r$p$saltB64$hashB64`),
`ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and optionally
`ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` (see `docs/ADMIN_GATEWAY_SETUP.md` + `.env.example`).

author: daun-gatal
body:
## Summary

- add a provider-neutral structured-output policy with `auto`, `native`, `tool`, `json`, and `plain` modes
- negotiate bounded formatter strategies and fall back to schema-guided plain JSON only for compatibility or output-shape failures
- expose the optional per-model policy in Admin → AI Models → Runtime parameters
- share the run timeout across the agent and formatter calls, bound initial schema prompts, and cache successful strategies with expiry

## Root cause

The formatter forced function calling for every `ChatOpenAI` transport. That class is also used for LiteLLM and other OpenAI-compatible gateways, where the routed provider may reject the generated function schema with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The fallback then converted the provider failure into a generic internal error.

## Impact

Structured AI capabilities such as Scheduled Queries and Data Health now let the LangChain adapter select its supported mechanism first, with bounded compatibility fallbacks. Authentication, throttling, timeout, and provider 5xx failures stop immediately instead of triggering additional billed calls. Regular chat/invoke capabilities are unchanged, and engine-only settings are not forwarded to provider SDKs.

No database migration is required because the policy is stored in the existing model params JSON column. Existing models default to `auto`.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun test packages/server/src/services/ai/structuredOutput.test.ts packages/server/src/services/ai/engine.test.ts`

author: vchelaru
body:
## Summary
- Investigated a raylib desktop-touch bug (single tap doesn't reliably register as a click, double-tap does) down to root cause: raylib's default GLFW backend has no real touch input and falls back to mouse-emulation, which hits Windows' touch-to-mouse click-disambiguation delay. Silk.NET and MonoGame DesktopGL don't have this problem because they're SDL-backed.
- Decision: document the limitation rather than chase a fix (would require an SDL-backed raylib native build, or Gum-side raw Win32 pointer handling — both bigger undertakings than this warrants right now).
- Adds a runtime compatibility table to the Cursor docs (raylib: Partial, Silk.NET/MonoGame DesktopGL: Full), linking to raylib's own source comment acknowledging the GLFW gap.
- Bundled: a `gum-samples` skill note (shared screen files via `<Compile Include Link=`) and a `skills-writer` rewrite (damped-response split into coverage vs. prose-density axes) — pre-existing edits carried along per repo convention of bundling skill improvements with the PR that surfaced them.

Commenting the trigger phrase on a **merged** PR fails the reusable infer workflow at the `Checkout PR head branch` step: `gh pr checkout <N>` tries to fetch the PR's head branch, which is deleted after merge (`fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/...`), killing the job before the action runs. Seen in [this adl run](https://github.com/inference-gateway/adl/actions/runs/29427144666/job/87392372047).

This guards the checkout on PR state: only `gh pr checkout` when the PR is `OPEN`; otherwise stay on the default branch, which already contains the merged work — exactly the context needed for follow-up requests on a merged PR.

Fixes inference-gateway/infer-action#211

author: farnoux
body:
## Contexte — TET-6699

Objectif : **réduire la taille du bundle front**.

Jusqu'ici, `packages/ui/src/global.css` importait `remixicon/fonts/remixicon.css`, ce qui embarquait **l'intégralité** du set RemixIcon (~2800 icônes) quel que soit l'usage réel :

| Ressource livrée au navigateur | Taille |
|---|---|
| `remixicon.css` (toutes les classes d'icônes) | ~148 Ko |
| `remixicon.woff2` (police complète) | ~176 Ko |

Or l'app n'utilise qu'~130 icônes distinctes.

## Approche

`@remixicon/react` expose chaque icône comme composant SVG (`<RiLeafLine />`) dont le tracé est inliné → **seules les icônes réellement importées sont incluses** dans le bundle. La police globale et son CSS disparaissent.

- **`Icon`** rend désormais le composant SVG passé en prop (taille appliquée via `cloneElement` sur les classes `h/w`) au lieu d'appliquer une classe de police `ri-*`.
- Tous les sites d'appel passent des composants `<RiXxx />` (au lieu de noms d'icônes en chaîne). Les maps/fonctions qui produisaient des noms (`niveauAccesToIcon`, `getFicheActionShareIcon`, `stateToIcon`, configs de nav en `.ts` via `createElement`, …) renvoient maintenant des `IconValue`.
- Suppression de l'import `remixicon/fonts/remixicon.css` et de la dépendance `remixicon` ; ajout de `@remixicon/react`.

Chaque nom d'icône a été résolu vers son export exact vérifié parmi les 3058 exports du paquet (gestion des cas particuliers `a-b`→`RiAB`, `24-hours`→`Ri24Hours`, etc.).

## Vérifications

- ✅ `nx run-many -t typecheck` (9 projets) — vert
- ✅ `nx lint` (app, ui, auth, site, panier) — 0 erreur
- ✅ `nx test app` (476) + tests `ui` (81) — verts
- ✅ `nx build app` — build de production réussi, plus aucune référence à la police remixicon

## Note de revue

Le diff est volumineux (~270 fichiers) car il touche chaque site d'appel d'icône, mais l'essentiel est **mécanique** (`icon="x"` → `icon={<RiX />}`). Les changements à regarder de près : `packages/ui/src/design-system/Icon/Icon.tsx`, les élargissements de types `icon?: string` → `IconValue`, et les fonctions/maps convertis.

## Mesures (build de production `apps/app`, `main` vs branche)

Même commandes de mesure sur les deux builds :

| Ressource (`.next/static`) | `main` | branche | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CSS — brut | 727,7 Ko | 605,8 Ko | **−121,9 Ko** |
| CSS — gzip (parsé à chaque page) | 123,4 Ko | 104,6 Ko | **−18,8 Ko** |
| Police woff/woff2 (téléchargée par le navigateur) | 1 315,0 Ko | 905,3 Ko | **−409,7 Ko** |
| Fichiers police remixicon (tous formats, dont `.svg`/`.ttf`/`.eot`) | 5 · 3 092,9 Ko | 0 | **−~3,1 Mo** |
| Total `static/` sur disque | 20 Mo | 16 Mo | **−~4 Mo** |

**Au premier chargement sur un navigateur moderne : ~195 Ko de moins téléchargés** = la woff2 des icônes (~176 Ko) éliminée + −18,8 Ko de CSS gzip (`remixicon.css`, ~2800 classes `ri-*`).

Coût : les ~130 icônes réellement utilisées sont désormais inlinées en SVG dans le JS (tree-shakées) — un ajout de l'ordre de quelques dizaines de Ko gzip, largement compensé.

_Note : le JS brut agrégé mesuré varie (`main` 14,65 Mo → branche 13,09 Mo) mais cette baisse relève du bruit de build (découpage de chunks non déterministe) — l'inlining SVG ne peut qu'ajouter du JS. Seuls les gains déterministes ci-dessus (CSS + polices) sont retenus._

author: ahmedsoliman
body:
Keep equality and IN predicates as exact ID selections in the DataFusion filter layer instead of collapsing large sets into scan ranges. This lets point-lookup tables preserve the user's requested IDs while range-scan tables can still convert the same selection back to bounds.

Teach the partitioned table provider to group exact point reads by Restate partition when the scanner can re-fetch the exact IDs itself. Use that for sys_invocation_status by adding an InvocationIdSet scan path backed by bounded RocksDB multi-get batches.

Split partition-store inclusive key-range scans into single-prefix and total-order variants, and use total-order scans when invocation-status, journal, or journal-events ID bounds span multiple partition keys. This preserves correctness for range-scan consumers of exact ID selections.

Adapt the worker cleaner to the fallible stream shape used by the new invocation-status scan path, and add scan-mode coverage for the new total-order range variant.


This design delivers 5-10x better performance for point-lookups than the concurrent iterator-per-entry approach that was previously used. This pays more dividends on slower disks and will allow us to leverage async I/O better when we build rocksdb with folly.

author: arthurwerle
body:
## Summary
This PR resolves a critical Docker networking issue where the staging MCP API service could collide with the production service on shared networks, causing Docker DNS to round-robin traffic between both environments and silently split requests.

## Key Changes
- **Service naming**: Renamed the staging service key from `mcp-api` to `mcp-api-staging` to create a unique DNS alias that won't collide with production
- **Network isolation**: Removed the `financer-transactions_transactions-network` external network dependency from the staging stack to prevent unintended network sharing with production
- **Configuration update**: Changed `TRANSACTION_SERVICE_URL` to use the staging-specific container name (`transaction-service-v2-staging`) instead of the generic service name (`transaction-service-v2`)
- **Documentation**: Added clarifying comments explaining the Docker DNS collision risk and why staging must use environment-specific identifiers

## Implementation Details
The root cause was that Docker registers service keys as DNS aliases on all attached networks. When both prod and staging stacks use the same service name (`mcp-api` or `transaction-service-v2`), Docker DNS resolves to both containers and round-robins between them if they're on a shared network. By using environment-specific identifiers (service key `mcp-api-staging` and container name `transaction-service-v2-staging`), we ensure staging traffic stays isolated to the staging environment.

author: bridgerz
body:
Reported by Stakin in the operator channel:

```
ERROR Failed to initialize BtcMonitor: JSON-RPC error: transport error: minreq: request url contains https:// but the https feature is not enabled
```

Any `https://` value in `bitcoin-rpc` failed at startup, which rules out hosted Bitcoin RPC providers (QuickNode and friends — which the runbook explicitly offers as an option) and TLS-terminated self-hosted nodes.

## Root cause

The transport chain is `corepc-client` → `jsonrpc` (`minreq_http` feature) → `minreq`, and no crate in the graph enables minreq's TLS feature, so minreq hard-errors on any https URL (`HttpsFeatureNotEnabled`).

## Fix

Direct workspace dependency on `minreq` with its rustls-based `https` feature — cargo feature unification enables it for the transitive copy `jsonrpc` uses. The dependency is otherwise unused (commented as such in both Cargo.tomls). Rustls-based rather than openssl, consistent with the rest of the stack.

## Verification

- `cargo tree -p minreq -e features` confirms `https`/`https-rustls` now active, driven by hashi
- Runtime-verified with a temporary test: an `https://` RPC URL now completes the TLS handshake and fails with an ordinary HTTP error instead of `HttpsFeatureNotEnabled` (test not committed — it needs network access)

## Also carried: ts-sdk.mdx refresh

This PR additionally carries the regenerated `design/docs/ts-sdk.mdx` (verbatim `fetch-sdk-readme.js` output) matching [hashi-ts-sdk#45](https://github.com/MystenLabs/hashi-ts-sdk/pull/45)'s style fixes — the docs CI job fetches the live upstream README, so every PR's `docs` check fails until this lands on main. Folded here instead of a separate PR (#826, closed) to land both in one merge.

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [c31de2e8-62ba-4c2c-b223-5c07ccdda9bd](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/c31de2e8-62ba-4c2c-b223-5c07ccdda9bd?fix-finding-id=AZ9mYNI7MtLwAQJIYX-2)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/c31de2e8-62ba-4c2c-b223-5c07ccdda9bd?fix-finding-id=AZ9mYNI7MtLwAQJIYX-2)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZ9mYNI7MtLwAQJIYX-2. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab3 View ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab3 View ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application passes user-controlled input into an operating system command without strict validation or safe argument handling. An attacker can abuse this flaw to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the application process. This can lead to data theft, service disruption, or full compromise of the host system. ## Changes Made The `cmd_lab3` view in `introduction/other_views.py` built `nslookup` and `dig` commands directly from the POSTed `domain` value and executed them through `subprocess.Popen`, which made the endpoint vulnerable to shell injection. The fix first normalized the input by defaulting a missing `domain` to an empty string and then rejected any value that did not match a strict hostname/FQDN allowlist with `re.fullmatch`, raising `ValueError` for invalid domains. It also changed the command construction from a single interpolated string to an argument list such as `['nslookup', domain]` or `['dig', domain]`, so the domain is passed as data instead of shell text. Finally, it removed `shell=True` from the `subprocess.Popen` call, preventing the shell from interpreting metacharacters embedded in user input. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation instructions: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input**: the fix adds a strict `re.fullmatch(...)` check for `domain` and rejects invalid input with `ValueError('invalid domain')`, which directly follows the guidance to validate user input before use. - **Do not construct the OS command from user-controlled data**: the command is now built as an argument list (`['nslookup', domain]` / `['dig', domain]`) instead of string interpolation, and `shell=True` was removed from `subprocess.Popen`, which aligns with the guidance to avoid shell-based command construction and reduces command injection risk. No specific library/framework was required by the guidance, so library usage is compliant by default. The code style remains consistent with the file’s existing Python/Django style. No new dependencies were introduced, so no manifest update was needed.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why These Changes are Necessary

Our development velocity was being bottlenecked by two distinct issues:
1. **Lack of Automated Testing & Static Verification**: Minor syntax, typing, and parsing errors were reaching production, resulting in UI crashes in our telemetry dashboards and incorrect nested structure tracking during analysis.
2. **Review Bottlenecks for Non-Core Changes**: A single-owner approval lock forced the sole human maintainer to manually review and merge every trivial asset change, utility tweak, and documentation update, stalling development.

This PR establishes a robust, automated quality gatekeeper system that guarantees zero runtime parsing/typing failures and enables safe, automated merging of non-core code paths—without sacrificing the integrity of core engine or cryptographic modules.

---

### Key Decisions & Technical Implementation

#### 1. Robust Telemetry and Parsing Fixes
* **Resolved Name-Resolution UI Crash**: Added the missing helper function `format_eta` to `rust-engine/run_gui.py` to fix runtime telemetry dashboard failures.
* **Stack-Based Brace Tracking**: Replaced a brittle regex-based tracker in `auditor.py` with a deterministic, stack-based parser to properly evaluate nested brace depth (`global_brace_depth`).
* **Dead Code Pruning**: Removed obsolete continuous coverage validation logic utilizing `explored_ranges` from `verify_cert.py`. Since the Rust engine transitioned to modern telemetry fields, this node was frequently empty, triggering unhandled runtime list parsing exceptions.

#### 2. Local & CI Tooling Alignment
* **Nix Dev Shell Provisioning**: Updated `flake.nix` (`devShells.default`) to automatically package `black`, `flake8`, and `mypy` natively. Developers no longer need to manually manage Python linters on their host machines.
* **Harmonized Quality Gates**: Integrated formatting, syntax, and type check targets inside the `Makefile` and mirrored them directly in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. A local `.flake8` configuration was created to align cosmetics (like maximum line length) with `black` formatting.

#### 3. Secure Self-Merging Pipeline
* **Auto-Merge Workflow (`.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`)**: Implemented a native GitHub workflow that automatically reviews, approves, and merges qualifying PRs once they pass CI.
* **Strict Security Guardrails**: Built-in directory exclusion logic ensures that self-merges **never** trigger if any modified files touch core engines (`rust-engine/`, `lean4-proofs/`) or cryptographic audit utilities (`verify_cert.py`, `cert_util.py`, `auditor.py`). These core files still strictly require manual owner approval.

---

### Change Summary

* **`rust-engine/run_gui.py`**: Added missing `format_eta` to fix UI crash during telemetry progress estimation.
* **`auditor.py`**: Replaced regex with stack-based logic to accurately track `global_brace_depth`.
* **`verify_cert.py`**: Cleaned up deprecated `explored_ranges` parsing routines to prevent crashes on empty ranges.
* **`flake.nix`**: Added `pkgs.python3Packages` dependencies (`black`, `flake8`, `mypy`) to the default development shell.
* **`Makefile`**: Added a `check` target executing formatting, linting, and type verification.
* **`.flake8`**: Added a linting configuration to prevent cosmetic conflicts with `black`.
* **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: Added automated syntax, formatting, and static typing validation steps.
* **`.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`**: Added a permission-safe workflow to auto-approve and merge non-core PRs.

## Summary

After unlocking the car, the lock entity showed **unknown/unavailable** instead of *unlocked*.

Root cause: the new `vehicle_status_updates` path (`vsu_helper.py`) maps `DOORLOCKSTATUSVEHICLE_UNLOCKED` to the integer `0` via `VSU_ENUM_VALUE_TO_INT`. The `is_locked` property in `lock.py` used a truthiness check (`if value and int(value) in (0, 3)`), so `0` was treated as missing data and the property returned `None`. The legacy VEP path delivered the string `"0"` (truthy), which is why this only surfaced with VSU messages.

## Changes

- `is_locked` now checks `value is None` explicitly instead of relying on truthiness
- Non-numeric values (e.g. `"error"`) return `None` instead of raising `ValueError`

- Logic table verified: `0`/`"0"` return unlocked, `1`/`2` locked, `3`/`"3"` unlocked, `None`/`"error"`/`4` return unknown

author: oten91
body:
## Summary

One branch closing a set of correctness/DoS findings from the codebase security audit, split into WebSocket hardening and general (non-WS) fixes. Every change is a guard that fires only on abusive/edge inputs or a latent-bug fix — normal relay and WebSocket traffic behaves identically (see **Behavior impact** below).

## WebSocket hardening
- **Setup-window race** — a frame arriving before `protocolCtx` was assigned (endpoint-speaks-first backends) tore the whole connection down (close 1011). Message processors now gate on a `ready` channel instead of rejecting a nil context.
- **Read size limit (H3)** — `ReadMessage()` had no `SetReadLimit`; a single oversized frame (from a client or a compromised endpoint) buffered whole → OOM. Capped at **15MB** on both connections (matches go-ethereum/bor `wsMessageSizeLimit`, so Polygon — the primary WS service — can't trip it).
- **Write deadline** — `WriteMessage` had no deadline; a stalled reader wedged the bridge's single goroutine indefinitely. Now bounded by `writeWaitDuration`.
- **Concurrent-connection cap (H4)** — nothing bounded live WS connections inside PATH. Added `WebsocketConnectionLimiter` (nil-safe, lock-free CAS), configurable via `max_concurrent_websocket_connections` (**default 10000**; negative disables).
- **Observation goroutines** — `BroadcastMessageObservations` spawned a goroutine per message (unbounded under a subscription firehose); now runs inline in the per-connection listener.

## General audit fixes
- **C1 — request body OOM** — `io.ReadAll(httpReq.Body)` was unbounded. Wrapped with `http.MaxBytesReader` at the router choke point; configurable `max_request_body_bytes` (**default 75MB**; negative disables).
- **C2 — batch goroutine bomb** — `handleBatchRelayRequest` spawned one goroutine per payload with the cap checked *inside* each. Now rejects oversized batches before the spawn loop and bounds concurrent payload goroutines with a semaphore.
- **C6 — pprof leaked onto metrics port** — the metrics server served `DefaultServeMux`, which `net/http/pprof`'s `init()` pollutes. Given it its own mux; pprof stays on its dedicated port.
- **C7 — unpinned CI action** — `rymndhng/release-on-push-action@master` pinned to an immutable SHA (v0.28.0).
- **H6 — sync-allowance underflow** — `perceivedBlock - syncAllowance` (uint64) underflowed to ~MaxUint64 when the allowance exceeded the height, rejecting *every* endpoint. Added `qos.MinAllowedBlockNumber` (saturating) across all five sites (evm×3, cosmos, noop).

## Observability
- **`path_request_body_size_bytes`** histogram — the existing counter only yields averages; this gives p99/max request-size visibility (closes an existing TODO). Bounded labels (reuses `rpc_type`/`service_id`), fixed buckets, one Observe on the per-request publish path.

## Behavior impact
Verified against production traffic (24h): average request body **~1.5KB**, largest per-service average ~9KB — so the 75MB body limit is ~50,000× the average, and the 15MB WS limit is above bor's own send limit. The only change that could reject *legitimate* traffic is the **10000 WS connection cap** — raise or disable it if a pod holds more than that concurrently.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean
- Unit tests green across gateway/config/router/metrics/qos/websockets (incl. new tests: WS read-limit teardown, connection limiter cap/CAS/concurrency, `MinAllowedBlockNumber` underflow)

## Out of scope (separate effort)
- C3/C4/C5 block-height poisoning (solana/cosmos/noop need EVM's median-anchored consensus ported — larger, riskier)
- H2 WebSocket `CheckOrigin` (low risk under PATH's header-auth model)

author: atd9876
body:
# Proposed Changes

Dell iDRAC returns @odata.etag on the UpdateService resource from schema version v1_15_0 onwards (confirmed on R770 v1_15_0 and R6715 v1_16_0). gofish's Entity.PostWithResponse automatically includes that ETag as an If-Match header on any POST. SimpleUpdate is an action endpoint, not a resource modification, so the BMC rejects If-Match with 412 Precondition Failed regardless of whether the ETag value is current.

- call DisableEtagMatch(true) on the UpdateService entity before calling PostWithResponse in the shared upgradeVersion helper. This applies to all vendors (Dell, HPE, Lenovo, local) since they all go through the same code path.
- add @odata.etag to the mock UpdateService fixture and enforce the correct 412 behaviour in handleSimpleUpdate so that the test suite would catch any future regression.


Fixes #1015

author: epic-serendipity
body: ## Summary Adds two quality-of-life features to the interactive scan experience: - **ASCII loading spinner** — while a scan operation's external command (Nmap, `dot`, `xsltproc`) is running, an ASCII spinner (`| / - \`) animates so it's clear that work is happening instead of the terminal just sitting silent. - **On-demand progress report** — pressing **space** during a running operation prints a brief, Nmap-style status line, e.g.: ``` -- progress -- Stats: 0:01:23 elapsed; 3/9 operations complete Current: Full TCP port scan - 0:00:45 elapsed [4/9] Remaining: UDP top 50, OS detection, Traceroute, Build host inventory, ... ``` Both features are automatic in an interactive terminal and are skipped entirely when output is redirected (pipes, log files, CI, tests). They can be toggled via the new `show_progress` setting (default on) in **Settings**. ## Implementation - **`pynmap/progress.py` (new)** — `ProgressMonitor` runs a daemon background thread that animates the spinner and reads single keypresses via `termios`/`tty` cbreak mode (with a Windows `msvcrt` fallback). It degrades to a no-op that still records state when stdout/stdin aren't TTYs, so the scriptable CLI and pytest are unaffected. A module-level "active monitor" lets the runner stay UI-agnostic. - **`runner.run_command`** — engages the active monitor around `proc.communicate()` and redirects the child's stdin to `DEVNULL` so it never competes with the monitor for terminal input. `sudo` still prompts via the controlling terminal, so privileged scans keep working. - **`engine.Observer`** — gains `run_started` / `run_finished` lifecycle hooks (no-ops by default), called by `run_operations`. - **`RichObserver`** — owns the monitor for the run, routes all console output through it (so messages never garble the live spinner line), and keeps the monitor quiet for privileged operations when passwordless sudo/root isn't available (so it doesn't fight sudo for the terminal). - **`config.Config`** — new `show_progress` field (default `True`) plus a Settings-menu toggle. ## Testing - `python3 -m pytest` — 35 passed (7 new tests in `tests/test_progress.py` covering elapsed formatting, report contents, plan/remaining tracking, no-op behavior without a TTY, and active-monitor registration). - Manual end-to-end verification under a real pseudo-terminal confirmed the spinner animates and that pressing space emits the progress report (`Stats:` / `Remaining:` lines).

author: cenewcombe
body:
## Summary

When lowering a binary elemental operation whose operands are arrays, `HlfirBuilder` took the result shape from the left operand (or the right one when the left is a scalar), regardless of whether that operand's shape was statically known. So when one operand had a compile-time constant shape (e.g. `x(3)`) and the other only a runtime, descriptor-based shape (e.g. an assumed-shape or allocatable `a(:)`), the elemental result was dynamically shaped (`hlfir.expr<?x...>`) even though the extents were known at compile time.

Elemental operands are conformable, so their extents are identical and the result  shape may be taken from either operand. This patch prefers an operand whose shape  is a compile-time constant, producing a statically shaped result. The left operand is checked first to avoid churn in lit test expectations.

## Motivation

A statically shaped elemental result:

* produces more precise FIR array types, and
* lets small constant-extent array assignments be fully unrolled instead of lowering to runtime-trip loops. For example, in

  ```fortran
  real, allocatable :: a(:,:)      ! deferred shape
  real              :: xx(3)       ! constant shape
  ...
  a(:,i) = a(:,i) + fc*xx(:)
  ```

  the `fc*xx(:)` and `a(:,i) + ...` elementals previously took `a`'s runtime (descriptor) extent, so the update lowered to a runtime-trip loop. With this change they take `xx`'s constant extent `3`, and the assignment fully unrolls.  This is what lets the enclosing loop become an innermost vectorization candidate for the SPEC OMP2012 `350.md` inner loop.

## Scope / limitations

Only a *wholly*-constant operand shape is used. The existing `// TODO: "merge" shape, get cst shape from front-end if possible.` is kept: the more general handling (folding the result shape from the front end via `Fortran::evaluate::GetShape`, and merging extents per dimension a la `hlfir.shape_meet`) is left as future work.

## Tests

* Adds `flang/test/Lower/HLFIR/elemental-array-constant-shape.f90`, covering a constant right operand, a constant left operand, both-operands-dynamic, and scalar-with-constant / scalar-with-dynamic operands.
* Updates `flang/test/Lower/HLFIR/matmul.f90`: in `matmul(a, b - x)` with `x(4,4)` constant, `b - x` is now inferred as `4x4` (its shape-inference regression check is updated accordingly; the matmul result type is unchanged).

## Notes

Part of #208086. This shape-inference change makes the enclosing loop an innermost vectorization candidate, but vectorization for the motivating benchmark will additionally require an LLVM LICM change to scalar-promote the conditionally-stored, loop-invariant reduction (`a(:,i)`) so the loop vectorizer can treat it as a reduction.
Assisted-by: Copilot

author: danielcopper
body:
Closes #1407.

During a unit's fetch/cover phase the main sync bar sat frozen at the unit's floor — deliberately, because the fetch and cover frames each count `current/total` from zero, and letting them move the coarse bar would make it jump backwards at every fetch→covers→apply boundary. For a platform whose dominant cost is the cover pull (e.g. ~2000 covers), the bar showed no movement for the entire phase.

**The fix — monotonic sub-slices within the running unit's width:**

- Progress frames now carry an optional `subStage` key (camelCase on the wire, matching the neighboring `totalSteps`/`runId`): the per-page fetch frames stamp `"fetch"`, both artwork passes (cover refresh + cover download) stamp `"covers"`. The field rides the persisted snapshot and `get_sync_status`, so a QAM remount mid-phase re-seeds correctly.
- The frontend's within-unit fill is now phase-aware (`withinUnitFraction` in `syncProgress.ts`, shares 15/25/60): fetch fills 0→0.15 of the unit slice, covers 0.15→0.40, apply 0.40→1.0. Phase transitions continue from the previous ceiling — monotonic by construction. The apply band is keyed on the stage alone, so a stale merged `subStage` can never mis-place it. A `fetching` frame without `subStage` (old snapshot) keeps today's rest-at-floor behavior.
- Skipped units are untouched (no phase frames, no width); ETA/estimates (#1382) and the session-budget gate (#1383) are unchanged.

**Known bounded limitation (documented):** the covers band is filled by two sequential passes (refresh, then download), each counting from zero — a mixed unit (changed covers + new covers) can dip within the covers band at that handover, bounded to the covers share of the unit's slice. The phase handovers themselves stay monotonic, and the common cases (first full sync, steady incremental without cover changes) don't dip.

**Tests:** backend pins `subStage` on the fetch/cover frames and the snapshot/`get_sync_status` round-trip; frontend covers every branch of the fill model including a full simulated frame sequence asserting frame-to-frame monotonicity and the legacy no-subStage fallback. Full suites: 5343 (py) / 1900 (fe) passed; all lint/type/format/build gates and the event-parity/callable-manifest checks green.

**Docs:** `backend-architecture.md` (sub-slice model, `subStage` payload field, the intra-covers-band wiggle disclosure) and `user-guide/syncing-your-library.md` (the bar now advances through fetch/cover phases) updated in this PR.

On-device note: the perceived smoothness on a large real platform in Game Mode still wants a Deck check — unit tests prove the math is monotonic; real frame cadence can't be exercised in CI.

author: whusterj
body:
Closes #138.

Makes a `specs/` directory explain itself — to a cold reader on GitHub, to agents grepping the tree, and to anyone opening a single assertion file.

## What's included

**CLI-managed block in `specs/README.md`** — `spekk init` writes a region fenced by `<!-- spekk:managed:begin -->` / `<!-- spekk:managed:end -->` holding the concept model, a full frontmatter reference (kept accurate against `internal/parser`), and a `spekk_schema_version`.

- Idempotent: regenerating with no schema change is byte-identical (no churn on repeated `spekk init`).
- Human prose outside the fence is preserved byte-for-byte.
- Legacy READMEs (no fence) are upgraded in place; corrupt fences (missing / duplicated / out-of-order markers) recover to exactly one clean region.
- No per-spec live state in the block — it's a pure function of the schema version. `spekk status` stays authoritative.

**Self-documenting file headers** — the coach and builder prompts now emit a brief HTML-comment frontmatter header (plus a pointer to `specs/README.md`) on newly authored spec/assertion files.

## Design notes

- Lean by construction: embedded Go string constants + marker-line string splitting. No templating engine, markdown/HTML parser, migration framework, or new subcommand.
- Corrupt handling is a single `regenerateReadmeContent` classifier (no-fence → append, well-formed → replace, corrupt → strip span + regenerate), not five bespoke branches.

## Testing

Built via the spekk dev loop (coach → coordinate → 4 builders → review). `go build ./cmd/spekk` and `go test ./...` green; `gofmt` clean. Test suite reviewed down to a lean high-value set (byte-identical idempotency, human-prose preservation, corrupt→one-clean-fence recovery, schema-accuracy, both `runInit` branches). Includes `RELEASE-NOTES-1.10.6.md`.

author: tatwater
body:
Reworks the social/privacy model per two decisions made while planning Phase 3, plus the trust-score design and a roadmap reorder. **Docs and code both updated; no behavioral surface that shipped (Phases 0–2.5) regresses** — the removed pieces were forward-loaded scaffolding (`friends`/`followers` levels were never active) and the Phase 2 visibility selector, which is superseded by "all reports public."

## What changed

**No social graph (D13).** No follow/friend graph — "a report is a report regardless of who made it." The `follows` table, `requireFollowApproval`, and the `friends`/`followers` visibility levels are gone.

**Reports are always public (D13).** Removed the report `visibility` field entirely (dropped `just_me` too — a private-only log withholds from the commons for a thin use case). Reads gate on **moderation + blocks** only. Deletion now anonymizes all reports uniformly.

**Profiles are the only privacy switch (D13).** `public` = searchable + full dossier (town, `bio`, counts, trust score, report history); `private` = name + photo only, not searchable. A private profile's individual reports are still public + name-attributed — it governs *personal discoverability*, not report reach.

**Minors are read-only (D41).** Since all reports are public, under-18 users can't post (server-rejected + client notice); minor profiles are forced private. **Interim guardrail, explicitly revisitable at the Q10 legal review (L2)** — a one-line flip if cleared.

**Trust score (new D50).** The asymmetric, public stand-in for the social layer's one real benefit ("whose reports do I trust"): raised by (a) corroboration on the same body within a tunable window and (b) helpful marks. Boost-only, window-bounded (nobody's penalized for conditions changing), cosmetic per D17 — never a safety weight (D3). Built in Phase 6.

**Roadmap reorder reconciled.** Phase order is now 4=Drive-time · 5=Newsfeed · 6=Bounties+trust · 7=Operator · 8=GPS · 9=Hazards; every cross-reference across the plans was updated. PRIVACY.md also now correctly states we collect date of birth (D41).

## Commits
1. Docs: remove social graph; add trust score (D50); reconcile phase reorder
2. Code: remove social graph; align visibility model with the plan
3. Docs: reports are always public (drop just_me); minors read-only
4. Code: reports are always public; minors read-only

## Not built here (their phases)
Block/mute enforcement + profile-search privacy (Phase 3); trust-score computation (Phase 6). Schema/types are ready; the seams are documented.

## Verification
`pnpm check-types` 6/6 · `pnpm test` 6/6 (Convex 100% stmts/funcs/lines) · `pnpm lint` clean.

author: sedkis
body:
## Summary
- The e2e harness waited for `/hello` then slept a fixed 2 seconds before running tests. Bundles load asynchronously, so on slow runners the suite starts while APIs still return 503 — this is the failure mode of the two red `main` e2e runs (Jul 14: all six tests 503; Jun 17: three tests where APIs responded but middleware hadn't attached yet). Same starter code and same pinned gateway ref passed on the PR branch, confirming a timing race rather than a code regression.
- Replaces the sleep with two readiness gates: (1) poll every API listen path from `apps/*.json` until none returns 503 (60s budget), then (2) a behavioral canary — the multi-bundle API must actually inject `X-Trace-Id` on `/multi/headers` (30s budget), proving bundle middleware executes, not just that routes exist.
- On timeout, dumps the last 30 gateway log lines and tears down, so a genuine failure is diagnosable instead of surfacing as six confusing test failures.

## Test plan
- `bash -n e2e/run.sh` passes
- The real validation is this PR's own e2e workflow run, which exercises the full harness against the goja gateway image

author: robertcsakany
body:
Implements OpenSpec change `fix-session-diff-open-nongit-and-preview`.

## Problem
Clicking a file row in the per-turn change-summary block opened a diff tab that rendered **"No changes for this file"** for newly written files. Root cause: a **path-format mismatch** — tool calls recorded absolute `args.path`, but the server keys `data.files` by relative-posix. The absolute path never string-equalled the relative key, so the panel blanked.

## Changes
1. **Path normalization at source** — new `lib/normalize-path.ts::normalizeUnderCwd` mirrors the server's `session-diff.ts::normalizePath` (absolute-under-cwd → relative-posix; else unchanged). Applied in `ChatView` to normalize **both** the displayed row and the `openDiffTab` argument so they can never diverge. `DiffViewer` retries with the normalized path on an exact-match miss.
2. **git ⇒ gitDiff, else session-derived diff** — `DiffPanel` precedence documented (selected change → gitDiff → session payload); non-git files render an all-additions/edit diff and never blank.
3. **First-class file preview** — the `Diff / File` control stays a persistent, labeled toggle in the split diff tab (`/api/session-file` + `SyntaxHighlighter`).

## Tests
New: `normalize-path.test.ts`, `summary-abs-path-open.test.ts` (reproduction), `DiffPanelPreview.test.tsx`; extended `DiffViewer.test.tsx`. Client suite: 3406 passed / 0 failures. Build green.

Docs: `docs/architecture.md` client/server path-agreement note; `packages/client/src/lib/AGENTS.md` row.

## Summary

Enhancement du checker `scripts/lean/check_i18n_siblings.py` (#6711) qui élimine les **deux classes de faux positifs** découvertes par l'erratum #4980 (issuecomment-4984015638) — l'audit DRIFT du cycle précédent avait produit 2 FP sur 3 verdicts, dont un a coûté une PR build-breaking (#6716, fermée).

1. **Self-qualifiers** : `_root_.X` (FR top-level) ↔ `<Ns>_en.X` (EN in-namespace) = la même référence exprimée depuis deux scopes. `normalize_body` efface désormais `_root_.` + `<Ns>.` pour les namespaces **déclarés dans le même fichier** (les qualifieurs étrangers restent du contenu comparé). Cas Arrow_en.
2. **Pattern consumer/extender** : un sibling EN qui `import`e le module FR canonique **réutilise** ses déclarations au lieu de les redéclarer. `check_pair` fait un check par sous-ensemble de blocs de déclaration et rapporte `OK-CONSUMER` (n blocs FR réutilisés). Cas Lattice_en.

```
game_theory_lean : 19 OK + 1 OK-CONSUMER (Lattice_en, 4 FR blocks reused) + 1 DRIFT + 0 orphan
  - Arrow_en    : DRIFT(FP) -> OK
```

author: aydiler
body:
## Problem

The **Publish to Snap Store** job failed on the v0.1.14 release run — but only on its trailing `Push snap store listing metadata` step:

```
Error: no such command 'push-metadata', maybe you meant 'upload-metadata'
```

The snap **upload itself succeeded** (`snapcore/action-publish@v1` → *Revision 17 created for 'md-viewer' and released to 'stable'*). So **v0.1.14 shipped fine to snap users** — only the store-listing description sync (unchanged from prior releases anyway) was skipped, and the overall run shows red because of this one step.

## Root cause

The step does `sudo snap install snapcraft --classic` (tracks *latest*). Newer snapcraft renamed the whole `push` verb family to `upload` (`push-metadata` → `upload-metadata`). This worked at v0.1.13 (~5 weeks earlier) with an older runner snapcraft — **environmental drift**, not a change from the release commit. Left as-is it fails on every future release.

## Fix

One-word verb rename: `snapcraft push-metadata` → `snapcraft upload-metadata` (same positional `<snap-file>` argument, same `--force` flag). Plus a comment + LESSONS.md entry + devlog 050 recording the rename and a suggestion to pin the snapcraft channel so the verb surface can't drift again.

CI-config + docs only; no Rust changes.

author: yschimke
body:
## Summary

The embedded `RcPlayer` (experimental Compose-based Remote Compose player) rendered text and container sizes ~density× off compared to the production View player. Root cause: pixel-valued fields were handed to Compose as density-independent units.

- **Text line height** — `RcPlayerText` built `lineHeight` from the pixel font size passed straight to `.sp`, double-applying the display density and inflating line spacing ~2–3× (bloated multi-line text, and cards/text that grew to fit it). Now gated on a non-default line height — matching `CoreText`, which only overrides `StaticLayout` line spacing when set — and converted px → sp otherwise.
- **Size constraints** — `widthIn`/`heightIn`/`dimensionConstraints` passed the core-resolved min/max (stored in pixels) straight to `.dp`, so a card's `heightIn(min = 64.dp)` became ~2.6× too tall. Now divided by density via a shared `constraintPxToDp` helper that preserves the `-1` "unspecified" sentinel.

`remote-core` folds density into `getMin`/`getMax` according to the document's `DENSITY_BEHAVIOR` header (scale for DP/LEGACY, raw pixels for PIXELS), and the player feeds that same display density into the core context — so dividing by density is correct for every behavior.

## Test plan

Added View-vs-embedded parity tests to `ExperimentalPreviewScreenshotTest` (each renders one document through both players and compares with MSSIM), run on an API 35 emulator:

author: drewhemm
body:
### Summary
This PR implements full, native, incremental plain-text tool-call streaming parsing and JSON translation for Gemma 4 checkpoints.

### Rationale
While Atlas currently carries standard parser registrations for Gemma 4, it lacks the traits and streaming mechanics required to compile streamed plain-text tool blocks on-the-fly:
1. Raw streaming boundaries can leak directly to the client's visual text stdout.
2. Streamed unbraced plain-text arguments (`call:NAME{...}`) fail to parse incrementally as standard structured JSON deltas.

### Key Changes
- **`crates/spark-server/src/tool_parser/gemma4.rs`**: Implemented `leak_markers()` for `Gemma4Parser` to register Gemma 4's unquoted envelope open/close delimiters (`<|tool_call>`, `<tool_call|>`) so they are properly stripped.
- **`crates/spark-server/src/tool_parser/streaming.rs`**: Extended `find_args_start()` to track Gemma 4's plain-text calling boundaries.
- **`crates/spark-server/src/tool_parser/streaming_emit.rs`**: Implemented the native translation block for Gemma 4 within `StreamingToolDetector::process`. This captures streamed unquoted arguments, compiles them incrementally into standard structured JSON fragments, and passes them cleanly to downstream execution layers.

### Verification
- Compiled and served Gemma 4 natively on Ada/Grace-Blackwell targets.
- Verified that parallel and sequential tool calls are streamed, intercepted, compiled, and dispatched dynamically with zero text leaks.

Fixes the two accepted findings from the round-6 review of #187:

- **P2** — backoff and grace state were reset before `SetCredentials` succeeded, so a failed persistence left the authenticator believing the refresh worked (https://github.com/futurehomeno/cliffhanger/pull/187#discussion_r3588442669). The resets now run only after successful persistence. Covered by the `failed persistence does not commit refresh state` test case.
- **P2** — 429 responses were retried on the fixed local `RetryDelay` (https://github.com/futurehomeno/cliffhanger/pull/187#discussion_r3588442679). Fixed via the simpler alternative: `ErrTooManyRequests` now exits immediately like `ErrUnauthorized`, leaving pacing to the caller's stateful backoff — sleeping the server-supplied `Retry-After` locally would block the authenticator mutex for a server-controlled duration. author: vjsingh1984
body:
## What

The adapter's edit-capture (`_file_edits` → `_generate_combined_patch`) was the sole patch source for the final eval. It silently lost patches for **20% of tasks** (`files_modified=0` → "No valid patch found") — even though the agent DID edit files on disk (proven by the verify_fn's git diff seeing real results like 75/76, 16/17 in-container).

## First-principles fix

The **disk state** (git diff) is the ground truth for "what the agent changed." The adapter's edit-capture is a fallible proxy that misses shell-based edits, stale snapshots, and some new files.

New shared `workspace_git_diff()` function: stages all changes (`git add -A`) then diffs staged vs HEAD (`git diff --cached HEAD`), capturing **modified + new + deleted files**. Used as the canonical patch source for BOTH paths:

1. **Adapter's `execute_task`**: `generated_patch = workspace_git_diff() or _generate_combined_patch()` — git diff primary, edit-capture fallback for non-git workspaces.
2. **Verify_fn**: replaced the inline `git diff HEAD` (which missed new untracked files) with the same `workspace_git_diff()` — **one source of truth** for both mid-task verify and final eval.

The edit-capture (`_file_edits`) is retained as fallback + for metrics (`files_modified` count), but the **patch comes from git diff**.

## Tests
2 new: `workspace_git_diff` captures modified + new files; returns "" for non-git dirs. 71 existing tests green. ruff/black/mypy clean.

## Impact
Recovers the ~20% of tasks that were silently scored "No valid patch found" despite the agent making correct edits. Combined with Phase 2's verify-and-retry (which achieved 97/97 VERIFIED on one task), this should move astropy off 0%.

author: jaxmatrix
body:
## What has been done

The first typed model for Phase 2 (PR 2b.1): the `FromXml`/`ToXml` conversion traits plus **hand-written** DrawingML text types `a:txBody` / `a:p` / `a:r` / `a:t`. (The `mjx-derive` proc-macro that will generate these is the follow-up PR 2b.2; these impls are its proving ground.)

- **`mjx-ooxml-core`**: `FromXml` / `ToXml` traits + `FromXmlError` (dep-free, `#[non_exhaustive]`, hand-written `Display`/`Error`).
- **`mjx-xml`**: `text::{escape_text, unescape_text}` — thin wrappers over quick-xml so typed models can decode/encode `a:t` text while quick-xml stays behind `mjx-xml`.
- **`mjx-dml`**: `TextBody`, `Paragraph`, `TextRun`, `Text` with accessors (`text()`, `paragraphs()`, `runs()`, `content()`).

## How it was done

- **Fidelity.** Each type stores its element `name` (with prefix), **all** attributes verbatim, the `empty` self-closing flag, and an **ordered** `content: Vec<…Content>` whose variants are the typed children plus a `Raw(RawNode)` catch-all. Order is preserved (a body's opaque `bodyPr`/`lstStyle` precede the typed `p`), so a parsed body re-serializes byte-for-byte even though only `txBody/p/r/t` are modeled and `bodyPr/lstStyle/pPr/rPr/br/fld` stay opaque.
- **Matching.** Children are matched by `(namespace, local)` — accepting **both** the strict and transitional DrawingML URIs, never by prefix. `from_xml` does **not** validate the element's own namespace, because a slide serializes `CT_TextBody` as `p:txBody` (presentationml) though its type is DrawingML.
- **Text.** `a:t` is decoded (entities unescaped) on read and **minimally** escaped (`<`, `&`) on write — byte-identical for canonical spellings (the modeled-part / tier-2 contract; documented on `escape_text`).
- **Interner discipline.** `to_xml` reuses the part's interned `Symbol`s, so its output is serialized within the same part's interner (documented on the trait module).
- Layering respected: `mjx-ooxml-core` stays dependency-free; quick-xml stays behind `mjx-xml`; `mjx-opc` is only a **dev**-dependency (for the exit test).
- The `mjx-dml::text` module docs record the exact shape PR 2b.2's derive must regenerate.

## How to test it

```sh
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps
```

- **Exit test** — `crates/mjx-dml/tests/txbody_roundtrip.rs::txbody_round_trips_byte_identical_in_context`: the real `p:txBody` from `sample.pptx`'s `slide1.xml` → `from_xml` → `to_xml` → the **whole slide is byte-identical**, and `TextBody::text() == "Hello OOXML"`.
- **15 fragment tests** — `crates/mjx-dml/tests/text_model.rs`: every round-trip is paired with a **structural** assertion (counts/variants/decoded text) so byte-identity cannot pass by dumping everything into `Raw`. Covers self-closing preservation, opaque `rPr`, `&`/`<` byte-identity vs `>` canonical-only, empty-text spellings, strict-URI matching, foreign children, `xml:space` + no trimming, `a:br` opacity, invalid-entity errors, and the `p:txBody` wrapper.

## Notes

Split from the handoff's PR 2b so the derive is designed against proven hand-written impls; PR 2b.2 builds the `#[derive(FromXml, ToXml)]` macro next. The DrawingML preset-shape ledger is a separate docs PR (#5).

author: simtop
body:
Stacked on #75 (merge order: #74 → #75 → this).

Previously the search query lived in the screen's `rememberSaveable` while the view model started blank, so after process death the restored UI showed the old text over the pre-search prompt — the results were gone until the user edited the query.

The query now lives in the view model behind a `SavedStateHandle`: `getStateFlow` feeds the existing debounce/`transformLatest` chain, so a recreated view model re-runs the search by itself, and the screen reads the query from the VM (`onQueryChange` writes through the handle), leaving one source of truth. To receive the `SavedStateHandle`, the VM switches from map-injected `@ViewModelKey` to metrox's `ViewModelAssistedFactory` (`@ViewModelAssistedFactoryKey` + `extras.createSavedStateHandle()`) — the screen still uses plain `metroViewModel()`, since assisted factories are tried first with `CreationExtras`.

Verified three ways: a new unit test builds the VM with a pre-seeded `SavedStateHandle` and asserts the search re-runs; full `make test` / `make screenshot-verify` / `make konsist` green; and end-to-end on an emulator — searched "ipa" (159 results), confirmed the process dead via `pidof` after `am kill`, relaunched, and the results list came back, not just the text.

author: agusgarcia3007
body:
## The bug

Since #19 the Release job ran a single `tegami ci`. Reading the tegami dist confirms `ci` = `versionPackages` + `publishPackages`, and `versionPackages` → `tegami.draft()` only **reads** already-drafted entries from `.tegami/changes/` (it would generate from commits only if the config set `conventionalCommits: true`, which it never has). The step that actually **generates** entries from conventional commits is bare `tegami` (no command), which auto-drafts non-interactively when `CI` is set.

`.tegami/changes/` is gitignored, so every runner started empty → `ci` found **"Nothing to version"** and shipped nothing. Result: **npm stuck at `0.1.1`** while `feat` (#18) and `fix` (#20) piled up on `main`. The Release run for #20 was green but published nothing — a silent no-op on every merge.

Verified locally: `CI=true bun scripts/tegami.ts` against `main` drafts `videos-sdk: minor` (from #18's feat) → would bump `0.1.1 → 0.2.0`.

## The fix

Restore the one-merge, publish-on-merge flow (the model CLAUDE.md documents):

- **draft** (`tegami`) → **version** (`tegami version`) → **check-publish** → **commit + push to `main`** → **publish** (`tegami publish`), as separate steps.
- The bump is pushed to protected `main` with **`RELEASE_TOKEN`** — a fine-grained PAT owned by the allowlisted admin (`agusgarcia3007`; `enforce_admins` is off). The runner's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't push to `main` (that's the `GH006` that killed the #18 one-merge attempt).
- `scripts/tegami.ts`: `versionPr: false` turns the Version Packages PR back off.
- A PAT push **does** trigger workflows, so a job-level `if: !startsWith(...'chore(release):')` skips the release commit's own run (a `chore` commit also drafts nothing — doubly stopped).
- CLAUDE.md's Publishing section rewritten to match, including the `tegami ci`-never-drafts trap.

## ⚠️ Before merging

1. Create a **fine-grained PAT** (owner `agusgarcia3007`, repo `Rehelios/videos-sdk`, **Contents: Read and write**), then add it as the repo secret **`RELEASE_TOKEN`**.
2. Merge this PR. On merge the new workflow drafts the accumulated `feat`/`fix` and **ships `0.2.0`** (clears the backlog), publishing to npm with provenance and cutting the tag + GitHub Release.

Without the secret set, the release fails loudly at the push step (no longer a silent no-op).

author: moomooskycow
body:
## What changed

- fix browser telemetry configuration to use literal module-scope `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` member reads, preserving Next.js production inlining for the endpoint and kill-switch
- add a compiled `.next/static` falsifier that requires the selected endpoint and enabled value; CI builds with `false` and `/ci-telemetry-sink` and scans the result
- run telemetry inventory checks/tests in the lint gate and the built-artifact scan in the production web-build gate
- change Playwright from `next dev` to `next build` + `next start`, seed a qa-local user in the existing pgvector CI test job, observe a real authenticated `POST /api/telemetry`, and make sink outage coverage exercise that same flow
- make the production-start QA server provider-independent: QA middleware and server auth use the signed local boundary, and the QA build uses a local auth context instead of loading Clerk
- close usage metadata to `fallbackAttempted` and validate performance-tag value types/ranges server-side

## Root cause

The telemetry client resolved configuration through a `process.env` object, which Next.js does not inline for public browser variables. The previous Playwright outage test only aborted a route while loading a public page that never emitted telemetry, so it could pass without exercising the sink.

## Validation

- `pnpm telemetry:test`: passed (5 tests)
- `pnpm telemetry:check`: passed (16 classified producers)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT=/ci-telemetry-sink pnpm deployment:build`: passed
- `pnpm telemetry:check -- --bundle-dir apps/web/.next/static --expect-endpoint /ci-telemetry-sink --expect-enabled false`: passed
- targeted telemetry Vitest files: passed (32 tests)
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint:design`, `pnpm deployment:check`, `pnpm deployment:test`, and `pnpm --filter extension build`: passed
- pre-commit/pre-push gitleaks, secrets, lint, and type-check hooks: passed
- CI run [29450786059](https://github.com/misty-step/sploot/actions/runs/29450786059): all jobs passed, including full DB-backed tests, retrieval eval, production-start Playwright QA, and merge-gate

author: fritzoid
body:
**(a) is done.** truthdb#100 gave the pool an **inbox** — a condvar queue a worker waits on for *either* a call or a **drain nudge** — so a releaser on one thread can hand parked work to a worker on another. That was the missing capability #99 identified, and with it the deadlock backstop joined the idle reaper on the maintenance thread.

Records the three constraints #98–#100 established, each found by shipping its opposite:

- **`reap_expired` is coupled to draining** — reaping a victim releases the locks that rescue the waiters behind it. That is what the nudge exists for.
- **A grantable waiter must never drive a sleep** — #98 won't reap one, so its deadline stays in the past; a wait derived from it computes zero. Measured at **3109 sweeps in 200ms**, only while every worker was busy.
- **Workers now block indefinitely** — no `recv_timeout` fallback, so a missing nudge parks a batch *forever*, not late.

Also corrects docs#53/#54's claim that nothing calls `EngineHandle::shutdown` — **the server does**, at `src/main.rs:195`. My grep covered `crates/` and missed the binary.

**New practice, learned expensively:** run a concurrency test's whole module 25+ times before believing it. A **20% flake survived three consecutive clean full-suite runs** in #100. The cause will recur: tests run in parallel in one binary, so a `static` counter observing a pool measures every other test's pool too — put them on `Shared`.

Note (b) is now *survivable*, not free: a blocked worker is still a lost worker, and `CloseSession` can still sit behind one.

Pairs with truthdb#99 and truthdb#100 (both merged).

author: dehvcurtis
body:
Closes the verified portion of the I15 ops-docs hardening initiative (ADV-197, ADV-199, ADV-200). Each finding was verified against source before any edit; several did not survive verification and were refuted rather than "fixed" (see below).

## ADV-197 — remove insecure-TLS flags from prod runbooks (verified REAL)

Premise verified first: `app.0xapogee.com` and `admin.0xapogee.com` both return HTTP 200 with `ssl_verify_result=0` (valid Let's Encrypt certs), so `-k` was never required against production. Its presence stripped MITM protection from commands carrying admin JWTs, internal service keys and rotation secrets, and trained operators to ignore certificate errors.

- 116 occurrences across 31 files (playbooks, pipelines, workflows, feature-tests, internal)
- `cli-installation.md` "SSL certificate error -> use `--insecure`" advice replaced with CA-bundle / proxy-CA guidance and an explicit never-disable-verification note

Scoped to production-targeted commands only. Local/self-signed contexts (localhost, harbor, local-development) intentionally retain `-k`. Historical records (`audit/`, `audits/`, `changelogs/`, `old/`) left as written.

## ADV-199 — origin-cert diagnostic (mostly refuted; real core fixed)

The step was framed "Bypass Cloudflare" and used `-k` — which suppressed the exact certificate error the step exists to detect (it diagnoses whether the origin serves a valid cert, the Cloudflare 526 cause), turning a diagnostic into a false "everything is fine". Reframed as an origin-certificate diagnostic with verification ON, documented outcome interpretation, and a pointer to ADV-38 (origin lockdown).

The load-balancer IP is deliberately NOT redacted: it is the documented global static address already published in `gcp/infrastructure.md`, `gcp/networking.md` and `standards/{domain-management,ingress-networking}.md`, and a GKE static LB IP is inherently discoverable. The real control is Cloud Armor (ADV-38).

## ADV-200 — MFA-reset audit logging (mostly refuted; real core fixed)

Resets are not auto-written to `admin_audit_logs`, yet the playbook framed the audit entry as "Consider creating" — optional. Disabling MFA on an admin account is a privileged security-control change; an unlogged one is indistinguishable from an attacker resetting MFA for account takeover. The entry is now REQUIRED, with the underlying application gap called out. A blast-radius caution was added to the bulk-reset path rather than removing a legitimate recovery procedure.

The reported "leaked real TOTP secret" (`JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP`) is the canonical RFC/library example base32 value, cited here as an illustration and in a post-mortem for a `.local` test account whose MFA the documented fix already reset. No rotation or history scrub required.

## Phases

changelog ✓ · security ✓ (no secrets/.env; changes remove insecure patterns, add no surface) · tests N/A (markdown-only repo, no suite) · docs ✓ (the change is the documentation) · standards ✓

Refs: ADV-197, ADV-199, ADV-200

author: vincelaird
body:
## PR 0 — spec only (the pre-code gate)

Commits the two line-open-runner specs so the implementation PRs (1 → 3) build against an immutable, reviewed model. **No code, no `--live`.** This is the spec-first rebuild that supersedes the closed #10/#11 (the stacked A+B stack).

### Architecture: Tier 0 — a statistical instrument, not a consensus protocol

Tier 0 measures **which model produces the best closing-line value (CLV)** on markets captured cleanly at their independently-derived open. It fires **per-market at the open** (a ready market never waits for a sibling), records each model's forecast, captures the close, and reports CLV **with** its coverage, sample size, and uncertainty. Imperfection is **measured and reported**, not structurally forbidden.

Deliberately **out of Tier 0** (deferred to a later adversarial tier only if the benchmark becomes an adversarial public leaderboard, outside agents submit results, money/reputation ride on it, or an audit demands independently-timestamped publication): the frozen `games` census + MVCC builder, per-fire negative-space denominators (`denominatorSha256` / `fire_coverage_snapshot`), the `schedule_changed` opening gate, whole-cohort salvage poisoning, and on-chain Polygon anchoring.

### What's here (two files only)
- `docs/SPEC-line-open-speculation-runner.md` — the **base spec** (the *unit* + the *firing model*): each `(gameId, market)` is an independent firing entity; detection and policy are separate layers; the per-speculation late gate; independently-verifiable entry timing from `odds_history` (§3.6). Repointed at Tier 0 throughout — the stale 30-minute gate, "twelve participants", per-market `speculation_status` denominator, and PR A/B sequencing are gone.
- `docs/SPEC-line-open-evidence-model.md` — the **Tier-0 evidence & measurement model**: what Tier 0 is + the 10 retained protections + the deferred list (§0); `odds_history` ground truth (§1); the strict `CohortManifestV1` + public-Git precommitment (§2); candidate discovery (pinned `gameDiscoveryWindowHours`) + per-market no-wait firing + the canonical window gates (two-sided V-lag) + deterministic admission ordering + full-roster fairness + the prepared-snapshot→`detectedAt`→claim→synchronous-projection ordering + co-arrival partial-claim (§3); the fire artifact + atomic at-most-once/budget/concurrency reservation (§4); per-fire entry verification + the arm-outcome enum + domain-bound `armDigest` / `responseSha256` provenance (§5); finalization — the `odds_history` universe keyed on **`games.sport`** (games used only as an identity join, never a census) + `effectiveEnabled(sport, market)` + global `U/F/C/M/X/D` coverage reconciliation (§6); close capture from `closing_lines` (`source==="jsonodds"`) + CLV + a byte-reproducible game-clustered bootstrap (§7); the trust boundary stated plainly (§8); PR 0→3 sequencing (§9); the 48-case acceptance matrix (§10).

### Coverage is derived, not self-reported
The load-bearing property: the expected universe `U` is reconstructed from independent `odds_history` first-appearances at scoring time and reconciled against the fired keys — published as fire/clean-entry/missed/extra/duplicate coverage **beside** CLV. A dropped market surfaces as a miss in `M = U − F`; it cannot hide, because membership is derived from the independent feed, not attested per fire.

### Sequence after merge
PR 1 (per-market firing + fire artifacts + at-most-once + rehearsal, `--live` **hard-disabled**) branches from `main` **only after this PR merges** — not concurrently. `--live` is enabled only in the reviewed PR 3. Run no paid cohort before PR 2's coverage reconciliation lands.

The OAuth experiment wired the session into Scalar's "Try it out" — bearer-token injection, an in-explorer login badge, a per-session credential toggle, and a reveal toggle for Scalar's built-in Authentication panel. body:
Fixes #397.

`environment: release` / `environment: docs-deploy` are inert unless the GitHub Environments carry protection rules — a settings-side fact the workflows can't enforce, and the 0.20.0 release proved the failure mode.

**In-repo backstop (this PR):** each environment-gated job (`finalize`, `release`, `library-release`, docs `deploy`) begins with a step that queries `GET /repos/{repo}/environments/{name}` with the workflow token and fails unless a `required_reviewers` protection rule is present. The logic: an *unprotected* environment starts the job with no approval — and the first step then refuses to publish/deploy. An unreadable environment also fails (fail-closed).

**Operational half:** already done — both environments now carry a required-reviewers rule (verified via the API before writing this PR).

Not included: the two informational nits from the issue (`cli_tag` via `env:` hygiene, `install.sh` latest-version robustness) — happy to follow up separately if wanted.

author: sepy97
body:
The fundamental score is a cross-sectional percentile, so it must not depend on **earnings timing** — the blackout is just a *display filter* (a limiting criterion), as noted in review.

`select_top` was ranking **after** dropping the blackout names, so a name's percentile shifted based on which peers happened to report soon. That (a) leaked options-timing into the fundamental score and (b) made a market screen and a single-ticker search disagree by a few %.

**Fix:** gate → **rank the full gate-passing set** → *then* apply the blackout (and the other limiting filters). One reorder in `select_top`.

**Result:** the score is earnings-timing-independent, and the screen and search show the **same** score for a name — verified: PLTR / GILD / CF / WMT now match to the last digit (CF was 0.718 vs 0.692, now identical). A blacked-out name (e.g. AA) still has a score in search and is simply filtered out of the screen — same number, just hidden there.

## Summary

Adds one new content entry: `content/rules/ai-generated-open-redirect-review-rules.mdx`.

A source-backed review checklist for AI-generated redirect/forward code: prefer an indexed mapping or hardcoded destination over echoing a raw client-supplied URL, restrict caller-supplied "return to" paths to relative same-origin paths, validate any unavoidable absolute-URL destination against a real parsed-host allowlist (not a `.includes()`/substring check, which `evil.com/mysite.com` and `mysite.com.evil.com` both defeat), give auth/SSO-callback redirects extra scrutiny since they're the highest-impact target for phishing chains, and confirm handler code actually halts after issuing a redirect.

This continues the `ai-generated-*-review-rules` family (CSRF, SQL injection, path traversal, SSRF, regex safety, XSS #5031, IDOR #5035, command injection #5038) — open redirect (CWE-601) is a common, well-documented class with no focused entry yet in this repo.

Sources cited (`sourceUrls`/`documentationUrl`): OWASP Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards Cheat Sheet, CWE-601, and two PortSwigger Web Security Academy references on open redirection. All four URLs were checked live and return 200.

- Single file, single category (`rules`), no edits to generated artifacts, README, or other content entries.
