# Remove stellar/winget-pkgs (fork of microsoft/winget-pkgs) from Stellar

## What
Adds a migration removing `https://github.com/stellar/winget-pkgs` from the
Stellar ecosystem.

```
reprem Stellar https://github.com/stellar/winget-pkgs
```

## Why
`stellar/winget-pkgs` is a **fork of `microsoft/winget-pkgs`** (the Windows
Package Manager manifest repo), created under the Stellar org to publish a
package to winget — standard practice. Because the fork carries upstream's full
contributor history, it pulls a large number of Windows-packaging contributors
into Stellar's developer counts:

- **~1,440 active developers** in the last 90 days, but only **2 stars**
- **1,440 of those 1,444 appear in no other Stellar repo**
- **≈27%** of Stellar's recent active developers in the current snapshot
  (`20260715T125411`)

None of these contributors do crypto work on Stellar — the attribution is purely
an artifact of the fork relationship.

## Precedent
This mirrors the prior removal of the equivalent Nethermind fork in
`migrations/2025-05-01T112748_mutations`:

```
reprem Ethereum https://github.com/NethermindEth/winget-pkgs
reprem Nethermind https://github.com/NethermindEth/winget-pkgs

body:
Adds the missing piece of the browser IDE: an **interactive terminal** in the console — a shell running **inside the sandbox** as uid 1000 in the app workspace, streamed to **xterm.js** over a **WebSocket**.

### Core (sandboxd)
- `docker.Client.ExecTTY` — interactive `docker exec -it` over a `creack/pty` PTY (interactive counterpart to the one-shot `Exec`).
- `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/terminal` — upgrades to a WebSocket (`gorilla/websocket`), bridges PTY ↔ WS (binary = keystrokes/output; text `{"resize":{cols,rows}}` = size), keeps the sandbox warm via `Inflight`, kills the shell on disconnect. Guards: 404 bad/unknown, 409 not-running; same-origin check; auth via the existing middleware.
- `statusWriter.Hijack` passthrough (api + logging wrappers) so the upgrade survives the middleware chain.

### Console
- A **Terminal** tab (xterm.js + fit addon), shown when the sandbox is running.

### Security
No new trust boundary — it runs in the **same container the agent already executes arbitrary code in** (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`), as **non-root uid 1000**. Just an authenticated, direct interface.

**Verified end-to-end (including under gVisor):** interactive `bash` as `USER=sandbox`, `UID=1000`, in `/home/sandbox/workspace/app`, real TTY (prompt, echo, bracketed paste). Go build/vet/tests + console tsc/build all green; OpenAPI updated + a guard test added.

## What this adds

Four commits on top of `main`, closing the security/architecture gaps that make the 146-table schema safe for real PHI. Backend code lives in the platform repo; this PR carries the schema, tests, ADRs, and the flag-gated desktop swap.

### Item 2 — Identity & isolation ADRs (`d9e7252`)
- `docs/architecture-decisions/0001-clinical-data-isolation.md` — dedicated project with HIPAA blast-radius rationale; why it doesn't fork the backend.
- `0002-identity-and-system-of-record.md` — single identity provider (clinical project), staged legacy migration, hashed-invitation patient-link spec.

### Item 4+5 — Migration 0012 + keystone test (`89c511c`)
- **`can_write_patient_data()`**: patient-scoped writes now require an active practitioner/admin/owner role — closes the confirmed finding that a patient's own login could write clinical rows. 81 bulk `FOR ALL` policies split into per-command (82 patient-gated SELECTs, 243 role-gated writes).
- Soft-deleted rows excluded from SELECT; `invitations.token` → sha-256 `token_hash`; `updated_by` normalized; CLI migration-history bootstrapped.
- `tests/practitioner_assignment_access.sql` extended to **37 assertions across all five domains** (clinical core, labs, supplements, reasoning, billing) — all pass live, rolled back. Advisor: **0 findings**.

### Item 6 — Flag-gated live `patients` namespace (`09fb9ce`)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_LIVE_API` (default off → mock). `patients.list`/`get` read real `patient_profiles` through the authenticated tRPC backend; desktop never touches Postgres directly. `summary` + all other namespaces stay mock.
- TanStack Query added; `CommandPalette` + `AssistantDrawer` moved onto the async façade.
- See `docs/live-api.md` for the full verification table.

### Item 7 — Docs cross-link (`a200413`)
- `docs/README.md` ties this repo's ADRs to the platform repo's Phase 0 audit + backend ADRs (merged to its `main` in PR #5).

## Verification (real output)
- Desktop default build: `tsc` + `eslint` + `next build` green (24 routes).
- Backend: `vitest` **198/198** (19 new authz + scrubber tests); clinical namespace live-enforces auth over HTTP.
- RLS: **37/37** live assertions; advisor 0 findings.
- Desktop live adapter exercised over HTTP against the backend's RLS-filtered wire shape.

Companion platform-repo PRs: #4 (hardening, merged), #5 (Phase 0 docs, merged), and the clinical tRPC layer on `claude/phase2-clinical-auth-layer`.

🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Unauthenticated access to `/api/analytics` and `/api/metrics` allowed potential exposure of internal application metrics and telemetry data to unauthorized users.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could scrape these endpoints to gather detailed insights into application performance, traffic patterns, error rates, and user session activity, which could aid in further attacks or information disclosure.
🔧 **Fix:** Introduced an `ADMIN_SECRET` environment variable and implemented a Bearer token authorization check in the GET handlers for both endpoints. Requests lacking a matching token now correctly receive a 401 Unauthorized response.
✅ **Verification:** Verified that linting and testing passes, and that the endpoints reject unauthenticated access while still operating normally when the correct authorization headers are provided.

author: egkip
body:
## Summary
- Configure pdf-parse to use its bundled worker data URL in production/development instead of the default ./pdf.worker.mjs path.
- Reuse that configured parser for both text-layer extraction and OCR page rendering.
- Add a regression test that asserts the worker data URL is registered before parsing outside test mode.

## Why
Production analysis was failing on Vercel with:

`Setting up fake worker failed: Cannot find module '/var/task/.next/server/chunks/pdf.worker.mjs'`

The default pdfjs worker path resolves relative to the bundled server chunk on Vercel, but that worker file is not emitted there. Using pdf-parse's bundled worker data URL avoids the missing runtime file path.

## Verification
- npm test -- src/lib/ai/__tests__/pdf-text.test.ts src/lib/ai/ocr/__tests__/pdf-text-ocr.test.ts src/app/api/upload/__tests__/route.test.ts

- npm run lint
- npm test — 427/427 passing
- npm run build

## Smoke after merge
Upload a PDF from the dashboard and confirm analysis moves past extraction instead of failing with missing pdf.worker.mjs.

author: oimiragieo
body:
## Summary
- `is_wsl_host()` (`src/tensor_grep/cli/runtime_paths.py`) only checked `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`/`WSL_INTEROP` env vars, then `/run/WSL`. A wrapper/service that strips both env vars on a WSL1-style host with no `/run/WSL` makes `is_wsl_host()` wrongly return `False`, which cascades: `is_cross_domain_native_binary()` returns `False` and the GPU probe hands a raw Linux `/tmp` path to the Windows `tg.exe` binary, producing a `path_not_found` fault that reads as "no GPU support" when the GPU route may be fine.
- Adds `/proc/version` (contains `"microsoft"`, case-insensitive, on every WSL1/WSL2 kernel; never on non-WSL Linux — confirmed live: `Linux version 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`) as a final, read-safe fallback checked *after* the existing env-var and `/run/WSL` checks (cheapest/env-based signals stay first).
- The read is wrapped in `try/except OSError` (covers `FileNotFoundError`) and returns `False` on any failure — never raises.
- This ONLY ADDS a WSL detection signal; it never removes one, so it cannot regress a currently-working WSL config.
- No other function touched: `native_binary_targets_windows`, `is_cross_domain_native_binary`, and `translate_path_for_windows_binary` are unchanged.

## Diff
```diff
 def is_wsl_host() -> bool:
     """True when this process is running inside a WSL (1 or 2) Linux environment.
 
     This is a NARROWER check than "any Linux box" -- it only adds the "genuinely WSL" signal on
     top of the `sys.platform.startswith("linux")` gate already applied by callers, so a
     `.exe`-suffixed path used by an unrelated fixture on a bare Linux CI runner (no WSL) is never
     misread as a real WSL path-domain mismatch. `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`/`WSL_INTEROP` are set by WSL
     itself in every real WSL session and are the standard, filesystem-read-free way to detect it;
     `/run/WSL` (also used by `core.hardware.device_detect`) is the fallback for a stripped
-    subprocess environment that dropped those variables.
+    subprocess environment that dropped those variables. `/proc/version` containing "microsoft"
+    (case-insensitive) is the canonical fallback for a fully stripped environment where a wrapper
+    or service dropped both env vars AND has no `/run/WSL` -- every WSL1/WSL2 kernel stamps this
+    string (e.g. "Linux version 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2"), and no non-WSL Linux kernel
+    does, so this signal is safe and cannot false-positive. The read is wrapped fail-closed:
+    any OSError (missing file, permission denied, etc.) is treated as "not WSL" rather than
+    raising.
     """
     if os.environ.get("WSL_DISTRO_NAME") or os.environ.get("WSL_INTEROP"):
         return True
-    return os.path.exists("/run/WSL")
+    if os.path.exists("/run/WSL"):
+        return True
+    try:
+        with open("/proc/version", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return "microsoft" in fh.read().lower()
+    except OSError:
+        return False
```
Plus 3 new cases added to `TestIsWslHost` in `tests/unit/test_runtime_paths.py` (mocking `builtins.open`, never touching a real filesystem):
1. `test_true_via_proc_version_when_env_and_run_wsl_both_stripped` — the new case, currently `False` on `main`.
2. `test_false_on_plain_linux_without_any_wsl_signal` — extended to mock a bare-Linux `/proc/version` (no "microsoft") to keep the negative case deterministic.
3. `test_false_when_proc_version_unreadable` — `/proc/version` open raises `FileNotFoundError` -> fails closed to `False`, never raises.

The 3 pre-existing cases (env vars set; `/run/WSL` present) are untouched and still pass, proving no regression.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv sync --extra dev` (cargo 1.96.0 on PATH)
- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/unit/test_runtime_paths.py -x -q` -> **51 passed, 1 skipped** (skip = real-`wslpath` smoke test, Windows host has no `wslpath`)
- [x] `uv run ruff check src/tensor_grep/cli/runtime_paths.py tests/unit/test_runtime_paths.py` -> All checks passed
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check --preview src/tensor_grep/cli/runtime_paths.py tests/unit/test_runtime_paths.py` -> 2 files already formatted
- [x] `uv run mypy src/tensor_grep` (full package, matches CI's `mypy` step) -> Success: no issues found in 80 source files
- [x] Whole-repo `ruff check .` -> All checks passed. Whole-repo `ruff format --check --preview .` -> 1 pre-existing, **unrelated** finding in `docs/architecture.md` (markdown code-fence formatting drift from an earlier merged commit, not touched by this PR)
- [x] Full `tests/unit` suite with `dev,ast` extras (CI parity for the `test-python` job) -> 3875 passed before an unrelated pre-existing failure in `test_retrieval_dense.py` (missing optional `model2vec` dep, gated behind the `semantic` extra, unrelated to this change) stopped the `-x` run; zero regressions attributable to this change
- [x] ASCII-only + LF verified on the staged git blobs directly (`git cat-file blob :<path>`, not `git show`, to avoid autocrlf smudge): 0 CRLF bytes, no non-ASCII bytes in either file

## Flag for reviewers
This touches the GPU/native-binary cross-domain detection surface (`is_wsl_host` feeds `is_cross_domain_native_binary`) — **needs the mandatory adversarial Opus gate** per this repo's change-control policy before merge.

Not merging this myself; opened as **draft**.

author: santhreal
body:
`From<HistDbEntry> for History` unwrapped `String::from_utf8` on the command/cwd/hostname blobs and `from_unix_timestamp` on the raw `i64`. A non-UTF-8 byte (legal in a POSIX path or command) or an out-of-range timestamp panicked the entire `atuin import nu-histdb`.

Decode the byte fields lossily and clamp an out-of-range timestamp to the epoch. Adds a test with an invalid UTF-8 field and an `i64::MAX` timestamp, plus a valid-row test.

author: wkasekende
body:
## The bug

When a setting line doesn't already exist, `rewriteSetting` appends it inside the YAML frontmatter — but the frontmatter match was `\n`-only, so a Windows-authored (`\r\n`) OPENCUES.md failed the match and the **whole append silently bailed**: the blank reported success, the file was never changed.

Surfaced while debugging the inline `loading animation … _` blank on WSL — it appends `blank-loading-frames`, a key absent from older files, so it hit the append path (an existing-line *replace* was already CRLF-safe via `[^\r\n]*`).

## Fix

Frontmatter match is now CRLF-tolerant (`\r?\n`), and the file's own EOL is captured + reused so styles never mix. No-frontmatter files are still left untouched.

Pinned by four `rewriteSetting` EOL tests (LF/CRLF replace, LF/CRLF append, no-frontmatter bail).

## Not in scope (deliberately)

- The loading-animation blank appearing dead on **opencode** was a **stale install** (the fork predated #299/#293, lacking the `loading-animation`/`model` factories). `opencues install opencode` fixes it — the runtime already prints that exact remedy in its `[err]` fill.
- `createBlankInvoke` ignoring `timeoutMs` was left alone: the `get()` provably doesn't hang (Bun repro), so a timeout on that hot shared path would be speculative.

`@opencues/runtime` 0.18.6 → 0.18.8 (0.18.7 reserved by the #306 branch, PR #307).

author: ayyitskevin
body:
## What this is

The first Wave-1 slice from the codebase review: an **authoritative STOP lever** for a compromised or runaway agent. Advances the operator loop's **Intervene** phase.

Before this, the only token-revoke path was owner-scoped, so the admin cockpit (`/admin/agents`) could *display* an agent's live tokens but offered no way to *disable* them — you could watch an agent, not stop it.

## What changed

- **`core/agent_commands.py` (new)** — the single owner of the logic:
  - `revoke_agent_tokens` — the kill switch: revoke every live token a user holds.
  - `offboard_user` — full lockout: demote to viewer + revoke every session + revoke every token.
  - Each runs as **one atomic, audited transaction** (the cardinal "one command owns each write" rule); web/REST/MCP are thin callers that translate one `AgentCommandError`, so the authorization guard and the **last-admin safety** live in exactly one place.
- **Data layer** — composable `tokens.revoke_all_tokens_for_user` / `sessions.revoke_all_sessions`, plus a `commit=` parameter on `users.set_role` for transaction composition.
- **REST** — `DELETE /users/{id}/tokens`, `POST /users/{id}/offboard`, gated on admin role **and** the admin token scope.
- **MCP** — `revoke_agent_tokens` + `offboard_agent` tools over the client.
- **Web** — danger controls on `/admin/agents` (CSRF + `data-confirm`), post/redirect/get with a result banner.
- **Bonus fix** — admin password reset now revokes the target's live sessions, closing the offboarding gap where a reset left a cookie valid for up to `SESSION_TTL_DAYS`.

## Testing

New `tests/test_agent_kill_switch.py` (16 tests) covers the data layer, the atomic audited command (attribution + last-admin guard), REST authorization (role + token scope + 404/409), the web controls (CSRF required, admin-only, banner), and the MCP surface. Also drove it end-to-end against a real booted app: an agent's bearer token returns 200 before the kill switch and 401 after, with the action recorded in the append-only activity log.

- `ruff check .` — clean
- `pytest -q` — **1359 passed, 39 skipped**

## Notes

Definition-of-done met: gate green, ran it against the real DB, no stray data stores, stayed in scope (the rest of the Wave-1 safety bundle — least-privilege default token scope, webhook SSRF hardening, non-skippable MCP gate, `idx_activity_actor` — will follow as separate PRs).

author: santhreal
body:
`CodeSplitter._chunk_node` recurses into oversized children, but a leaf node (a long string literal, comment, or token with no AST children) hit the empty loop and returned `[]`, silently dropping its text.

Emit an oversized leaf as its own chunk instead. An atomic token that cannot be subdivided is allowed to exceed the size limit rather than vanish. Adds a test asserting the literal survives.

## Purpose

Rebuild the complete live application runtime from a validated `ApplicationStateSnapshot` without allowing partial state application.

## Changes

- Add `SnapshotRehydrator`
- Add `RehydratedApplicationState` as the complete replacement runtime graph
- Rebuild one shared `InMemoryUserAccountRepository`
- Recreate general, customer, employee, and administrator login services against that shared repository
- Restore inventory listings and purchase requests through `Offer.restore(...)`
- Restore customer ownership and payment plans
- Restore the payment ledger from immutable transactions
- Continue payment transaction numbering from the highest restored `PAY-xxxxxx` identifier
- Validate snapshot version, account uniqueness, account roles and credentials, contiguous listing and request IDs, listing references, accepted-payment terms, ownership records, transaction identity, cumulative totals, and balances
- Reject malformed snapshots before constructing or applying replacement state
- Atomically replace all live repositories, services, inventory, ownership, and payment state only after successful validation
- Clear the active session after a successful runtime replacement
- Return `INVALID_CONTENT` when rehydration validation fails
- Add tests for full runtime reconstruction, shared repository behavior, accepted request state, ownership balances, ledger restoration, sequence continuation, duplicate accounts, and broken listing references

## Scope controls

- Stacked on `refactor/versioned-persistence`
- Snapshot schema remains version 1
- No database or external persistence technology introduced
- No merge performed

author: johazores
body:
## Summary

Fixes two user-facing failures: instant test top-ups could not complete on fresh deployments, and the currency converter could become unavailable or block the Add Funds screen.

## Root cause

Fresh deployments were configured to hold test USDC but did not automatically create and fund a USDC treasury. The fallback created a temporary Friendbot account containing XLM, then attempted to send USDC that account did not own, causing the Stellar transaction to fail.

The Add Funds page also loaded wallet data and exchange rates together with `Promise.all`, so a rate-provider outage prevented users from seeing their address, QR code, balance, or top-up controls. The converter depended on one market-data provider and also produced duplicate or invalid currency selections after the held asset changed.

## Add Funds fixes

- Fresh test deployments now use fundable XLM unless a valid USDC treasury is configured.
- Database synchronization repairs older test environments that have USDC selected without an existing treasury account.
- The top-up endpoint validates the current network and treasury configuration again before moving funds.
- Public-network environments never receive an automatic asset change and cannot use instant test funding.
- The Add Funds page loads wallet information independently from exchange rates.
- Users can choose 100, 500, or 1,000 test units and receive a clear success or failure message.
- The UI identifies the actual asset added and explains when incomplete USDC test configuration was safely repaired to XLM.
- Copy-address failures now provide a useful browser fallback.

## Currency converter fixes

- Adds ExchangeRate-API as the primary USD-to-fiat source with Frankfurter as fallback.
- Uses CoinGecko for XLM pricing with Coinbase as fallback.
- Adds an eight-second timeout for each upstream rate provider.
- Preserves the last successful same-configuration rates during temporary provider outages.
- Adds explicit retry behavior, stale-rate status, source attribution, and an estimate-only warning.
- Removes duplicate held-asset currency options.
- Corrects invalid selections when the configured held asset changes.
- Prevents malformed decimal input and improves small-screen layout.
- Keeps the converter on Add Funds without allowing it to block funding actions.

## Valuable placement

Adds a dedicated Family Tool at `/home/tools/converter` for planning tuition, monthly support, gifts, and emergency funds across PHP and common OFW destination currencies. It is linked from the Family Tools page and remains available beside the user’s wallet balance on Add Funds.

## Configuration

Adds the idempotent `rates.fiatUrl` setting and optional deployment overrides:

- `RATES_FIAT_URL`
- `STELLAR_TREASURY_ACCOUNT_ID`
- optional `COINGECKO_API_KEY`

No database schema migration is required.

## Regression coverage

CI now verifies the real user-facing path:

1. Synchronize a fresh database and confirm it defaults to fundable XLM.
2. Simulate incomplete USDC configuration and confirm deployment sync repairs it without overwriting unrelated settings.
3. Start the production backend.
4. Sign up a temporary user.
5. Create and encrypt a Stellar wallet.
6. Submit `/wallet/add-test-funds` against Stellar testnet.
7. Confirm the deposit balance reflects the transaction.
8. Load PHP and USD estimates and confirm multiple source providers are reported.

## Validation

GitHub Actions completed successfully:

- Production dependency installation
- Production-only Prisma generation
- Prisma migrations, database synchronization, and safe seed
- Test funding configuration repair
- TypeScript typecheck
- ESLint
- Backend and frontend production builds
- Real API sign-up, wallet creation, testnet top-up, deposit balance, and currency-rate smoke test
- Independent Stellar testnet claimable-balance end-to-end flow

author: santhreal

`html_to_df` did `xpath("//table")[0]`, raising `IndexError` on valid HTML with no `<table>`. The `text_as_html` produced by document partitioners is not guaranteed to wrap the content in a table, so this crashed the node parser.

Return `None` like the sibling `md_to_df` does for empty input. Adds tests for the no-table and well-formed-table cases.

author: octopollux
body:
## Problem

On the Anthropic/Claude provider path, auxiliary subagents failed **every time** they ran, with:

> Streaming is required for operations that may take longer than 10 minutes.

Observed live during a 10-turn playthrough pinned to `env-anthropic` (opus-4-6 / sonnet-4-6 / haiku-4-5). Affected subagents:

- **`scribe`** (world-state persistence) — failed on essentially every turn, so entities/inventory/notes were **not persisted**; player resources degraded to a bare `HP=▢▢▢▢` instead of full Breathless state.
- **`style_scene`** (theme-styler at handoff) — failed, so scenes never got themed (no `key_color`).
- `scene-tracker` (smaller `max_tokens`) ran fine.

The OpenAI path had none of these failures on the same scenario.

## Root cause

The SDK's `messages.create()` runs a **client-side** `calculateNonstreamingTimeout` guard ([`client.js`](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript)) that *throws before any HTTP request* whenever `max_tokens` implies a request that could exceed the 10-minute ceiling (≈ `max_tokens > 21333`). Thinking bumps `max_tokens` to the model max (128000 on Opus, in `toAnthropicParams`), so heavy subagent calls tripped it. Subagents call the model **non-streaming** (no `onDelta`), so they hit the guard; the DM narration streams and was unaffected — exactly matching the observed pattern.

## Fix

The non-streaming branch of `anthropicChat` now uses `client.messages.stream(...).finalMessage()` internally and buffers the result (no `onDelta`) — suggested option 1. The streaming endpoint has no 10-minute ceiling, `finalMessage()` returns the identical `Message` shape, and `stream.response` still carries the `anthropic-ratelimit-*` headers, so nothing downstream changes.

## Tests

- New `anthropic.long-request.test.ts` faithfully reproduces the SDK guard (exact threshold + error text) and asserts `chat()` with a large `max_tokens` — including the thinking-driven 128000 bump that first surfaced the bug — routes through `stream()` and never touches `create()`.
- Updated the two existing tests that mocked the non-streaming `create()` path (`anthropic.usage.test.ts`, `preserves-thinking.contract.test.ts`) to drive through `stream()`.

Full provider suite (261 tests), targeted related suite, and the offline golden replay all pass; lint + typecheck clean.

## Not yet done

No live API run (the `mvplay` + temp `MV_CONFIG_DIR` repro that spends metered credit). Another Claude is standing by to test that live.

body:
## What

Completes Stage 0 by resolving each member's typed `startLocation` address into coordinates (via **Mapbox** forward geocoding) inside `getRecommendations()`, *before* `recommend()`. This **activates** the meeting point + travel-radius filter on real form input — until now they were dormant because the form sends free-text addresses, not coordinates.

- **`lib/geocode.js`** — `geocodeAddress` + `geocodeMembers`. SF-proximity bias so bare place names resolve locally; `fetch` is injectable so tests never touch the network; idempotent (members already carrying coords pass through). An un-geocodable address throws a tagged `GEOCODE_FAILED` error naming the member + address.
- **Controller** — surfaces `GEOCODE_FAILED` as **422** (bad user input), not a generic 500.
- **Validation** — requires a non-empty string `startLocation`; validates `travelRadius` when present.
- Geocoding stays in the service/lib layer; the engine remains network-free.

## Why Mapbox (not OSM Nominatim)

Chosen deliberately for better geocoding quality + a higher rate limit. This **reverses the earlier free/OSS default** — it adds a commercial, API-keyed dependency. Logged in the decision/preferences notes.

## Product question resolved

Per **US #3**, the organizer types each member's starting location — members are **not** app users, so coordinates can't come from a `User` row. Geocoded per request. No schema change.

## Testing

- **125 tests green** (`npm test`), incl. 9 new geocode unit tests (stubbed fetch). DB-integration tests now pass pre-geocoded coords so they exercise the DB→engine path, not the network.
- Server boots clean.

## ⚠️ Requires config before it runs live

**`MAPBOX_TOKEN` must be added to `.env`** (not currently set) — without it, `geocodeAddress` throws "MAPBOX_TOKEN is not set". The **live end-to-end smoke test (real address → populated `meetingPoint`) has NOT been run** since no token is configured.

author: nitronitronitro
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized the `list_recent_history_dates` function in `content_store.py` by introducing a `_read_item_count_fast` helper. This helper reads only the first 2048 bytes of a JSON snapshot file and uses a regular expression (`\n  "item_count":\s*(\d+)`) to extract the `item_count` metadata field. If the field is not found in the chunk, it safely falls back to a full `json.load()` parse.

🎯 **Why:** 
The `list_recent_history_dates` function iterates over the last 7 days and all registered sources, opening and parsing *entire* JSON files just to retrieve a single `item_count` integer. Because snapshot files can contain hundreds of AI-summarized items and comments, loading the entire structure into memory in a tight loop is a massive CPU and memory bottleneck, causing slow API responses for the history dates endpoint.

📊 **Impact:** 
Significantly reduces memory allocations, GC pressure, and CPU time when generating the history list by avoiding parsing massive JSON lists unnecessarily. 

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Run the `/api/history/dates` endpoint with several days of large generated snapshots. The response time will be drastically lower since it reads small file chunks rather than fully parsing every historical JSON file. All existing unit tests pass, confirming no correctness regressions.

author: pacheco
body:
**Stacked PR 4/4** (base `wasm-benchmark-log` = PR #134). Merge #132, #133, #134 first.

## What

Documentation only — new `docs/ideas.md` section 0. Analysis of what remains after PR #132–#134, re-measured post-forwarding. No code change.

## Findings

After the two fixes, wasm-eth variables and constraints **lead** powdr; the one remaining axis is **bus interactions** (+8%, concentrated in apc_037/012). Root cause, measured on apc_004 (memory already at parity 44 = 44): **range-obligation packing**. apc emits one tuple-range check (bus 7) per timestamp `lower_decomp` limb where powdr batches several into a linear-combination arg; and apc range-checks single `a__` result byte limbs where powdr uses byte-*pair* checks on the bitwise bus (bus 6). apc_004: bus-7 68 vs powdr 22, bus-6 1 vs 24. The fix is a **global range-obligation rebuild** — the large-corpus version of the existing repack passes; bus-only, variable-neutral.

Residuals that **fell out of the forwarding cascade** (documented as do-not-build): the `bit_shift_carry` / `a__` variable excess (apc_037 now only +33 vars), functional-XOR lookups (partly collapsed), and the ≤1-emitted-check cap (not binding — memory at parity). Plus a runtime profiling note: flat runtime, with a memoized pre-linearized address-slot side table as the cheap lever.

body:
#### What

Implements the first library-side step for canonical cross-backend report IDs from #3137 and #3136.

A report now has a canonical `UUID` identity:

- Existing integer UUIDv4 IDs are converted losslessly when reports are read.
- New reports use UUIDv7. Python <3.14 uses the `uuid6` backport; Python >=3.14 uses the standard library.
- `_hash` remains available as `report.id.int`.
- IDs are serialized as strings at backend boundaries.

Project summaries expose this identity as `report_id`, while the existing `id` column remains the backend locator accepted by `project.get()`.

#### Backend adapters

- Hub sends and reads `report_id`, matching the nullable UUIDv4/UUIDv7 field from skore-hub#1665.
- MLflow stores the value in the `skore_report_id` tag and exposes it as `report_id`.
- Local storage keeps the physical `artifact_id` separate from canonical `report_id`. Legacy local metadata without `report_id` remains compatible.

Legacy Hub rows and MLflow runs may expose `report_id=None` until backfilled.

#### Compatibility

- Directly unpickled legacy reports are migrated through `__setstate__`.
- State deserialization migrates legacy integer IDs through `from_dict()`.
- Only RFC-compatible UUIDv4 and UUIDv7 IDs are accepted.

This PR does not introduce put idempotency, revisions, duplicate folding, or synchronization semantics.

author: jaco-brink
body:
Closes #94.

## What & why

The #92 LLM language sweep's first **cru** dry-run produced 190 clean null-fills but **8 relabels — a mixed bag**. Several were false positives: the detector relabelled **English articles `es` from their bilingual page chrome**, not the body.

| verdict | cited evidence | reality |
|---|---|---|
| `en → es @0.8` | footer **"©2025 Cru. todos los derechos reservados."** | Spanish footer on an English article |
| `en → es @0.8 / 0.9` | breadcrumb **"Comparte el evangelio"** | English body |
| `es → en @0.99` | *entirely Spanish* prose | internally contradictory — almost certainly wrong |

Genuine fixes in the same batch (must be preserved): `vi → es @0.99` on Spanish body (old mis-tag), and `es → en` where the body is genuinely English under a `/mx/es/` path.

### Root cause — detector guidance, not the sweep machinery

1. `SYSTEM_PROMPT` asked for the single **DOMINANT** language of "the document" + one ≤120-char evidence quote, with **no instruction to weigh the article body over boilerplate** — so the model rests a verdict on a salient chrome quote.
2. `cleanText()` only collapses whitespace; it does **not** strip chrome, so nav/breadcrumb/footer reach the model.
3. The sweep sends `cleanText(...).slice(0, maxDetectChars)` — the **front** of the page, which on scraped cru pages leads with nav/breadcrumb chrome.
4. `resolveFromLlm` trusts any confident verdict with **no floor** (ADR-0009, deliberately) → a @0.8 chrome verdict becomes a real relabel. A floor wouldn't help anyway — the worst case was @0.99.

## The fix (prompt-only)

Rewrite `SYSTEM_PROMPT` to score the **MAIN BODY**, name site chrome explicitly and require it ignored, state **body-wins** on a language disagreement, and require the **evidence quote to come from the body**. No port, engine, model, or policy change. See **ADR-0010**.

## Verification — TDD simulation (throwaway harness)

Proven **red→green against the *real* `OpenRouterLanguageDetector`** over OpenRouter (`google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, matching prod). Minimal 7-fixture corpus, three classes, laid out **chrome-first** to mirror a scraped page:

- **confirmed** — already-correct EN / ES pages (must not change)
- **clean-mislabel** — body ≠ stored label, no chrome trap (the genuine `vi→es`, `es→en` relabels — must still fire)
- **mixed-chrome** — English body + Spanish chrome, and the ES-body/EN-chrome mirror (the target)

The harness spends live LLM calls, so it lives in `scratch/lang-detect-sim/` and is **not committed / not in CI** (~14 calls per run, cents). The committed guard is a cheap **offline** test.

### RED (pre-fix, real adapter) — gate exits **1**
```
C3-en-body-es-footer      [mixed-chrome] expect=en | adapter: FAIL es@0.90   ← evidence: "Recursos Sobre nosotros Donar … Comparte esta página: Facebook Twitter Correo."
C3-en-body-es-breadcrumb  [mixed-chrome] expect=en | adapter: FAIL es@0.90   ← evidence: "Inicio › Artículos › Vida cristiana › Comparte el evangelio …"
── adapter: 5/7 all, 1/3 mixed-chrome
GATE(adapter): FAIL — 2 fixture(s) mislabelled  (exit 1)
```
Faithfully reproduces the prod false positives — the label rests on Spanish chrome.

### GREEN (post-fix, **same command**, real adapter) — gate exits **0**
```
C3-en-body-es-footer      [mixed-chrome] expect=en | adapter: PASS en@0.90
C3-en-body-es-breadcrumb  [mixed-chrome] expect=en | adapter: PASS en@1.00
C3-es-body-en-chrome      [mixed-chrome] expect=es | adapter: PASS es@1.00
── adapter: 7/7 all, 3/3 mixed-chrome
GATE(adapter): PASS — every fixture labelled by its body language.  (exit 0)
```
The flips are gone; confirmed + clean-mislabel classes unchanged (genuine relabels preserved).

### Tune iterations
1. **Candidate prompt v1** — body-over-chrome + explicit chrome list + body-wins + body-sourced evidence. Passed all 7 fixtures on the **first** live run; no prompt iteration needed.
2. **Fixture faithfulness v1→v2** — the initial *footer* fixture used a long, dominant English body and the current prompt still read it `en` (only the breadcrumb flipped). That under-reproduced prod, whose footer flips happen on **short** pages (the sweep's real domain). Shortening the body so the Spanish footer carries proportional weight made **both** mixed-chrome cases flip in RED — a faithful reproduction — which the fix then cleared.

### Committed checks
- **370 tests pass** (368 + 2 new), typecheck / eslint / dependency-cruiser clean.
- New offline test (mocked `fetch`) pins the wired prompt: directs at the main body, names footer/breadcrumb chrome, keeps "body wins", requires body-sourced evidence, and **must not** revert to the "single DOMINANT" framing.

## Scope / bounds

Simulation only — **nothing was run against production**. The cru relabels are not applied here; re-running the dry-run with this fix is the follow-up. The throwaway harness is not part of this PR.

## Files
- `src/adapters/openrouter/openrouter-language-detector.ts` — the prompt fix
- `src/adapters/openrouter/openrouter-language-detector.test.ts` — offline regression guard
- `docs/decisions/0010-detector-scores-body-over-chrome.md` — ADR

author: bassim-matar
body:
Follow-up to #5. Two commits.

## Scope the short connect timeout to downloads only (fixes the crash)
#5 gave every `_fetch` an 8s connect budget. But `urllib` reads the HTTP
response status line *under* the connect timeout (the socket is only relaxed
to the read budget afterwards), so the 8s also capped the i14y API's
time-to-first-byte. A transient slow response from the API then failed all
retries and **crashed the build-deploy on `main`** in
`select_classifications → codelist_csv`, after the 4-minute fetch had already
run.

Only the data-file downloads (non-fatal, dead/geo-blocked distribution hosts)
now pass `connect_timeout`; the i14y API keeps its full budget, restoring the
pre-#5 behavior there. Verified: a dead download host still fails fast
(~8s/attempt), an API-style fetch uses the full connect budget again, and a
live codelist fetch succeeds.

## Drop source history and editorializing from the README
The "Why i14y" section named a specific upstream source and judged its
harvested datasets. Keeps the functional native-vs-harvested distinction but
states it soberly.

> ⚠️ `main`'s build-deploy is currently broken by the regression above; this PR
> restores it.

## What

Adds `faq_schema: true` to two top-cited blog pages that have genuine FAQ/Q&A sections but were not opted into FAQPage schema emission:

- `content/blog/infrastructure-as-code-tools/index.md` — our #1 AI-cited page (247 citations in the trailing 28 days per Profound). Has a `## Frequently Asked Questions` section with 9 real Q&A pairs (e.g. "Which IaC tool should I choose for AWS?", "Is Terraform still worth learning in 2025?").

author: noctonca
body:
Closes #408.

## Symptom

Above native vertical resolution, actor ground shadows (hero and NPC) vanish in the bottom part of the screen. Field-reported by EPmager: 720p dropped the bottom 240 lines of shadow, 1080p the bottom 600. The culled band is exactly `ModeResY - 480` in both cases.

## Root cause

Actor shadows are rasterised through per-scanline span tables in `SOURCES/BEZIER.CPP`:

```cpp
#define MAX_SCAN_LINES 480
S32 TabCoorPoint[MAX_SCAN_LINES][4];   // span endpoints, one row per scanline
S32 TabNbPoint[MAX_SCAN_LINES];        // span count per scanline
```

`DrawOmbre` drops any span at `y >= MAX_SCAN_LINES`, and `DrawLineShade` clamps its fill loop to `MAX_SCAN_LINES - 1`. Both are pinned to the native 480. Once the 3D view opened above 480 (the `fix/widescreen-y-clamp` campaign), every shadow whose projected screen-Y landed at or below line 480 was silently never drawn. That is a separate Y-axis pin the earlier clamp work didn't reach.

## Fix

Point `MAX_SCAN_LINES` at `ADELINE_MAX_Y_RES` (1080), the same constant that already sizes the `TabOffLine[]` / `TabOffPhysLine[]` line-offset tables, so the span tables cover the full active height. The visible clamp is already handled upstream by `ClipYMin`/`ClipYMax`, which are `ModeResY`-aware, so no other logic changes are needed. The result is a no-op at native height (nothing was ever indexed past 479 there) and byte-identical at 640x480.

## Verification

- Confirmed visually: shadows now draw across the full bottom band at 720p and 1080p.
- Clean incremental build + link; clang-format clean.
- No-op at 480 by construction (larger array bound, same `ClipYMax`-bounded fill range).

Ships test-light: a 1-line data-size change with a mechanism that matches both field measurements exactly. Documented as audit entry A11 in `docs/WIDESCREEN_HARDCODED_DIMS_AUDIT.md` and a Done row in `docs/WIDESCREEN.md`.

author: copilot
body:
`Fault::configuration_invalid` was declared and included in the `requires_reset_and_post` latch mask but had no `raise()` call anywhere — the "invalid config ⇒ latched, requires physical reset + POST" invariant was structurally unreachable.

## Changes

- **`safety_manager.hpp`** — adds `bool configuration_valid` to `SafetyInputs` with a doc-comment matching the existing brownout/watchdog field convention (true = valid, false = fault).

- **`safety_manager.cpp`** — adds the raise site in `evaluate()`, immediately after the `communication_healthy` check, mirroring the brownout/watchdog wiring:

  if (!inputs.configuration_valid) {
      raise(Fault::configuration_invalid, true);  // latch=true → requires reset+POST
  }

author: santhreal
body:
## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

`function_to_dict` read `param.annotation.__name__` for every annotated parameter, but a PEP 604 union hint such as `str | None` is a `types.UnionType` with no `__name__`, so any tool function using modern union hints crashed with `AttributeError`

The fix extracts the non-None union member and maps its type, so `int | None` maps to `integer` and `str | None` to `string` instead of crashing, falling back to the annotation string form when there is no member name

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

This is a pure typing utility with no proxy surface to curl; the regression test in `tests/litellm_utils_tests/test_utils.py` builds the tool schema for a function with `str | None` and `int | None` parameters and asserts the resulting JSON schema types. It fails before this change (the `int | None` parameter falls back to the default `string`) and passes after

\`\`\`
isolated-vm@6.1.2 STDERR ../src/isolate/platform_delegate.h:15:
  error: 'SourceLocation' in namespace 'v8' does not name a type

isolated-vm 6.x uses \`v8::SourceLocation\`, added in Node 22's V8. Node 20's V8 doesn't have it. Backstage 1.53 pulled in isolated-vm ^6.0.1 via plugin-scaffolder-backend. Butler-portal downgraded to node:20 in v0.5.4 (commit a89abbb) because of a node-fetch v2 gzip-stream-close regression on Node 22 that returned empty bodies on 200 responses. That regression was fixed upstream in Node 22.7. \`node:22-bookworm-slim\` ships current 22.x, so it should no longer bite. ## What & why

Two additions for classic Outlook, where the full `.msg` (body, From, all Cc) comes through on drag.

### Inline body preview
Emails that have a body now show a **Preview** button. Clicking it expands an inline, scrollable panel with the message body; the button flips to **Hide**. Expanded state is kept in memory, so opening a preview survives search/filter re-renders.

The card now renders **all** From and Cc recipients as clickable chips (labelled **From** / **Cc**), de-duplicated across both. Clicking any chip filters the list to that person. This replaces the previous single plain-text sender with uniform, searchable chips.

author: copilot
body:
`valid_configuration()` short-circuits `return true` for `!calibrated`, so `factory_defaults()` and any uncalibrated record passed the validity check without range validation. Nothing in the control layer enforced that an uncalibrated config could never reach actuation.

## Changes

- **`SafetyInputs` — new field `configuration_valid`**  
  Caller sets this to `r2::application::valid_configuration(cfg) && cfg.calibrated`. Value-initialises to `false` (fail-closed: a zeroed `SafetyInputs{}` asserts the fault by default).

- **`SafetyManager::evaluate()` — control-layer gate**  
  ```cpp
  if (!inputs.configuration_valid) {
      raise(Fault::configuration_invalid, true);  // latched
  }
  ```
  A latched fault drives state to `fault_latched` → `bridge_must_be_disabled()` true, `motion_permitted()` false, `arm()` refused — independent of `actuation_enabled`. `valid_configuration()` itself is unchanged; the `return true` short-circuit for uncalibrated records stays.

  `configuration_invalid` was already in the `requires_reset_and_post` set inside `clear_recoverable_faults`, so it cannot be cleared with a physical acknowledgement alone.

- **New test `test_safety_configuration_invalid()` (H5)**  
  Documents that `factory_defaults()` has `calibrated=false` and that `valid_configuration()` intentionally returns `true` for it, then proves evaluate with `configuration_valid=false` produces an active+latched fault, `fault_latched` state, refused arm, disabled bridge, and an irrecoverable fault without reset+POST — including that the latch survives a subsequent fully-healthy evaluation (ported from #959).

---
This PR is the canonical fix for both coupled config issues (supersedes #959).

Closes #954
Closes #955

author: alhomaidhi
body:
Fixes needing to press **Sync** repeatedly to get all reviews in. The Outscraper pull was fine — storing it was the bottleneck: reviews were written one at a time (two HTTP driver round-trips each, ~300 sequential queries for a 154-review store), so each sync request stored only a chunk before running out of time. Worse, after a partial ingest the next sync anchored its cutoff at the newest stored review, which could permanently skip the older tail on larger stores.

## Changes

- **Batched ingestion**: `upsertReviews` inserts in 500-row batches via `jsonb_to_recordset` with targetless `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (covers both unique keys, including collisions within the same statement). A full history now lands in a couple of queries — one sync stores everything the job returned
- **Full pulls until one completes**: new `stores.history_synced_at` flag, set only when a full (cutoff-less) pull ingests successfully. Until then, every sync re-pulls the full history (dedup makes that safe) instead of going incremental — an interrupted sync means starting over, never building on incomplete data
- New `pending_full` column records whether the tracked job was a full pull, so the flag is set correctly whichever polling request ends up ingesting it
- Both columns are added by `ALTER TABLE … IF NOT EXISTS` migrations

## Note on existing stores

The flag starts null, so each existing store's next sync performs one full re-pull (billed once by Outscraper) to guarantee nothing was missed, then switches to incremental permanently.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass
- After deploy: sync the 154-review store once — the count should reach the full total in a single sync

author: gmprestes
body:
## Problem

`IsDoubleAFixedInteger` checks `floor(value) == value`, which Infinity satisfies. The value then flows into `BsonValueAsInt64` and saturates to `INT64_MAX`, producing for `$type`:

```
(BadValue) Invalid numerical type code: 9223372036854775807
```

where MongoDB reports:

```
(BadValue) Invalid numerical type code: inf
```

For `$size` and the bitwise query operators, an Infinity argument was silently accepted as a fixed integer instead of failing to parse the way MongoDB does.

## Fix

- `IsDoubleAFixedInteger` now requires a finite value, so `$size` and bitwise operators reject Infinity like MongoDB;
- `$type` reports non-finite numeric codes with MongoDB's exact spelling (`inf`/`-inf`/`nan`) before the fixed-integer check.

## Validation

FerretDB compatibility suite compared side-by-side against a real MongoDB 7 replica set: the `$type` Infinity cases (`TestQueryElementCompatElementType`) and `TestQueryArrayCompatSize/Infinity` now behave identically to MongoDB. Full suite (8 groups) runs clean with the change, on two environments.

author: schlaflied
body:
## Summary

Adds an 8th signal to Block G — Posting Legitimacy (`modes/oferta.md`): **Benefits/Employment Terminology Country Mismatch**. Cross-checks the JD's stated location against jurisdiction-specific benefits/employment terms found in the JD text — e.g. a Canada-located posting listing "401(k)" or "W-2 employment," which are US-only terms.

This is a copy-paste-template-error detector, not a ghost-job signal — the posting can be entirely live and real and still describe the wrong country's benefits. A candidate deciding whether a comp/benefits package is competitive needs accurate terms for the country they'd actually work in.

Follows the exact pattern of signals 6 (Employment Classification Risk) and 7 (AI-Buzzword vs. Infrastructure Mismatch): prompt-instruction only (no new script), a jurisdiction table that's a data reference (extensible without touching rule text), non-alarmist descriptive tone, and explicitly orthogonal to the High Confidence / Proceed with Caution / Suspicious tier — reported separately from ghost-job detection.

Closes #1935

## Motivation (from #1935)

Two real, same-day postings surfaced this gap:
1. A posting located in Ontario, Canada listed "401(k) match" — a US-specific retirement plan term; Canadian employers use RRSP.
2. A separate agency-sourced posting, also located in Ontario, listed "W2 employment" and "401(k) retirement plan" — both US employment-classification/benefits terms not used in Canada.

Both look like a US-market JD template reused for a Canada-listed posting, rather than a genuinely Canada-based role with accurate terms.

## Changes

- `modes/oferta.md`: inserted signal 8 into Block G, right after signal 7 and before the `### Output format:` heading. Signals 1-7 are unchanged/unrenumbered.

## Summary
- Change default `worker_processes` in `template/base-nginx-conf.ejs` from `1` to `auto`
- With a single worker, multi-core CPUs are largely underutilized; `auto` lets nginx use one worker per CPU core

Current defaults roughly limit concurrency to ~512 concurrent requests per process (`1 × 1024 / 2`). High traffic, long-lived connections, or large uploads hit this ceiling first. Switching to `auto` is the standard nginx recommendation for production.

author: gmprestes
body:
## Problem

With `defaultUseCompositeOpClass` enabled, every index created through a plain `createIndexes` comes back from `listIndexes` with an extra field MongoDB never returns:

```json
"storageEngine": { "enableOrderedIndex": true }
```

This breaks clients and tooling that compare or replicate index specs — the entire CreateIndexes/DropIndexes groups of the FerretDB compatibility suite fail on it (36 cases).

## Fix

The `CustomIndexOption` enum already distinguishes exactly the two cases the existing TODO in `SerializeIndexSpec` asks to separate:

- `CustomIndexOption_True` — the user explicitly asked for the option → keep surfacing it;
- `CustomIndexOption_DefaultTrue` — the index is ordered merely because of the server default → suppress it, matching the MongoDB response.

This resolves that TODO using the enum's own semantics. Explicit `enableOrderedIndex: false` behavior (gated by `EmitEnableOrderedIndexFalseInResponse`) is unchanged.

## Validation

FerretDB compatibility suite against a real MongoDB 7: CreateIndexes and DropIndexes go from 36 failing cases to zero; full suite (8 groups) clean, on two environments.

author: njbrake
body:
## Description

Two tests inject a disk-write failure by making a profile dir read-only, then assert the subsequent write returns `Err`:

- `src/session/storage.rs` (`session::storage::tests::test_update_write_failure_emits_no_notify`): `set_mode(0o500)` then `assert!(update_res.is_err())`.
- `tests/integration/storage_concurrency.rs` (`test_update_propagates_disk_write_failure`): `set_mode(0o555)`, same pattern.

Root (uid 0) bypasses the Unix DAC permission bits, so the write succeeds and the `is_err()` assertion falsely fails. Anyone running `cargo test` as root (a common container setup, and a likely one for an agent orchestration tool) sees these as hard failures on a clean checkout of `main`. CI runs as a normal user, so the chmod actually bites there and `main` stays green, which is why this is invisible in CI.

**What/why:** a test that cannot inject the failure it is checking for should skip, not assert. This PR adds a small `running_as_root()` helper (euid == 0 via `nix::unistd::geteuid`, already a dependency) and short-circuits both sites with a clean `eprintln!` skip, matching the existing "Skipping: ..." convention used elsewhere in the suite. The concurrency test's earlier ad-hoc write-probe skip is replaced by the same up-front euid check so both sites read the same way.

I inspected the other `set_mode`-based tests (`src/hooks/dir_guard.rs` setuid/setgid/sticky/mode rejection tests); those assert that stat-based mode inspection rejects a bad dir, which root does not bypass, so they are left unchanged.

Fixes #2861

author: gmprestes
body:
## Problem

Neither `CreateAndDrainSingleBatchQuery` nor `PlanForcedPersistentQuery` passes `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK`, so `pg_plan_query` never produces a parallel plan for any aggregation: a full-collection `$group` runs its HashAggregate — group-key expression evaluation, bson decompression and decoding per document — in a single process regardless of `max_parallel_workers_per_gather`. Misleadingly, EXPLAIN shows a parallel plan, because the explain path plans with different cursor options than the execution path.

## Fix

Both paths drain the entire result in one executor run (`DrainStatementViaExecutor`: `execute_once=true`, `count=0`): no portal is suspended and no cursor scrolls backwards — precisely the execution shape a parallel plan requires.

- `CreateAndDrainSingleBatchQuery`: allow parallel plans for read-only queries.
- `PlanForcedPersistentQuery`: allow them only when the plan is destined for the file-based cursor path (hold cursor + `useFileBasedPersistedCursors`), where continuation pages go to a file instead of a suspended portal. If such a plan ever lands on the suspended-portal path, the executor detects the bounded fetch and runs the Gather leader-only — the failure mode is "not parallel", never "wrong results".

## Measured impact

98k-document collection, `$group` by a bson field path, warm cache, 4 workers, group-count statistics on the key: **690ms → 128ms**, at parity with MongoDB 7 on the same machine (109ms).

## Validation

Full FerretDB compatibility suite (8 groups, side-by-side against MongoDB 7) with `useFileBasedPersistedCursors` enabled: zero failures, on two environments (macOS/Docker Desktop and a 40-core Linux host).

Reviewed by Claude (Fable 5 model) as part of an AI-assisted debugging session; the commit carries co-author trailers for the agents involved.

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.15.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.15.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: one of the performance improvements in 7.15.1 (pull 2215) dramatically
  increased memory use during reporting for large projects. Now we use a
  different approach that is both faster and slimmer than 7.15.0. Fixes `issue
  2229`_.

.. _issue 2229:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2229


.. _changes_7-15-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.15.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: in the HTML report with ``show_contexts`` enabled, a context label
  containing ``</script>`` (for example a parametrized pytest node id) could
  close the inline ``<script>`` element in a file page early, injecting markup.
  Context labels are now fully escaped. Thanks, `Rajath Mohare <pull 2224_>`_.

- A number of performance improvements thanks to Paul Kehrer, in pull requests
  `2213 <pull 2213_>`_, `2214 <pull 2214_>`_, `2215 <pull 2215_>`_, `2216
  <pull 2216_>`_, `2218 <pull 2218_>`_, `2220 <pull 2220_>`_, and `2221 <pull
  2221_>`_.

.. _pull 2213: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2213
.. _pull 2214: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2214
.. _pull 2215: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2215
.. _pull 2216: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2216
.. _pull 2218: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2218
.. _pull 2220: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2220
.. _pull 2221: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2221
.. _pull 2224: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2224

.. _changes_7-15-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.15.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Since 7.14.0, reporting commands implicitly combine parallel data files. Now
  those commands have a new option ``--keep-combined`` to retain the data files
  after combining them instead of the default, which is to delete them.
  Finishes `issue 2198`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report would incorrectly count excluded functions as uncovered,
  as described in `issue 2205`_. This is now fixed thanks to `Martin Kuntz
  Jacobsen <pull 2206_>`_.

- When running your program, coverage now correctly sets
  ``yourmodule.__spec__.loader`` as `strongly recommended <--loader--_>`_,
  avoiding the deprecation warning described in `issue 2208`_. Thanks, `A5rocks
  <pull 2209_>`_.

- Fix: with Python 3.10, running with the ``-I`` (isolated mode) option didn't
  correctly omit the current directory from the module search path, as
  described in `issue 2103`_. That is now fixed thanks to `Ilia Sorokin <pull
  2211_>`_.

.. _--loader--: https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#module.__loader__
.. _issue 2103:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2103
.. _issue 2198:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2198
.. _issue 2205:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2205
.. _pull 2206: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2206
.. _issue 2208:  https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2208
.. _pull 2209: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2209
.. _pull 2211: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2211


.. _changes_7-14-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the default ``...`` exclusion rule now also matches function bodies
  whose closing return-type bracket is on its own line (for example, after a
  long ``-> dict[ ... ]`` annotation that a formatter has split over multiple
  lines). Closes `issue 2185`_, thanks `Mengjia Shang <pull 2196_>`_.

- Fix: On 3.13t, we incorrectly issued ``Couldn't import C tracer`` errors.
  We can't import the C tracer because in 7.14.2 we stopped shipping compiled
  wheels for 3.13t. Thanks, `Hugo van Kemenade <pull 2203_>`_.

.. _issue 2185: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2185
.. _pull 2196: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2196
.. _pull 2203: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2203


.. _changes_7-14-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some messages were being written to stdout, making ``coverage json -o
  -`` useless for capturing JSON output. Now messages are written to stderr,
  fixing `issue 2197`_.

- Fix: ``CoverageData`` kept one SQLite connection per thread that recorded
  coverage, but never closed them when those threads terminated. On long runs
  with many short-lived threads this leaked one file descriptor per dead
  thread, eventually failing with ``OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files``.
  Connections belonging to terminated threads are now closed and dropped.
  Fixes `issue 2192`_.  Thanks, `Matthew Lloyd <pull 2193_>`_.

- Fix: when using sys.monitoring, we were assuming we could use the
  ``COVERAGE_ID`` tool id.  But other tools might also assume they could use
  that id.  Pre-allocated ids don't really make sense, so now we search for a
  usable one instead. Fixes `issue 2187`_.

- Following `the advice of cibuildwheel <no-13t_>`_, we no longer distribute
  wheels for Python 3.13 free-threaded.

.. _issue 2187: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2187
.. _issue 2192: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2192
.. _pull 2193: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2193
.. _issue 2197: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2197
.. _no-13t: https://py-free-threading.github.io/ci/#building-free-threaded-wheels-with-cibuildwheel


.. _changes_7-14-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the HTML report used typographic niceties to make file paths more
  readable by adding a small amount of space around slashes. Those spaces
  interfered with searching the page for file paths of interest. Now the report
  uses CSS to accomplish the same visual tweak so that searches with slashes
  work correctly. Closes `issue 2170`_.

- `Add a 3.16 PyPI classifier <hugo-316_>`_ since we test on the 3.16 main
  branch.

.. _issue 2170: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2170
.. _hugo-316: https://mastodon.social/hugovk/116588523571204490


.. _changes_7-14-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.14.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: now when running one of the reporting commands, if there are
  parallel data files that need combining, they will be implicitly combined
  before creating the report. There is no option to avoid the combination; let
  us know if you have a use case that requires it.  Thanks, `Tim Hatch
  <pull 2162_>`_. Closes `issue 1781`_.

- Fix: the output from ``combine`` was too verbose, listing each file
  considered. Now it shows a single line with the counts of files combined,
  files skipped, and files with errors. The ``-q`` flag suppresses this line.
  The old detailed lines are available with the new ``--debug=combine`` option.

- Fix: running a Python file through a symlink now sets the sys.path correctly,
  matching regular Python behavior. Fixes `issue 2157`_.

- Fix: ``Collector.flush_data`` could fail with "RuntimeError: Set changed
  size during iteration" when a tracer in another thread added a line to the
  per-file set that ``add_lines`` (or ``add_arcs``) was iterating. The values
  passed to ``CoverageData`` are now snapshotted via ``dict.copy()`` and
  ``set.copy()``, which are atomic under the GIL. Thanks, `Alex Vandiver <pull
  2165_>`_.

- Fix: the soft keyword ``lazy`` is now bolded in HTML reports.

- We are no longer testing eventlet support. Eventlet started issuing stern
  deprecation warnings that break our tests. Our support code is still there.

.. _issue 1781: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1781
.. _issue 2157: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2157
.. _pull 2162: https://git
